items.physical_scope: The pair's declared effective one-dimensional model for a spinless massive particle: its state space, position and momentum assignments, its assigned energy operator for a real bounded measurable potential, its bound-state and stationary vocabulary, and its declared generalized stationary solutions used for the scattering reading. The model is an additional assumption of the pair, not a derivation from the three-dimensional massive-particle model P5, and no identification of a concrete apparatus or material system with the model is asserted; such an identification would be a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of P7. No experiment and no empirical value appear.

items.title: The declared interval models with Dirichlet and Robin boundary conditions, and the declared zero-range (delta) model
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework postulates and units of clause (a)
of [[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]], and the vocabulary of
its clauses (b)-(f): the effective one-dimensional state space, the position
and momentum assignments, the assigned energy operator $H_{V}=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V}$
for a real bounded measurable potential, bound states, stationary solutions
and declared generalized stationary solutions. Fix $m>0$, $\hbar>0$ and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Dirichlet interval model.** Fix $0<L<\infty$ and a real $V\in
C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, read as a potential energy in joules, and put
$\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, a real continuous function on $[0,L]$ with the
dimension of an inverse square length under the conventions of the framework;
the factor $2m/\hbar^{2}$ has unit $\mathrm{J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$, so the products
in clause (c) of the next item are dimensionally consistent. The **Dirichlet
interval model** declares the state space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$ of
almost-everywhere classes with the pairing linear in the first argument
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) and the assigned energy
operator
$$H_{D,V}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{D,V}):=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\},$$
where $D^{2}$ is the second weak derivative and $u^{*}$ the continuous
representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]; in
the notation of [[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]]
this operator is $(\hbar^{2}/2m)(A_{D}+M_{\tilde V})$ with
$D(A_{D})=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\}$, and for $V=0$ its
declared free eigenpairs are the pairs
$\bigl(\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}(\frac{n\pi}{L})^{2},\,e_{n}\bigr)$ with
$e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$, $n\ge1$, read from
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]] and
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]]. The vanishing endpoint condition
is a declared idealization of an infinitely high wall at each endpoint; the
pair does not derive it from the line model, and no reflection coefficient or
wall model of a material system is asserted.

**(c) Robin interval model.** Fix $0<L<\infty$, real $\alpha,\beta$, read as
**declared boundary parameters** in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a real $V\in
C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ and $\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ as in (b). The **Robin
interval model** declares the state space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$ and the
assigned energy operator
$$H_{\alpha\beta,V}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{\alpha\beta,V}):=\{u\in H^{2}(0,L):u'^{*}(0)=\alpha u^{*}(0),\ u'^{*}(L)=\beta u^{*}(L)\},$$
the operator $(\hbar^{2}/2m)\,A$ of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green-resolvent]] with potential
$\tilde V$; the boundary parameters are declared model parameters, not derived
quantities, and no physical interpretation of a particular value of $\alpha$
or $\beta$ is asserted. The Dirichlet model of (b) is not the limit
$\alpha,\beta\to\infty$ in this definition; the Dirichlet condition is a
separate declared boundary condition.

**(d) Zero-range (delta) interface model.** Fix a real **coupling** $g$, read
in joule metres, and put $\alpha_{g}:=2mg/\hbar^{2}$, a real number in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Let $A_{\alpha_{g}}$ be the delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]] on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$,
$$D(A_{\alpha_{g}})=\{u\in H^{1}(\mathbb R):u|_{(0,\infty)},u|_{(-\infty,0)}\in H^{2},\ u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\alpha_{g}u^{*}(0)\},\qquad A_{\alpha_{g}}u=-D^{2}u,$$
where the displayed action is understood piecewise: $(A_{\alpha_g}u)|_{(0,\infty)}=-D^2(u|_{(0,\infty)})$ and $(A_{\alpha_g}u)|_{(-\infty,0)}=-D^2(u|_{(-\infty,0)})$, with each weak derivative taken on that open half-line. The resulting two $L^2$ classes are glued across the null point $0$; $D^2u$ here is not the global weak second derivative on $\mathbb R$, which need not be an $L^2$ class when the first derivative jumps. Declare the **zero-range model** with coupling $g$ to be the model whose
assigned energy operator is
$$H_{g}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,A_{\alpha_{g}},\qquad D(H_{g}):=D(A_{\alpha_{g}}).$$
The interface condition $u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=(2mg/\hbar^{2})u^{*}(0)$ is the
declared realization of a zero-range interaction at the origin: the pair reads
it as the model counterpart of a formally written term $g\,\delta(x)$ in the
energy expression, while recording that $\delta$ is not a function and that
the model is defined by the interface condition and not by an $L^{2}$
potential. The scaling of the operator is $(\hbar^{2}/2m)$ times the
mathematical operator, by the conventions of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]]. No identification of a
concrete impurity or material with the model is asserted.

**(e) Units, scope and status.** All three assignments are declared energy
operators with the joule as declared unit. The interval-spectra theorem proves
self-adjointness, compact resolvent, the complete discrete eigenbases and the
stated spectra for $H_{D,V}$ and $H_{\alpha\beta,V}$. For $H_g$, the
zero-range theorem proves self-adjointness and the stated classification of
negative eigenvalues and bound states; it does not assert a complete description
of the spectrum or an eigenbasis for $H_g$. These properties are established
by the theorems of this page, not presupposed here. The boundary conditions,
boundary parameters and coupling are declared assumptions of the pair; nothing
in this definition asserts that a laboratory system realizes them, and no
count, rate or measured value is recorded.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.1 printed pages 75-79 (PDF pages 83-87): the square potential well with matching conditions and bound-state spectrum

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 9.1-9.2, printed pages 181-195 (PDF pages 193-207): Sturm-Liouville operators on intervals and separated self-adjoint boundary conditions (Theorem 9.6), with the Dirichlet condition as the case alpha=0 (eqs. (9.22)-(9.25)); PDF page = printed page + 12

items.physical_scope: The pair's declared confined and point-interaction models of the effective one-dimensional massive particle: the interval model with Dirichlet endpoint conditions, the interval model with separated Robin endpoint conditions with declared real boundary parameters, and the zero-range (delta) interface model with a declared real coupling. The boundary conditions, boundary parameters and coupling are additional model assumptions of the pair; they are not derived from the line model, from P5 or from any material system, and no experiment, count or measured value is asserted. The operator assignments are well defined as mathematical operators on their displayed domains; their self-adjointness and spectra are established by the pair's theorems and are not presupposed here.

items.title: The line model's energy observable, flow and stationary states
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), all
read through the declared effective one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and spin label $s=0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, let $\|V\|_\infty=\sup|V|$,
and let $H_{V}$ be the assigned energy operator of clause (c) of the model,
with flow $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ and evolved preparations
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. Then:

(a) $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model in the
sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]: $H_{V}$ is
densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$, and
$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$ for every $f\in D(H_{V})$.

(b) *Flow.* The family $t\mapsto U(t)$ is the model's strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group of the assigned energy observable; the
Schroedinger equation $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{V}\psi(t)$ holds in the
norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{V})$,
and for other vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not
asserted; density preparations evolve as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with
$\rho(t)$ a density operator for every $t$.

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure
preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and
only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{V}$; in that case, with eigenvalue
$E$, one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is
time-independent, and if $\|\psi\|=1$ the law assigns probability one to the
singleton $\{E\}$, so the energy mean exists and equals $E$, with second
moment $E^{2}$. Moreover every bounded assigned sharp observable compatible
with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in every preparation.

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit pure preparation $\psi$ the declared
position assignment of the model has outcome law
$\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$;
and if $\psi$ is a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$, the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ coexist as readings of the same
preparation, of the action of the declared observables, without any joint
measurement claim.

(e) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
line model; it asserts no discrete spectrum or eigenbasis for a general
bounded measurable $V$, no completeness or scattering statement, no
identification of $H_{V}$ with any laboratory Hamiltonian beyond the tested
identification allowed by P7, and no empirical result.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 2.1 and 3.2, printed pages 20-30 and 66-75 (PDF pages 23-33 and 69-78): the time-independent Schroedinger equation, eigenfunctions and their energies

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1 printed pages 55-58 (PDF pages 67-70): the Schroedinger operator as a self-adjoint operator and the domain-qualified equation; Section 5.1 printed pages 123-126 (PDF pages 135-138): Stone's theorem and the time evolution

items.physical_scope: The line model of the pair for a spinless massive particle with a real bounded measurable potential: the fact that its declared energy operator is an assigned sharp observable, generates the model's unitary flow, and that its stationary preparations are exactly the eigenrays with a point-mass energy law. The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared effective one-dimensional model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no measured energy, no apparatus, no discrete-spectrum claim for a general bounded potential, no completeness of eigenfunctions and no empirical result.

items.title: Rectangular barrier: scattering solution, flux balance and transmission
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]], with $m>0$, $\hbar>0$ and
energy, potential and position read in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $a>0$, $U>E>0$ and the incident reference
amplitude $A_{\mathrm{in}}:=1\,\mathrm{m}^{-1/2}$, and let
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}U,&0<x<a,\\ 0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
let $k:=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar$, and consider the
declared generalized stationary solutions of the model at energy $E$ (clause
(e) of the model) that are bounded, classically $C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ and
$C^{2}$ on each of $(-\infty,0),(0,a),(a,\infty)$. Then:

(a) *Scattering solution.* There is exactly one such $\psi$ with the
*transmission asymptotics*
$\psi(x)=A_{\mathrm{in}}(e^{ikx}+re^{-ikx})$ for $x<0$ and
$\psi(x)=A_{\mathrm{in}}t e^{ikx}$ for $x>a$, where the amplitude ratios
$r,t\in\mathbb C$ are dimensionless and uniquely determined; with
$D:=2\cosh(\kappa a)+i\bigl(\frac{\kappa}{k}-\frac{k}{\kappa}\bigr)\sinh(\kappa a)$
one has $t=2e^{-ika}/D$, and
$$T:=|t|^{2}=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^{2}\sinh^{2}(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1},\qquad R:=|r|^{2}=1-T .$$

(b) *Conserved current and flux balance.* The declared probability current
$j(x):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x)}\psi'(x)\bigr)$
of the scattering solution is constant on $\mathbb R$, equal to
$\frac{\hbar k}{m}|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^{2}(1-|r|^{2})=
\frac{\hbar k}{m}|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^{2}|t|^{2}$. With the **reference
current** $j_{\mathrm{in}}:=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^{2}$ of the
incoming term $x\mapsto A_{\mathrm{in}}e^{ikx}$, the transmitted right-going current equals
$T\,j_{\mathrm{in}}$, the reflected left-going current has magnitude
$R\,j_{\mathrm{in}}$, and
$$T+R=1 .$$
The pair reads $T$ and $R$ as the transmitted and reflected fractions of the
reference current of the declared scattering solution; this reading is part of
the model and is not a measurement.

(c) *Thick-barrier form and error.* With $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$ and
$C:=U^{2}/\bigl(4E(U-E)\bigr)$ one has
$$T=\frac{(4/C)\,q}{1+\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^{2}};$$
consequently, whenever $\delta:=\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^{2}$ satisfies
$|\delta|\le\frac12$,
$$\Bigl|T-\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}\,q\Bigr|\le\frac{32E(U-E)}{U^{2}}\,q\,|\delta| .$$

(d) *Scope.* The scattering solution $\psi$ is a declared generalized
stationary solution, not an element of $L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$; it is not
a preparation of the model, and no Born probability is read from it. The
numbers $T,R$ are exact model quantities of the declared solution, read as
ratios of currents under the model's scattering reading; the statement
contains no wave-packet construction, no time-dependent limit, no detector
response and no measured count, and it asserts neither that a particle passes
through the barrier nor that it is reflected.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.4.2, printed pages 60-63 (PDF pages 63-66): tunnelling through a finite potential barrier, the matching calculation and the transmission probability

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.3, printed pages 84-89 (PDF pages 92-97): scattering of free particles, incoming and outgoing amplitudes, reflection and transmission, and tunnelling through a potential barrier

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 9.6-9.7, printed pages 209-220 (PDF pages 221-232): spectral transformations and the spectra of one-dimensional Schroedinger operators; PDF page = printed page + 12

items.physical_scope: The line model of the pair with the declared rectangular barrier of height U and width a, in the scattering reading of the model: the unique bounded piecewise-classical stationary solution with prescribed asymptotics, its conserved probability current, the exact transmission and reflection coefficients with the flux balance T+R=1, the identification of T and R with ratios of the transmitted and reflected currents to the reference current of an incoming reference amplitude of one inverse square root metre, and the thick-barrier error bound. The scattering solution is a declared generalized stationary solution and not an element of the model state space; the statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared barrier data and the cited mathematics, and asserts no wave-packet dynamics, no detector, no count and no empirical result.

items.title: Finite square well: bound-state conditions, simplicity and count
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and spin label $s=0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $a>0$,
$U>0$ and let
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}-U,&|x|<a,\\ 0,&|x|>a,\end{cases}$$
with arbitrary real endpoint values $V(-a)$ and $V(a)$, so that $V$ is a total bounded measurable function. It is read in joules, with $U$ in joules and $a$ in metres; let $H_{\mathrm w}$ be
the assigned energy operator of the line model with this potential, so that by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]]
$D(H_{\mathrm w})=H^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_{\mathrm w}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi$; finally put
$K:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar$. Then:

(a) $(H_{\mathrm w},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable; $H_{\mathrm
w}$ is self-adjoint on $H^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and bounded below.

(b) *Bound-state conditions.* For $E<0$ with $-U<E<0$ write
$\varepsilon:=-E$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m\varepsilon}/\hbar>0$ and
$k:=\sqrt{2m(U-\varepsilon)}/\hbar>0$, so that $k^{2}+\kappa^{2}=K^{2}$. Then
$E$ is an eigenvalue of $H_{\mathrm w}$ if and only if
$$k\tan(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(even case)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad -k\cot(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(odd case)} .$$
Every such eigenvalue is simple; its eigenfunction is, up to a nonzero scalar,
$x\mapsto\cos(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by $ce^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the
even case, and $x\mapsto\sin(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by
$c\,\operatorname{sgn}(x)e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the odd case. No $E\le-U$
and no $E\ge0$ is an eigenvalue, so every eigenvalue of $H_{\mathrm w}$ lies in
$(-U,0)$; the bound-state energies of the model are exactly these eigenvalues,
and each bound state is stationary with energy equal to its eigenvalue.

(c) *Count.* The number of negative eigenvalues of $H_{\mathrm w}$ equals
$\bigl\lceil 2aK/\pi\bigr\rceil$; more precisely, the equations of (b) have
exactly one solution $k$ in each interval
$\bigl(\frac{n\pi}{2a},\frac{(n+1)\pi}{2a}\bigr)$, $n\ge0$, whose left
endpoint satisfies $\frac{n\pi}{2a}<K$, and no solution in $(0,K)$ elsewhere,
and the solutions are alternatively of even type ($n$ even) and odd type
($n$ odd). In particular $H_{\mathrm w}$ has at least one bound state for all
$a,U>0$.

(d) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared well
data $a,U$ and the cited mathematics; the energies are read in joules when
$a$ is in metres, $U$ in joules and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. No material
well, impurity or measured spectrum is identified with the model, and no
empirical result is asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.3.1, printed pages 42-48 (PDF pages 45-51): the finite potential well, matching conditions, parity, the even and odd root conditions and the finite number of bound states

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.1, printed pages 75-79 (PDF pages 83-87): the square potential well, its parity decomposition, the condition k tan(ka)=K and the bound-state count

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 9.7, printed pages 214-220 (PDF pages 226-232): the spectra of one-dimensional Schroedinger operators, the essential spectrum [0,infinity) for decaying potentials (Lemma 9.35) and the Sturm nodal count below the essential spectrum (Theorem 9.40); PDF page = printed page + 12

items.physical_scope: The line model of the pair with the declared finite square well potential of depth U and half-width a: self-adjointness and boundedness below of the assigned energy operator, the exact root conditions for its negative eigenvalues, the absence of eigenvalues outside the interval (-U,0), the simplicity and parity of the bound states, the bound-state count, and the stationary-state reading of the eigenpairs. The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared potential data and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured spectrum, no material well and no empirical result.

items.title: Interval models: discrete spectra, complete eigenbases, min-max bounds and nodal counts
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), read
through the declared interval models
[[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] with $0<L<\infty$,
$m>0$, $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a real
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ write
$\|V\|_{\infty}:=\max_{x\in[0,L]}|V(x)|$ and put
$\tilde V:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, so that the assigned
energy operators of the definition satisfy
$H_{D,V}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)(A_{D}+M_{\tilde V})$ and
$H_{\alpha\beta,V}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha\beta,\tilde V}$. Then:

(a) *Dirichlet interval model.* $(H_{D,V},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp
observable; $H_{D,V}$ is self-adjoint with compact resolvent and has a complete
orthonormal family $(\psi_{n})_{n\ge1}$ of eigenvectors. Its eigenvalues,
listed with multiplicity, form a sequence
$\mathcal E_{1}\le\mathcal E_{2}\le\cdots$ with
$\mathcal E_{n}\to\infty$ and
$\sigma(H_{D,V})=\{\mathcal E_{n}:n\ge1\}$, and no other spectral points; each
eigenspace is one-dimensional, so the list is strict,
$\mathcal E_{1}<\mathcal E_{2}<\cdots$, and the eigenvector belonging to
$\mathcal E_{n}$ has exactly $n-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$. The min-max comparison
$$\Bigl|\mathcal E_{n}-\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}}\Bigr| \le\|V\|_{\infty}\qquad(n\ge1)$$
holds. If $V=0$, a complete orthonormal family of eigenpairs of $H_{D,0}$ is
$\bigl(\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}},\,e_{n}\bigr)$ with
$e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$, $n\ge1$, a complete orthonormal family of
$L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$. Every eigenvector at the displayed energy is a
nonzero scalar multiple of the corresponding $e_n$.

(b) *Robin interval model.* For real $\alpha,\beta$ (the declared boundary
parameters in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$), $(H_{\alpha\beta,V},\mathrm J)$ is an
assigned sharp observable; $H_{\alpha\beta,V}$ is self-adjoint with compact
resolvent; it has a complete orthonormal eigenfamily, every eigenspace is
one-dimensional, its spectrum consists exactly of its eigenvalues, which can
be listed strictly increasingly as $\mathcal E_{1}<\mathcal E_{2}<\cdots$ with
$\mathcal E_{n}\to\infty$, and its essential spectrum is empty. With
$\lambda_{n}:=2m\mathcal E_{n}/\hbar^{2}$ and $u_{a}(\cdot,\lambda)$ the unique
$C^{2}$ solution of $-u''+\tilde Vu=\lambda u$ with $u(0)=1$, $u'(0)=\alpha$,
one has $u_{a}(L,\lambda_{n})\ne0$ and
$$\beta=\frac{u_{a}'(L,\lambda_{n})}{u_{a}(L,\lambda_{n})}\qquad(n\ge1).$$

(c) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, on the declared
boundary conditions and on the cited mathematics. The boundary conditions and
parameters are declared model assumptions; the eigenvalues are read in joules
when $V$ and $\hbar$ enter in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. No laboratory wall, box or
surface is identified with the boundary conditions, no measured spectrum is
asserted, and no completeness of any continuum or scattering object is
claimed.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.1.2, printed pages 24-27 (PDF pages 27-30): the infinite potential well, its boundary conditions, eigenfunctions and quantized energies

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 9.1-9.2, printed pages 181-195 (PDF pages 193-207): Sturm-Liouville operators and separated self-adjoint boundary conditions (Theorem 9.6); Section 9.7, printed pages 214-220 (PDF pages 226-232): one-dimensional line operators, Sturm comparison and the full-line nodal count below the essential spectrum (Theorem 9.40 has line-domain hypotheses); PDF page = printed page + 12
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.1, printed pages 75-79 (PDF pages 83-87): the square potential well, its parity decomposition and its discrete bound states

items.title: The zero-range (delta) model: self-adjointness and the unique attractive bound-state preparation
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] and the declared zero-range
model of [[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] clause (d) with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, coupling $g\in\mathbb R$ (in joule
metres) and $\alpha_{g}=2mg/\hbar^{2}$. Let
$H_{g}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha_{g}}$ be the assigned energy operator of the
zero-range model on the domain $D(H_{g})=D(A_{\alpha_{g}})$ of the interface
operator. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{g})$ consists exactly of the classes $u\in H^{1}(\mathbb R)$ whose
restrictions to $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$ are of class $H^{2}$, subject to
the interface condition
$$u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\frac{2mg}{\hbar^{2}}\,u^{*}(0),$$
On that domain, $(H_gu)|_{\mathbb R_\pm}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2(u|_{\mathbb R_\pm})$, where $\mathbb R_+=(0,\infty)$, $\mathbb R_-=(-\infty,0)$ and each second weak derivative is taken on its open half-line; these two $L^2$ classes are glued across the null point $0$. The action is not the global weak second derivative of $u$ on $\mathbb R$. $(H_{g},\mathrm J)$ is
an assigned sharp observable: $H_{g}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{g})$.

(b) *Repulsive and free couplings.* If $g\ge0$, then $H_{g}$ has no negative
eigenvalue, and for every $g\in\mathbb R$ the value $0$ is not an eigenvalue of
$H_{g}$.

(c) *Attractive coupling.* If $g<0$, then $H_{g}$ has exactly one negative
eigenvalue, namely
$$E_{g}=-\frac{mg^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}<0,$$
and its eigenspace is one-dimensional, spanned by the unit class
$$\psi_{g}(x)=\sqrt{\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}}\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}|x|\Bigr).$$
For $g<0$ this is the unique bound-state preparation of the zero-range model: every
eigenvector of $H_{g}$ with negative eigenvalue is a nonzero multiple of
$\psi_{g}$, the preparation $[\psi_{g}]$ is stationary with energy $E_{g}$, and
the energy outcome law assigns probability one to $\{E_{g}\}$.

(d) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
interface realization and the cited mathematics; the coupling $g$ is a
declared model parameter, not a measured quantity. No scattering coefficient,
no transmission or reflection statement, no material impurity and no measured
spectrum is asserted; the formal writing $g\,\delta(x)$ is not used as a
function and no potential in $L^{2}$ is involved.

items.title: What the one-dimensional potentials page establishes, assumes and defers
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What is established.** The page fixes a declared effective one-dimensional
model of a spinless massive particle
([[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]]) and proves, as
conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics, the
following statements. The mathematical lemmas
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] identify the
free operator with the weak second-derivative operator and transfer
self-adjointness, resolvents, spectra and eigenfamilies along positive
scaling; [[lem-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-flux-identity]] proves the
one-dimensional continuity identity and the constancy of the current of a
stationary solution.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-line-model-energy-and-stationary-states]] establishes
that the declared energy operator of the line model with a real bounded
measurable potential is an assigned sharp observable, generates the unitary
flow of the model, and that its stationary preparations are exactly the
eigenrays with point-mass energy law.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-interval-spectra-completeness-and-nodes]] establishes,
for the declared Dirichlet and separated Robin interval models with continuous
real potentials, self-adjointness with compact resolvent, complete
orthonormal eigenbases, discreteness and simplicity of the spectra, the
min-max comparison of the Dirichlet energies with the free box energies and
the nodal counts, together with the Robin eigenvalue condition.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-bound-states]] gives the exact root
conditions, simplicity, parity and count of the bound states of the finite
square well, and
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-delta-point-interaction-bound-state]] gives the
self-adjointness of the declared zero-range interface operator and its unique
bound state for attractive coupling with the exact energy
$-mg^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})$. [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]
gives the unique scattering solution of the rectangular barrier, its conserved
current, the exact coefficients $T$ and $R$, the flux balance $T+R=1$, the
reading of $T$ and $R$ as fractions of the reference current, and the
thick-barrier error bound.

**What is assumed, not derived.** The page's model data are declared, not
derived: the reduction of the three-dimensional massive-particle model to one
spatial dimension, the position and momentum assignments of the line model,
the Dirichlet and Robin boundary conditions with their boundary parameters,
the zero-range interface condition with its coupling, and the scattering
reading of the current ratios. Each is an assumption of the pair in the sense
of the preparation and apparatus discipline P7; an identification of a
concrete material system with any of them is a tested identification with
uncertainty and is not produced by these items. The operators rest on the
mathematical supplier [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
and on the interval and contact mathematics of
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and the items of the intervals
pair, whose Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses are inherited by
every consumer above.

**What is not addressed.** No wave-packet or time-dependent scattering limit
is computed; no arrival-time, detector-response, efficiency or background
model is declared; no count, rate, cross-section or measured spectrum appears.
The scattering solution of the barrier item is not an element of the model
state space, so no Born probability is read from it. Potentials with
unbounded or singular growth, the harmonic oscillator, the Coulomb problem,
higher-dimensional scattering, resonant and above-barrier behaviour, and the
Airy/WKB connection problem for smooth barriers belong to other pages of the
category and are not consumed or anticipated here. The example page of the
pair carries exact finite checks of the barrier and well formulas; those are
model computations, not measurements.

**Evidence status.** The page is a conditional model development. It contains
no experiment, no reported observation, no uncertainty statement and no
statistical inference; agreement of any of its formulas with data would be
evidence about the combined model, apparatus and analysis assumptions and
would not prove the model.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Chapter 2, printed pages 19-63 (PDF pages 22-66): one-dimensional potentials, bound states, scattering and tunnelling
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 5, printed pages 75-103 (PDF pages 83-111): motion in step potentials, wells, barriers and scattering

items.title: Tunnelling through a rectangular barrier: an exactly solvable scaling and its thick-barrier comparison
items.statement:
Work in the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$,
action constant $\hbar>0$, and lengths, energies and currents read in the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Declare the incident
energy $E>0$ and the barrier height $U:=2E$, so that
$\kappa:=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar=:k$; declare further the barrier
width $a:=\ln(10)/\kappa>0$, so that $\kappa a=\ln 10$ and
$e^{\kappa a}=10$. Consider the scattering solution of
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]] for this barrier and
set $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$. Then, as exact identities in the model:

(i) $C:=U^{2}/(4E(U-E))=1$, $q=1/100$, and
$$T=\frac{400}{10201},\qquad R=1-T=\frac{9801}{10201};$$

(ii) with rational brackets,
$$\frac{3921}{100000}<T<\frac{3922}{100000},\qquad \frac{96078}{100000}<R<\frac{96079}{100000};$$

(iii) the thick-barrier approximation value is
$\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}q=\frac{1}{25}$, the exact difference is
$$T-\frac{1}{25}=-\frac{201}{255025},$$
which lies between $-0.000789$ and $-0.000788$, and the error bound of the
theorem reads
$$\Bigl|T-\frac1{25}\Bigr|\le\frac{201}{125000}=0.001608 ;$$

(iv) since $q=1/100>0$, the transmission $T$ is positive although the
declared barrier height satisfies $U>E$; and by clause (b) of the
barrier theorem the number $T$ is the transmitted fraction of the reference
current $j_{\mathrm{in}}=(\hbar k/m)|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^{2}$, with
$A_{\mathrm{in}}=1\,\mathrm{m}^{-1/2}$, while $R$ is the reflected fraction.

The example is an exact computation in the declared barrier model with
declared data $U,E,a,m,\hbar$ related as above; it records no measurement and
no apparatus value.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.4.2, printed pages 60-63 (PDF pages 63-66): the barrier matching calculation, the transmission probability and the thick-barrier exponential suppression
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.3, printed pages 87-89 (PDF pages 95-97): tunnelling through a potential barrier

items.physical_scope: A finite check in the declared line model of the pair: the rectangular barrier with height twice the incident energy and a width scaling chosen so that the barrier exponent is the natural logarithm of ten. The example computes the exact transmission and reflection coefficients as rational numbers, brackets them by rationals, compares the exact value with the thick-barrier approximation and verifies the theorem's error bound. It is a computation in the model, not a measurement; it reports no count, no apparatus and no empirical value, and it makes no claim about nature.

items.title: Finite square well: an exactly solvable bound state and exact bound-state counts
items.statement:
Work in the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$
and action constant $\hbar>0$, energies, lengths and the depth $U$ read in the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and consider the finite
square well $V(x)=-U$ for $|x|\le a$, $V(x)=0$ for $|x|>a$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-bound-states]] with half-width $a>0$ and
depth $U>0$.

(i) *Exact boundary case of the first branch.* Declare
$$U:=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{16ma^{2}} .$$
Then $K=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar=\pi\sqrt2/(4a)$, the count parameter is
$2aK/\pi=\sqrt2/2$, there is exactly one bound state, it is an even
(cosine-type) state, and its binding energy is exactly
$$E=-\frac{U}{2}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{32ma^{2}} .$$
For this declared depth the root of the even condition is exactly
$k=\kappa=\pi/(4a)$.

(ii) *Exact counts at declared depths.* With
$$U:=\frac{25\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}}{32ma^{2}}$$
one has $K=5\pi/(4a)$ and $2aK/\pi=5/2$, so there are exactly three bound
states, with types even, odd and even in order of increasing energy. With
$U:=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(8ma^{2})$ one has $K=\pi/(2a)$ and exactly one bound
state; with $U:=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(2ma^{2})$ one has $K=\pi/a$ and exactly two
bound states. For every declared depth $U>0$ there is at least one bound
state.

(iii) *Rational bracket of the first case.*
$$\frac{707}{1000}<\frac{2aK}{\pi}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}<\frac{708}{1000},$$
so the count $\lceil 2aK/\pi\rceil$ equals one in case (i).

The example is a conditional computation in the declared well model and
asserts no measured binding energy; the identities in (i) and (ii) are exact in
the model at the displayed declared data.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.3.1, printed pages 42-48 (PDF pages 45-51): the finite well, the even and odd root conditions and the graphical solution count

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.1, printed pages 75-79 (PDF pages 83-87): the square well, the condition k tan(ka)=K, the always-present ground state and the count thresholds

items.physical_scope: Finite checks in the declared line model of the pair for the finite square well: an exactly solvable depth at which the unique bound state has energy minus one half of the depth, and exact bound-state counts and branch parities for declared depths. The example is a conditional computation in the model; it reports no measurement, no material well and no empirical value, and asserts no conclusion about nature.

items.title: The Dirichlet box: exact spectrum, nodes, constant shift and gaps
items.statement:
Work in the declared Dirichlet interval model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] clause (b) with
$0<L<\infty$, mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$, and energies in joules
under [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then, as exact identities
in the model:

(i) *Free box.* For $V=0$ the eigenpairs of the assigned energy operator
$H_{D,0}$ are exactly
$$\Bigl(\mathcal E_{n},\,e_{n}\Bigr),\qquad \mathcal E_{n}=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}}{2mL^{2}},\qquad e_{n}(x)=\sqrt{\frac2L}\,\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\quad n\ge1,$$
the family $(e_{n})_{n\ge1}$ is a complete orthonormal family of
$L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$, each eigenvalue is simple, and $e_{n}$ has exactly
$n-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$, namely the points $x_{k}=kL/n$, $k=1,\dots,n-1$.

(ii) *Constant shift.* If $V=c$ is the constant potential of value $c\in
\mathbb R$ (joules), then $H_{D,c}$ has exactly the same eigenfunctions
$e_{n}$ and the eigenvalues $\mathcal E_{n}+c$; consequently the min-max
comparison bound of the interval theorem is attained with equality,
$|\mathcal E_{n}+c-\mathcal E_{n}|=|c|=\|V\|_{\infty}$ for every $n$.

(iii) *Gaps.* $\mathcal E_{n+1}-\mathcal E_{n}
=\frac{\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}(2n+1)}{2mL^{2}}>0$, so the spectrum is strictly
increasing.

The example is an exact conditional computation in the declared box model
and asserts no measured transition energy.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 2.1.2, printed pages 24-27 (PDF pages 27-30): the infinite potential well, its sine eigenfunctions, nodal structure and quantized energies

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 9.1, printed pages 181-187 (PDF pages 193-199): Sturm-Liouville interval setup; separated self-adjoint boundary conditions are treated in Section 9.2, including Theorem 9.6. The full-line nodal theorem in Section 9.7 has different domain hypotheses and is not used here

items.physical_scope: Finite checks in the declared Dirichlet interval model of the pair: the free box eigenpairs, their explicit nodal points, the exact spectrum under a constant potential shift, the attainment of the min-max bound and the eigenvalue gaps. The example is an exact conditional computation in the declared confined model; it asserts no material wall, no measured spectrum and no empirical result.

items.title: What the one-dimensional potentials examples establish
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**The three computations.**
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-rectangular-barrier-tunnelling-and-thick-limit]] treats
the rectangular barrier of [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]
at the exactly solvable scaling $U=2E$ with $\kappa a=\ln 10$: it obtains
$T=400/10201$ and $R=9801/10201$ as exact rationals, brackets them by
$3921/100000<T<3922/100000$, compares the exact value with the thick-barrier
value $1/25$ (the difference is exactly $-201/255025$) and verifies the
theorem's error bound $201/125000=0.001608$; the computation is a finite check
of the model formulas, including the positivity of transmission through a
classically forbidden barrier.
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-exact-root-and-count]] exhibits a declared
well depth at which the unique bound state is exactly solvable (even state,
$k=\kappa=\pi/(4a)$, binding energy $E=-U/2=-\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(32ma^{2})$),
verifies the even root condition with the special value $\tan(\pi/4)=1$, and
verifies the count and branch criterion at declared depths: exactly three
bound states with types even, odd, even when $2aK/\pi=5/2$, exactly one when
$2aK/\pi=1$, exactly two when $2aK/\pi=2$, and at least one for every
$a,U>0$.
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-box-spectrum-and-nodes]] records the exact free Dirichlet
box eigenpairs $\mathcal E_{n}=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}/(2mL^{2})$ with sine
eigenfunctions, their explicit $n-1$ nodal points $kL/n$, the exact spectrum
$\mathcal E_{n}+c$ of a constant potential with the min-max bound attained,
and the positive gaps $\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}(2n+1)/(2mL^{2})$.

**What is and is not compared.** The comparisons are internal: the exact
barrier formula and its thick-barrier approximation, the exact well root
condition and the exact branch count, and the exact box spectrum with the
min-max bound. They verify the cited theorems at declared parameter points by
exact rational and algebraic checks; they are not numerical approximations of
generic transcendental roots, they contain no simulation presented as data,
and they report no measured value, no uncertainty and no significance
statement. The displayed decimals are rational bracket endpoints or exact
terminating decimal expansions of rational values, including
$201/125000=0.001608$; each is justified in the verifications.

**Evidence status.** All three items are conditional computations in the
declared line, well and box models of the pair's A page, under the same P1,
P2, P4, P5 assumptions and the same cited mathematics; the empirical
qualifications of the A page carry over unchanged. Nothing on this page is an
observation, an apparatus model or a statistical inference, and agreement of
the displayed identities with any measurement would be evidence about the
combined model and apparatus assumptions rather than a proof of the model.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 5, printed pages 75-103 (PDF pages 83-111): square wells, scattering and tunnelling

items.title: Eigenspaces of the diagonal operator
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a complete orthonormal family of $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), let $(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]:
$$D(A)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\sum_n\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Ax=\sum_n\lambda_n\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n .$$
Then:

(a) for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the eigenspace of $A$ at $\lambda$ is the closed linear span of the basis vectors carrying the eigenvalue $\lambda$:
$$\ker(A-\lambda I)=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:\lambda_n=\lambda\};$$
in particular $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ exactly when $\lambda=\lambda_n$ for some $n$;

(b) if $\lambda_m\ne\lambda_n$ whenever $m\ne n$, then $\ker(A-\lambda_nI)=\mathbb Ce_n$ for every $n$: every eigenspace is one-dimensional with eigenvector $e_n$, the eigenspaces are pairwise orthogonal, and every nonzero eigenvector of $A$ is a nonzero multiple of some $e_n$;

(c) in the situation of (b) the linear span of all eigenspaces of $A$ is $\operatorname{span}\{e_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, which is dense in $H$.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §2.4 pp. 73-74 (eigenvalues, eigenspaces and the multiplication-operator example)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §1 pp. 1-9 (non-degeneracy of the oscillator ground state and the ladder spectrum)

items.title: Transport of spectral projection-valued measures along isometric bijections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $U:H\to K$ be a bijective linear map with
$$\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle x,y\rangle_H\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in H .$$
Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and define
$$D(T'):=U D(T),\qquad T'(Ux):=U(Tx)\quad(x\in D(T)).$$
Then:

(a) $T'$ is well defined, linear, densely defined and self-adjoint on $K$;

(b) the assignment $E(B):=U E_T(B) U^{-1}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, and it is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$;

(c) for every unit vector $x\in H$ the scalar laws of the two operators agree,
$$\mu^{T'}_{Ux}(B):=\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2=:\mu^{T}_x(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$

(d) $\sigma(T')=\sigma(T)$.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §3.1 printed pages 89-92 (PDF pages 101-104): integration against a projection-valued measure, the functional calculus and unitary equivalence (3.30) with equal spectra

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 3 'Linear algebra: vector spaces and operators', §7 'Hermitian and Unitary operators', printed pages 24-28: unitary operators preserve inner products and the adjoint/unitary calculus

items.title: The quadratic-potential oscillator model of the framework
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1)$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $1$ is the dimensionless unit, and the spectral coordinate $n$ records the number of excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1)$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §3.1 printed pages 37-41 (PDF pages 45-49): the quadratic potential as the equilibrium approximation, the Hamiltonian (3.1), the length scale (3.15) and the stationary states
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §1 printed pages 1-9: the quantum harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian, its length scale and its spectrum

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §8.3 printed pages 178-179 (PDF pages 190-191): the oscillator as an exactly solvable self-adjoint operator and the polynomial-Gaussian eigenbasis

items.physical_scope: The one-dimensional and isotropic three-dimensional quadratic-potential (harmonic) oscillator model of a spinless massive particle of the non-relativistic framework: state space L^2(R,dx) respectively L^2(R^3,dx), position and momentum operators with declared units m and kg m s^-1, the assigned energy observable H_osc with unit J and a potential-energy convention in which V(0) is subtracted, and the assigned dimensionless excitation-number observable N_psi with declared unit 1. The one-dimensional energy operator is the self-adjoint realization of the formal differential expression -hbar^2/(2m) d^2/dx^2 + (m omega^2/2) x^2 fixed by the oscillator scaling theorem for the declared parameters m>0, omega>0 and hbar>0. The model is an adopted idealization of the quadratic part of a C^2 scalar potential-energy function V:R->R near a non-degenerate local minimum, after subtracting V(0); it asserts no measured values, no derivation of m or omega from any microscopic theory, no damping, driving or time dependence, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic or relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect.

items.title: The energy observable of the oscillator model: spectrum, eigenbasis and outcome law
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $(g_n)$, $D$, $A$, $(\psi_n)$ and $H_1$ be the Hermite family, the unitary, the dimensionless diagonal operator, the scaled eigenbasis and the energy operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a) and (b), so that $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's one-dimensional assigned energy observable of the model definition clause (c). Put
$$N_\psi:=DND^{-1},\qquad a_\psi:=DaD^{-1},\qquad a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1},$$
where $N$ is the number operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and $N_\psi$ is the assigned excitation-number observable with unit $1$ of the model definition clause (c); these are the number and ladder operators transported from that lemma, with domains $D(N_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(N)\}$, $D(a_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a)\}$ and $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a^\dagger)\}$. Write $E_n:=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and, for the three-dimensional realization of the model definition clause (d), let $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ and $(\psi_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^3}$ be its assigned energy observable and its product eigenbasis. Then:

(a) **Spectrum, eigenbasis and simplicity.** $D(H_1)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$, the family $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $\mathcal H_1$ and its algebraic span is a core for $H_1$, $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, and the spectrum and eigenspaces are
$$\sigma(H_1)=\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\},\qquad \ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n\quad(n\in\mathbb N);$$
the ground energy is $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and the gap between consecutive levels is $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$;

(b) **Excitation reading.** $H_1=\hbar\omega\bigl(N_\psi+\tfrac12I\bigr)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$; $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with spectrum $\mathbb N$ and eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$; $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are closed with $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$, and on the eigenbasis
$$a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad a_\psi\psi_0=0,\qquad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1},\qquad N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n;$$
the eigenspace of $N_\psi$ at each $n\in\mathbb N$ is exactly $\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its nonzero eigenvectors are precisely the nonzero scalar multiples of the $\psi_n$; the outcome law of $N_\psi$ in the pure preparation of $\psi_n$ is the point mass $\delta_n$;

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in\mathcal H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; in particular the law has no mass outside $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$;

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model and the cited mathematics. They concern the eigenvalue list, the eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic outcome law of the model's assigned energy observable; they assert no measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus realization, no selection rule and no transition rate. The identification of a laboratory resonance or spectral line with an eigenvalue difference of this model is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not a consequence of this theorem.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §1 printed pages 1-9: the spectrum E_n = hbar omega (n+1/2), the eigenstates and the ground-state equation
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §3.1 printed pages 37-41 (PDF pages 45-49): the energy levels (3.12), the non-degenerate ground state and the ladder operators

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, §8.3 printed pages 178-179 (PDF pages 190-191): completeness of the polynomial-Gaussian eigenbasis and the exact oscillator spectrum

items.physical_scope: The energy and excitation-number observables of the quadratic-potential oscillator model: for the one-dimensional realization with parameters m>0, omega>0 and hbar>0 the exact energy eigenvalue list hbar omega (n+1/2) under the convention that subtracts the potential-energy value V(0), with quantum ground energy hbar omega/2, one-dimensional eigenspaces spanned by the Hermite eigenbasis, completeness of that basis, the energy gap hbar omega, the assigned dimensionless excitation-number observable in unit 1 and the atomic outcome laws; and for the isotropic three-dimensional realization of the spinless massive particle the energy spectrum hbar omega (M+3/2) with multiplicity (M+1)(M+2)/2. The statement is a conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5, of the adopted oscillator model and of the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured spectral line, no value of m, omega or hbar and no empirical result.

items.title: The coherent states of the oscillator model
items.statement:
**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], and let $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the model's assigned excitation-number observable of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c), with its stated domain and unit $1$.

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a),
$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in\mathcal H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$, with modulus $e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations (their overlap modulus is less than $1$, whereas unit vectors on the same ray have overlap modulus $1$) and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its amplitude is $|z|$; when $z\ne0$, its phase is the class $\arg z\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, while $z=0$ has zero amplitude and no phase label. The mathematical coherent-state series gives the quadratic-form value $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$ for the assigned, dimensionless excitation-number observable $(N_\psi,1)$; this is the number coordinate intended by the model's P2 reading. Under the model's flow, [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (c), (e), (f) gives $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$ and the position and momentum means $\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}(ze^{-i\omega t})$ and $\sqrt2\hbar\operatorname{Im}(ze^{-i\omega t})/\ell$, respectively; thus the mean pair, in coordinates scaled by $\sqrt2\ell$ and $\sqrt2\hbar/\ell$, rotates with the phase label at angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this interpretation of the label, not an outcome of measuring the label itself.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §§4.1-4.3 printed pages 26-33: the definition of the coherent state as a translated ground state, its position and momentum expectation values and its uncertainties

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §§4.4-4.5 printed pages 33-41: coherent states in the energy basis, the Poisson number distribution and general coherent states

items.physical_scope: The coherent states of the one-dimensional quadratic-potential oscillator model of the framework: for each complex dimensionless label z the unit vector Psi_z obtained by transporting the coherent vector of the Hermite oscillator basis along the model's scaling unitary, its properties as a preparation of the model (normalization, annihilation-operator eigenvalue z, non-orthogonality), and the amplitude and phase reading of z together with its operator-expectation excitation-number coordinate in the assigned unit 1. The definition asserts no measurement procedure, no uniqueness or minimality property among preparations, no overcompleteness or resolution of unity, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

items.title: Fluctuations of the oscillator coherent states and the position-momentum relation of the model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', §4.3 printed pages 30-33: the coherent-state uncertainties (4.31)-(4.33) and the time-independence of Delta x

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §3.1 printed pages 37-41 (PDF pages 45-49): the Gaussian ground state, its position and momentum dispersions and the saturated uncertainty product
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), §2.2 printed pages 34-41 (PDF pages 37-44): the oscillator eigenstates and the normalizable Gaussian ground state

items.physical_scope: The preparation spreads of position and momentum in the coherent states of the one-dimensional oscillator model, the exact value hbar/2 of their product, the one-dimensional position-momentum relation Delta Q Delta P >= hbar/2 for every unit preparation vector in the common domain of the two model operators, and the saturation of that relation by every coherent preparation. The statement is a conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2 and P5, of the adopted oscillator model, of the cited uncertainty and moment results and of the cited mathematics; it concerns the two separately assigned outcome laws in one preparation and asserts no joint outcome law, no apparatus resolution, no disturbance and no empirical result.

items.title: Evolution of the oscillator coherent states: classical mean motion and stationary fluctuations
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and define $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) **Coherent evolution.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $\mathcal H_1$ and
$$U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\,\Psi_{z(t)};$$
consequently the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ evolves under the model's Schroedinger dynamics to the coherent preparation $[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, and the labels of the evolved family rotate with angular frequency $\omega$;

(b) **Classical mean motion.** The preparation means of position and momentum at time $t$ are
$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\qquad \langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),$$
equivalently, for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ with $x(t):=\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}$, $p(t):=\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}$; these functions are differentiable with $\dot x(t)=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$, so the means follow the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$ through $(x_0,p_0)$;

(c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has
$$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution;

(d) **Energy statistics.** The mean and the outcome law of the assigned energy observable in the coherent preparation are
$$\langle H_1\rangle_{z}=\hbar\omega\Bigl(|z|^{2}+\frac12\Bigr),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}\bigl(\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\}\bigr)=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the pushforward under $n\mapsto\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ of the **Poisson law** on $\mathbb N$ with parameter $s:=|z|^2$, defined by the weights $p_n=e^{-s}s^n/n!$, with $s^0=1$ also at $s=0$; consequently $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the model's spectrum theorem, the coherent-state fluctuation theorem and the cited mathematics. They concern the exact evolution of the model's coherent preparations and the statistics of its assigned observables; no measurement record, no apparatus realization, no damping or driving and no empirical value is asserted, and the identification of the mean motion with the motion of a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, §3.2 printed pages 41-44 (PDF pages 49-52): the oscillation of the position expectation value at the classical frequency omega
