Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.2 and 4.3, printed pages 59-62 and 68-70 (PDF pages 67-70 and 76-78): translating kets, momentum as the generator of translations and translational invariance with conservation of momentum; PDF page = printed page + 8

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 7.2-7.3, printed pages 167-169 (PDF pages 179-181), equations (7.24) and (7.27): the free Hamiltonian and evolution as Fourier multipliers in the convention hbar=1, m=1/2; Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187), equations (8.3)-(8.7): translations, momentum generators and conservation

items.title: A bounded nonconstant potential with no nontrivial translational symmetry
items.statement:
Let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be any real, bounded, measurable, nonconstant
potential energy, expressed in joules. Then for every nonzero $a\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ the
translation $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of the declared bounded-potential dynamics
with energy $H_{V}$.
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the declared massive model with a bounded measurable potential energy: a positive energy scale times the indicator of the ball of radius one metre has no nontrivial translational symmetry, so no nonzero translation commutes with its bounded-potential energy operator, while the potential itself is bounded and measurable and its model is self-adjoint on W^{2,2}. The item refutes a universal claim about translations of bounded nonconstant potentials; it asserts nothing about the physics of a laboratory potential and records no measurement.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.3, printed pages 68-70 (PDF pages 76-78): translational invariance of a potential as the condition for momentum conservation
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): momentum conservation for potentials invariant under translations

items.title: A radial bounded potential: rotational and parity symmetry and conservation of the rotation generators
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$, rotation action $U(R)$ and coordinate-rotation generators
$L_{i}$ ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]); assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $v:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and
measurable, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and
measurable with
$$V(x)=v(|x|)\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
a **radial potential almost everywhere** (if $V$ is the composition
$x\mapsto v(|x|)$ everywhere, this holds with empty exceptional set). Let
$$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the bounded-potential energy operator. Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $V(R^{-1}x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, and
$V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$;

(b) every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a
strongly continuous unitary symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved observable: for every preparation $\rho$,
Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
with conserved mean and second moment for unit vectors in $D(L_{i})$ and
time-zero values $\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$, $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$, in the
unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]);

(c) the parity action $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and its outcome law in
every preparation is time-independent;

(d) **Scope.** The example is conditional on the postulates and the bounded
radial class; it computes no eigenvalue, no bound state, no degeneracy and no
radial solution, and the boundedness of $v$ excludes the Coulomb potential and
other unbounded radial models, which require their own self-adjointness and
spectral analysis. No claim is made that any particular physical potential is
radial, and no empirical result is recorded.
items.physical_scope: A model example for the massive spin-s model with a bounded measurable potential that is radial almost everywhere: every spatial rotation is a symmetry, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group, the coordinate-rotation generators are conserved sharp observables in J s, and the parity action is a symmetry with a conserved parity law. The item is conditional on the bounded radial class; it asserts no eigenvalue, bound-state or degeneracy claim, no Coulomb or other unbounded radial model, and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.3-4.3, printed pages 62-70 (PDF pages 70-78): the rotation operator and its generators, the commutator [J_i, S]=0 for scalar operators and the conservation laws of symmetric Hamiltonians; PDF page = printed page + 8

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.1.1, printed pages 96-99 (PDF pages 99-102): the angular momentum commutation relations, with the angular momentum operators as the generators of rotations

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 1.3, printed pages 9-11 (PDF pages 9-11): central potentials and the commutativity of the angular momentum operators with the Hamiltonian (equation (1.70))

items.title: What the worked items of the symmetry companion page establish
items.statement:
## The worked items and what they establish

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
translations need not remain symmetries for nonconstant potentials:
for the bounded measurable potential energy $E_{*}1_{B(0,R)}$, with
$E_{*}>0$ in J and $R=1\,\mathrm m$, no nonzero translation is a symmetry,
because the shifted potential differs from the original on a set of positive
measure, so the symmetry criterion of the translation theorem is not met.
For a specified translation $a$, the criterion is exactly
$V(\cdot-a)=V$ almost everywhere; nonconstancy in a direction alone does
not exclude discrete translations along that direction.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-central-potential-rotation-invariance]] verifies the
almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

## What none of the items establishes

None of the four items is an experiment: no apparatus, preparation map,
calibration, detection model, efficiency, resolution, background model,
sampling model, uncertainty budget, count or dataset appears, and no measured
value of any model parameter is asserted. The objects $m$, $q$ when present,
$s$, the potentials and the conserved laws are model data and model statements
in the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; deciding that a
laboratory system realizes the model, that its potential is approximately
radial or even, or that a transition amplitude is the matrix element computed
here, is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus assumptions, and it is external to this page. In particular the
parity selection rule is an identity about the model's assigned position
observables: turning it into a statement about observed intensities requires a
time-dependent coupling model, the corresponding transition-rate analysis, a
detection model and a sampling model, none of which is supplied here.

## Limits of the statements

The free computation is conditional on $V\equiv0$; the counterexample concerns
one potential inside the bounded measurable class and refutes only the
universal claim that every bounded nonconstant potential has all nonzero
translations as symmetries (potentials constant along a direction keep the
corresponding translations). The central-potential example assumes the radial
identity almost everywhere and a bounded radial function; it asserts no
eigenvalue, bound state, degeneracy, radial solution or spectral line, and its
boundedness hypothesis excludes the Coulomb and other unbounded radial
models. The parity example requires the evenness hypothesis and, for definite
parity, the nondegeneracy of the eigenvalue; at a degenerate eigenvalue only
the eigenspace invariance is asserted. No item of this page makes a claim about
antiunitary or time-reversal symmetries, about superselection, about spinorial
rotations or the internal factor, or about relativistic and field-theoretic
structures.
items.physical_scope: Scope of the companion examples page: an inventory of the exact model computations, the conditional construction and the counterexample it contains, and of the physical questions it does not address. The remark asserts no new dynamics and records no empirical data.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.3-4.3, printed pages 62-70 (PDF pages 70-78): the rotation operator, parity and vector operators, symmetry of the Hamiltonian and conservation laws; PDF page = printed page + 8

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 2.2-2.3.1 and 4.1.1, printed pages 39-47 and 96-99 (PDF pages 42-50 and 99-102): parity of energy eigenfunctions and even/odd bound states, and the angular momentum commutation relations

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): conserved operators and their constant Heisenberg representatives

items.title: Self-adjointness and the flow of a self-adjoint operator perturbed by a bounded operator commuting with its flow
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint
operator on $H$ with domain $D(A)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and let $B$ be a
bounded self-adjoint operator on $H$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with
$$B\,e^{isA}=e^{isA}B\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
where $e^{isA}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{is\lambda}\,dE_A(\lambda)$ is the unitary
group of $A$ in the spectral calculus
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put $A+B$ on its natural domain
$D(A+B):=D(A)\cap D(B)=D(A)$. Then:

(a) $A+B$ is self-adjoint;

(b) $e^{isB}e^{itA}=e^{itA}e^{isB}$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$; the flows of
$A$ and of the bounded $B$ commute;

(c) the family $s\mapsto P(s):=e^{isA}e^{isB}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group
([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]), and its
infinitesimal generator $G$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G=i(A+B)$: the
quotient $\frac1s\bigl(P(s)x-x\bigr)$ converges as $s\to0$ exactly for
$x\in D(A)$, with limit $i(A+B)x$. Consequently $P(s)=e^{is(A+B)}$ for every
$s\in\mathbb R$.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.4 printed pages 73-79 (PDF pages 85-91): resolvents of a self-adjoint operator and the Neumann series for the resolvent, and Section 5.1 printed pages 123-125 (PDF pages 135-137): the unitary group generated by a self-adjoint operator and Stone's theorem

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1-4.2, printed pages 58-68 (PDF pages 66-76): continuous transformations and their generators, and the transformation of operators under a unitary

items.title: The SU(2) lift of the spatial rotation action on the component-valued wave-function space and its coordinate generators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put
$r:=2s+1$, and let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the
special orthogonal group ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]), let
$U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be the componentwise spatial rotation action
$$(U(R)f)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r)$$
of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], and let
$\rho_0:SU(2)\to SO(3)$ be the quaternion conjugation cover of
[[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]], using the matrix identification
$$a+bi+cj+dk\longmapsto\begin{pmatrix}a+bi&c+di\\-c+di&a-bi\end{pmatrix}$$
and the imaginary basis $(i,j,k)$ of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].
For the physical coordinate axes used by the Pauli matrices fix
$$C:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&-1\\0&-1&0\\-1&0&0\end{pmatrix}\in SO(3),\qquad \rho(W):=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C.$$
Thus $\rho$ is the same two-sheeted cover transported to the axes
$(Ce_1,Ce_2,Ce_3)=(-e_3,-e_2,-e_1)$; it is not the literal matrix $\rho_0$ in the imaginary basis. It is smooth by
[[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]]. Let
$F_{s}:\mathcal S_{2s}\to V_{s}=\mathbb C^{r}$ be the unitary identification
$v_{k}\mapsto e_{s-k}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] clause
(d) (for $s=0$, $\mathcal S_{0}=\mathbb C v_{0}$ and $F_{0}v_{0}:=1$),
define $D_{s}:SU(2)\to U(V_{s})$ by
$D_{s}(W):=F_{s}U_{2s}(W)F_{s}^{-1}$ for $s>0$ and
$D_{0}(W):=I_{\mathbb C}$, and let $S_{i}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the self-adjoint
spin endomorphisms of $V_{s}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (a). By clauses
(b),(d),(f) of the theorem the maps $D_{s}$ are strongly continuous unitary
representations of $SU(2)$.
For $W\in SU(2)$ define the matrix action $M_{s}(W)\in\mathcal B(H_{s})$ and
the lifted operator $U_{s}(W)$ by
$$(M_{s}(W)f)(x):=D_{s}(W)\bigl(f(x)\bigr),\qquad U_{s}(W):=U(\rho(W))\,M_{s}(W)\qquad(f\in H_{s},\ x\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
where the matrix $D_{s}(W)$ acts on the column vector $f(x)\in\mathbb C^{r}$.
For any $T\in\operatorname{End}(V_s)$ write $M_Tf(x):=Tf(x)$ almost
everywhere, and define the spin operators on $H_s$ by
$$S_i:=M_{S_i^{\mathrm{fin}}},\qquad D(S_i):=H_s.$$
These bounded self-adjoint operators, rather than the endomorphisms
$S_i^{\mathrm{fin}}$ on $V_s$, occur in all sums, spectral commutation
claims and conjugations on $H_s$ below.
Finally let $R_{i}(t)$, $i=1,2,3$, be the coordinate rotation matrices and
$L_{i}$ the self-adjoint coordinate-rotation generators on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] (so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$), and put
$A_{i}(t):=\cos(t/2)I_{2}-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_{i}\in SU(2)$ with the Pauli
matrices $\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e). Then:

(a) for every $W\in SU(2)$ the operator $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary, with
$U_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})$ for
all $W_{1},W_{2}\in SU(2)$, and $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]);

(b) $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and every $i$, and
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(c) the operators $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ strongly commute (their spectral
projection-valued measures commute;
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), the sum $J_{i}:=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with
domain $D(J_{i}):=D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint, and
$$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
moreover for $W\in SU(2)$ one has the conjugation identities including
domains
$$U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l},\qquad U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l},$$
where $Q_{j},P_{k}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a) and
$\rho(W)_{lj}$ are the matrix entries of the transported cover in the standard basis; the sums mean the maximal directional realizations $Q(\rho(W)e_j)$ and $P(\rho(W)e_k)$ of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clause (b), with domains $U_s(W)D(Q_j)$ and $U_s(W)D(P_k)$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is a mathematical statement about the
finite-dimensional spin representation and the componentwise rotation action;
it asserts no physical interpretation, no measurement, no dynamics and no
value of $\hbar$, $s$ or $W$. The spatial action enters only through
$U(R)=U(\rho(W))$ and the internal action only through $M_{s}(W)$; no action
on a second spatial or internal factor is introduced.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 7.2-7.4, printed pages 145-164 (PDF pages 153-172): orbital generators and spherical harmonics, spin as an intrinsic representation, the rotation of spinors and the spin rotation operators

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 2, printed pages 11-18 (the algebraic theory of angular momentum: ladder operators, multiplets and the spin representations) and Chapter 10 'Addition of Angular Momentum', Sections 1-2, printed pages 1-7 (tensor-lifted addition of angular momenta)

items.title: The orbital Casimir identity: the restrictions of the orbital generators to the degree-l blocks are spin-l models
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]: $S^2$ with its
polar measure $\sigma$, the Hilbert space $L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), the complete orthonormal
family $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks
$V_{l}:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$, the finite span $H$,
the self-adjoint operators $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ with $L_{3}=L_{z}$ and
$L_{i}Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$ for all $l,m,i$, and the diagonal sphere Laplacian $A$
with $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Then for every $l\ge0$:

(a) each $L_{i}$ leaves $V_{l}$ invariant, and the restriction
$L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of the finite-dimensional
inner product space $V_{l}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for $-l\le m\le l$;

(b) the triple $\bigl((1/\hbar)L_{1}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{2}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{3}|_{V_{l}}\bigr)$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$l$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; in particular
$$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F\qquad(F\in V_{l});$$

(c) for every $F$ in the finite span $H$ one has
$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}AF$.

The statement is a mathematical statement about the operators on
$L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation as angular momentum of a
particle is asserted.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.2, printed pages 145-154 (PDF pages 153-162): the orbital angular momentum operators on the spherical harmonic blocks, l(l+1) as the Casimir eigenvalue and the ladder structure of the m multiplets

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 2, printed pages 11-18: the algebraic angular momentum multiplets, J^2 eigenvalue j(j+1) and the ladder conditions

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 8.1-8.2, printed pages 173-178 (PDF pages 185-190): position and momentum, angular momentum, the rotation group generated by the orbital generators and the simultaneous eigenbasis theorem

items.title: Orbital, spin and total angular momentum of the massive spin-s model: assigned sharp observables, units and readings
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables. They satisfy $S_+^*=S_-$; for $s>0$ they
are not self-adjoint, since $S_+e_{-s}=\hbar\sqrt{2s}\,e_{-s+1}\ne0$
whereas $S_-e_{-s}=0$, while for $s=0$ both vanish and are self-adjoint.
For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action, using the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ defined in that lemma (rather than the literal quaternion-coordinate cover $\rho_0$),
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.
items.physical_scope: The angular momentum readings of the massive spin-s particle model: the orbital generators of the spatial coordinate rotations, the internal spin matrices of the spin assignment P6, and their self-adjoint sum, each read as an assigned sharp observable of the framework with units of action, together with the declaration that the internal factor is not a spatial object. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus or detection model, no spin-orbit or relativistic structure and no empirical identification of any laboratory quantity with the operators named.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 7, Sections 7.2 and 7.4, printed pages 145-154 and 158-164 (PDF pages 153-162 and 166-172): orbital angular momentum, spin as an intrinsic angular momentum, and the total angular momentum J of a particle with spin

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 1.2, printed pages 6-9 (properties of the orbital angular momentum operators) and Section 2, printed pages 11-18 (the algebraic theory of angular momentum and its multiplets)

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 4.1-4.1.2, printed pages 96-103 (PDF pages 99-106): angular momentum as the generator of rotations, its algebra and the l,m quantum numbers

items.title: Effective magnetic-moment coupling of the finite-spin model: gyromagnetic parameter, magnetic moment and Zeeman energy operator
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, for the declared massive
spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the
scope stated below, the following **effective magnetic-moment coupling**
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

**(i) Gyromagnetic parameter and magnetic moment.** For the declared spin
label $s$ assign a real **gyromagnetic parameter** $\gamma_{s}$, with unit
$\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, and define the **magnetic moment** of the model as
the internal-factor operator
$$\boldsymbol\mu:=\gamma_{s}\mathbf S=(\gamma_{s}S_{1},\gamma_{s}S_{2},\gamma_{s}S_{3}),$$
with unit $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$. Here $\mathbf S=(S_{1},S_{2},S_{3})$ are the
spin operators of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] read on
the internal factor as in
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c). The
parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is an empirical model parameter of the species: it is
part of the declared model data, with uncertainty, and it is not derived from
$s$, from the mass parameter $m$ or from the charge of the particle; no
relation between $\gamma_{s}$ and any other species parameter is asserted by
this postulate.

**(ii) Prescribed field and Zeeman energy operator.** Let
$\mathbf B:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a real bounded measurable
vector field, the **prescribed magnetic field profile**, with components
$B_{i}$ in tesla, entering the model as externally prescribed data
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]); in the
declared inertial frame the model adopts the **Zeeman energy operator**
$$H_{Z}:=H_{0}+M_{W},\qquad H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad M_{W}f:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\gamma_{s}B_{i}(\cdot)\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)(\cdot),$$
on the componentwise domain
$D(H_{Z}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, the domain of $H_{0}$
(componentwise, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]];
$\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ is the componentwise free operator with that domain by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied to each component). The added term $M_{W}$ is bounded with
$\|M_{W}\|\le|\gamma_{s}|\sum_{i}\|B_{i}\|_{\infty}\max_{i}\|S_{i}\|$;
its matrix value is Hermitian almost everywhere since $B_i$ and
$\gamma_s$ are real and each finite spin matrix is self-adjoint. Integrating
the fibrewise inner-product identity gives $M_W^*=M_W$ on $H_s$.
For completeness, if $y\in D((H_0+M_W)^*)$ and $z=(H_0+M_W)^*y$, then
$\langle H_0x,y\rangle=\langle x,z-M_Wy\rangle$ for every $x\in D(H_0)$.
Self-adjointness of $H_0$ gives $y\in D(H_0)$ and $H_0y=z-M_Wy$;
the reverse adjoint inclusion follows from symmetry. Thus $H_Z=H_Z^*$
on the unchanged domain
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), with unit
joule, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is
a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group read in the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The profile
$\mathbf B$ is a model input; the items of this page assert neither the
Maxwell equations nor a source or boundary realization of $\mathbf B$, and
the boundedness of $\mathbf B$ is an explicit hypothesis, not a general
property of magnetic fields.

**(iii) What is assumed and what is not.** (a) The coupling
$-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B(Q)$ is an **effective interaction**: it is
adopted, not derived from the spin representation P6, from the
minimal-coupling postulate P5a of the framework or from classical
electromagnetism. (b) No value of $\gamma_{s}$ and no comparison with
measured gyromagnetic ratios or $g$-factors is made here. (c) No spin-orbit
coupling, no fine or hyperfine structure, no relativistic correction and no
radiation reaction is included. (d) A time-dependent field profile requires
its own domain and evolution hypotheses and is outside this postulate. (e)
The internal factor is not a spatial current distribution and $\boldsymbol\mu$
is not asserted to arise from a rotating charge distribution.

(iv) **Status.** This postulate is an adopted model assumption with the
physical scope above; it is motivated by and formulated after the cited
sources, which treat the coupling as a model input, and no deduction of it
from the framework's other postulates is claimed.
items.physical_scope: The effective magnetic-moment coupling of the framework's massive spin-s particle model in a declared inertial frame, for a prescribed real bounded measurable magnetic field profile and a declared real gyromagnetic parameter gamma_s: the magnetic moment mu = gamma_s S with unit J T^-1, the Zeeman energy operator H_Z on the domain of the free operator, its units and the autonomous unitary evolution assigned to it by P4, and the status of gamma_s and of the static field profile as empirical or externally prescribed model inputs. The item asserts no Maxwell equation, no source model, no derivation of gamma_s from charge and mass, no spin-orbit or relativistic correction, no time-dependent or open-system dynamics and no measured value; it is a model assumption adopted on this page only.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.4, printed pages 158-169 (PDF pages 166-177): spin angular momentum, the magnetic moment of a spin-half particle, the Stern-Gerlach coupling and magnetic precession

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin One-Half, Bras, Kets, and Operators', Section 1, printed pages 1-7 (the magnetic dipole in a nonuniform magnetic field and the two-peak Stern-Gerlach idealization) and Section 4, printed pages 16-19 (the spin operator in an arbitrary direction and its two eigenvalues)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 2-3, chapter pages 2-6 (spin precession in a uniform magnetic field and the precession frequency)

items.title: Spin spectra and outcome laws of the massive spin-s model: directional components, the Casimir law and the spin-half probabilities
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume
the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the
outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a
unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint
matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. For every unit $n$, read
$(S_{n},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable under P2. Put
$S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ and, for its outcome-law claim in
(b), read $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ as an assigned sharp observable
under P2. Then:

(a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum
$\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each
$m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the
fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix
$n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$,
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$
and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$;

(b) the Casimir operator $S^{2}$ equals $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as a bounded
operator, so for every preparation $\rho$ the law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ is the Dirac law at
$\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, and one has the
commutation relations
$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and
$[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$ on $H_{s}$, componentwise on the internal factor;

(c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has
$$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$
where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular,
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and
each number lies in $[0,1]$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and
P6, the sharp-observable assignments stated above and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal
factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no
measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components,
no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements
do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement,
and they contain no comparison with data.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state, observable and kinematics postulates P1, P2, P5 and of the internal spin assignment P6 for the massive spin-s model: the spectra and Born outcome laws of the explicitly assigned directional spin observables n·S, the assigned squared-spin observable with operator S^2 = hbar^2 s(s+1) I and, for s = 1/2, the explicit spin-up/spin-down probabilities. The item concerns the internal factor only; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measured spin value and no empirical identification of the operators.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 7.1 and 7.4, printed pages 139-145 and 158-168 (PDF pages 147-153 and 166-176): the angular momentum multiplets with j(j+1), the spin-half Pauli matrices and the magnetic quantum numbers

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin One-Half, Bras, Kets, and Operators', Sections 2-4, printed pages 7-19: the directional spin operator, its eigenvalues and the spin-up/spin-down probabilities; Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Sections 1-2, printed pages 1-18: the algebraic spectrum j, j-1, ..., -j

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 4.1-4.1.2, printed pages 96-103 (PDF pages 99-106): the angular momentum operators, their commutation relations and the spherical-harmonic eigenvalues

items.title: Orbital angular momentum eigenstates of the massive model: spherical harmonics, the l,m quantum numbers and the Casimir value
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $l\ge0$, $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$, a unit vector
$w\in\mathbb C^{r}$ and a complex-valued $R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$, and
let $h_{lm}$ be the harmonic homogeneous polynomial of degree $l$ with
$h_{lm}|_{S^2}=Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c)
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]). Define
the model vector
$$\psi(x):=R(|x|)\,h_{lm}(x)\,w\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ x\ne0),\qquad \psi(0):=0 .$$
Then:

(a) $\psi$ is a well-defined class in the model's state space $H_{s}$ and in
fact $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal
S^{(r)}$; it lies in $D(L_{i})$ for each $i$, and for $x\ne0$
$$(L_{i}\psi)(x)=R(|x|)\,\bigl(-i\hbar\,D_{i}h_{lm}\bigr)(x)\,w,\qquad D_{i}h_{lm}=(x\times\nabla h_{lm})_{i},$$
so that $-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm}$ is the polynomial representative of the sphere
function $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]]; in particular
$L_{3}\psi=\hbar m\,\psi$;

(b) with $\|R\|_{l}^{2}:=\int_{0}^{\infty}|R(r)|^{2}r^{2l+2}\,dr$ one has
$\|\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}$ and
$$\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}\,\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{3}\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)\,\|\psi\|^{2},$$
so the Casimir quadratic form of the model's orbital generators on $\psi$
takes the value $\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$;

(c) consequently, for the pure preparation of the unit vector
$\psi/\|\psi\|$ (for $R\not\equiv0$), the mean and the second moment of the
outcome law of $(L_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ are finite and equal
$\hbar m$ and $\hbar^{2}m^{2}$, so the variance vanishes; for each $i$ the
mean and second moment of the law of $L_{i}$ are finite and the second moment
equals $\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}$; the model reads $(l,m)$
as the **orbital angular momentum quantum numbers** of the preparation, in
the sense of the eigenvalue of the angular momentum-squared form and the
eigenvalue of $L_{3}$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited mathematics, and concern the spatial factor of the massive
model. The item asserts no dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no
joint sharp values of two different components $L_{i},L_{j}$, no empirical
value and no spectral resolution of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$: the identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$ is a quadratic-form statement on the
displayed smooth vectors and is not read as a statement about a self-adjoint
operator $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on the full spatial Hilbert space.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6 for the massive spin-s model and its orbital generators: for a smooth compactly supported radial profile times a spherical harmonic, the model vector is an eigenvector of the third orbital generator with eigenvalue hbar m, the Casimir quadratic form takes the value hbar^2 l(l+1), and the orbital quantum numbers are those of the spherical harmonic family. The statement concerns the spatial factor only, uses no dynamics and no measurement model, and asserts no spectral decomposition of the full spatial Hilbert space, no hydrogen spectrum and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.2, printed pages 145-154 (PDF pages 153-162): spherical harmonics as angular momentum eigenfunctions with quantum numbers l and m and the eigenvalue l(l+1) of the Casimir

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 4.1-4.1.2, printed pages 96-103 (PDF pages 99-106): orbital angular momentum, the commutators, the l,m quantum numbers and the l = 0 exceptions

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 1, printed pages 1-11: orbital angular momentum and the spherical harmonic eigenvalues in the radial problem

items.title: Conservation of total angular momentum for a spin-independent rotation-invariant bounded-potential dynamics
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) and the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable with
$V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the model's spin-independent bounded-potential energy operator on
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with flow
$U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$ in the reading of P4, and let
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ be the total angular momenta of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(d). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the lifted coordinate rotation family
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c) is a
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries of the declared
dynamics: $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))\,U(u)=U(u)\,U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ for all $t,u$ and
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$;

(b) each $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable of
the model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
and for a unit vector $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$ the mean and
the second moment of the law of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the pure
preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero
values $\langle J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) in the same situation each spin component $S_{i}$ and each orbital
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable in the same sense,
the laws of $S_{i}$ and $L_{i}$ being time-independent in every preparation;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
cited results, and concerns the declared isolated model with a real bounded
measurable potential invariant under every spatial rotation. It asserts no
symmetry of any concrete external field or apparatus, excludes spin-dependent,
singular and unbounded potentials (which require their own domain and symmetry
arguments), introduces no measurement, detector or empirical record, and
makes no claim that a definite numerical value of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is
revealed at each time: the conserved object is the outcome law.

The lifted rotations use the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ fixed in [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]]; its coordinate subgroups satisfy $\rho(A_i(t))=R_i(t)$, so the total generators retain the stated signs and axes.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 for the declared isolated massive spin-s model with a real bounded measurable spin-independent potential invariant under every spatial rotation: the lifted coordinate rotation subgroups are one-parameter symmetry groups, and each total angular momentum component is a conserved assigned sharp observable whose outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, with conserved mean and second moment on D(L_i). The item asserts no symmetry of any concrete system, no spin-dependent or singular potential, no measurement procedure and no empirical result.

items.title: Spin precession and the Zeeman splitting in a uniform magnetic field: Larmor angular frequency and the conservation of one component
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling
adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant
$B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile
$\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the
postulate is
$$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$
with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put
$\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle
S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then:

(a) $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})$ and
$$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
so in particular the transverse means satisfy, for every $t$,
$$\langle S_{1}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0)+\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0),\qquad \langle S_{2}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)-\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),$$
and the transverse vector $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(t),\langle S_{2}\rangle(t)\bigr)$
is the rotation of $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)\bigr)$
by the angle $-\omega t$ in the $(1,2)$-plane;

(b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$
and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$
and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent
in every preparation;

(c) the conjugation identities
$$e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2},\qquad e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$$
hold as bounded operator identities, and with $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$
(the Casimir operator of the model) also $S^{2}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S^{2}$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling; it concerns the uniform static field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$
with $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the declared isolated model. It excludes
inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, spin-dependent spatial potentials,
radiation, relaxation and environment coupling, asserts no measured
precession frequency and no measured gyromagnetic parameter, and identifies
no apparatus: $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ is a model quantity computed from
assigned model parameters.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling, for a uniform static magnetic field along the third axis of a declared inertial frame: self-adjointness and factorization of the Zeeman energy operator, conservation of the spin component along the field, and Larmor precession of the transverse spin expectations with angular frequency gamma_s B_z. The item concerns the declared model only; it excludes inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, radiation and relaxation, asserts no measured precession frequency or gyromagnetic ratio, and identifies no apparatus.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 7.4, printed pages 168-169 (PDF pages 176-177): magnetic precession of a spin in a uniform field and the Larmor frequency

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 1-3, chapter pages 1-6 (PDF pages 1-6 of 22): spin precession in a uniform magnetic field and the precession angular frequency

items.title: The conditional Stern-Gerlach force prediction of the spin-half Zeeman model: transverse momentum rate in a smooth bounded gradient field
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s=\tfrac12$, together with the effective
magnetic-moment coupling of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with parameter
$\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$ and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ be real with
$B_{z}$ and $B_{z}'$ bounded, let
$$\mathbf B(x):=\bigl(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1})\bigr),$$
let $H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the magnetic-moment postulate for this
profile, acting on $H_{1/2}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ with domain
$D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$, and let $u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$
be its flow. Identify $H_{1/2}$ with
$\mathcal H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\oplus L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
through the internal basis $(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, and let $P_{+}:=\tfrac12(I+2S_{3}/\hbar)$
be the fibrewise orthogonal projection onto the spin-up line $e_{1/2}$.
Then:

(a) under this identification $H_{Z}$ is the operator
$$K(u_{+},u_{-})=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{+}-\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},\ \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{-}+\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-}\Bigr),\qquad D(K)=W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2},$$
of [[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditional-stern-gerlach-force]] with
$\gamma_{s}:=\gamma_{1/2}$; consequently $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint,
$S_{3}H_{Z}=H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$, the sector weights
$\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are
independent of $t$;

(b) if in addition $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ is a unit vector with
$P_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ and $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}$ in a Borel set
$N\subseteq\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus N}\eta_{+}(x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0$, where
$\eta_{+}(x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|u_{0}^{+}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$
is the first-coordinate marginal density of the spin-up component, then
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigr|_{t=0}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle=\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}\,G ;$$
for $t\ne0$ the general rate is
$\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{1/2}\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$;

(c) the profile satisfies $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point of
$\mathbb R^{3}$, as identities of the displayed components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling. Clause (b) is a model prediction for the rate of the mean
transverse momentum of a prepared spin-up state under the marginal-support
hypothesis; it is not an observation of a beam splitting, a trajectory or a
count, it identifies no apparatus, calibration or detector, and it asserts
neither a source-free realization of $\mathbf B$ nor a Maxwell solution.
The word "Stern-Gerlach" names this conditional model, not a reported
experiment; no measured value of $\gamma_{1/2}$ enters and no empirical
conclusion is drawn.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling for the spin-half model in a static field profile B = (0,0,B_z(x_1)) whose component B_z is C^1 with bounded value and derivative: the identification of the model's Zeeman operator with the smooth bounded-coefficient force model, conservation of the field-aligned spin component and of the sector weights, the conditional rate gamma_s hbar G/2 of the transverse mean momentum in the spin-up sector when the gradient equals G on the support of the transverse marginal, and the divergence-free, curl identity of the profile. The item asserts no apparatus, no measured trajectory, no beam splitting observation and no source-free field realization; it is a model prediction conditional on its stated preparation assumptions.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin One-Half, Bras, Kets, and Operators', Section 1, printed pages 1-7 (the force on a magnetic dipole in a nonuniform magnetic field and the Stern-Gerlach two-peak idealization) and Section 4, printed pages 16-19 (spin states in an arbitrary direction)

items.title: Composition of two spin labels: total spin operators, the Clebsch-Gordan block decomposition and the spin-half singlet
items.statement:
Adopt the composition postulate P1 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6 in the readings of
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] and
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix two declared
spin labels $s,t\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with internal factors
$V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$, $V_{t}=\mathbb C^{2t+1}$ and spin matrices
$J^{(s)}_{i}$, $J^{(t)}_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], and consider the
composite internal factor $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$. On this composite, explicitly
adopt the diagonal internal rotation assignment
$D_{s,t}(W):=D_s(W)\otimes D_t(W)$ for $W\in SU(2)$, where each $D_s,D_t$
is the representation assigned by P6 clause (ii). This two-factor action
is a local composite model assignment, not an additional conclusion of P6.
Put
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=\hbar\bigl(J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}\bigr),\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\bigl(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\bigr)^{2},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}:=S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3}.$$
Write $S^{(s)}_i:=\hbar J^{(s)}_i$ and
$S^{(s)2}:=\sum_i(S^{(s)}_i)^2$, and similarly for $t$; define
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_\pm:=S^{\mathrm{tot}}_1\pm iS^{\mathrm{tot}}_2$.
Then:

(a) each $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ satisfying
$[S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{k}$,
$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ is self-adjoint and commutes with every
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$, and
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=S^{(s)2}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes S^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{3}S^{(s)}_{i}\otimes S^{(t)}_{i};$$

(b) there is an orthogonal decomposition
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ into
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}$-invariant subspaces with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$, on each of
which the triple $(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3})$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$j$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] scaled by $\hbar$; in
particular $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}j(j+1)I$ on $W_{j}$, each $j$ occurs
exactly once, and there is an orthonormal basis $(v_{j,k})$,
$0\le k\le2j$, of $W_{j}$ with
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}v_{j,k}=\hbar(j-k)v_{j,k},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{k(2j-k+1)}\,v_{j,k-1},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{(k+1)(2j-k)}\,v_{j,k+1};$$
the coefficients of the $v_{j,k}$ in the product basis $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})$
are the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and are determined by the phase of the
top vector $u_{j}$ (a unit vector of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-weight $\hbar j$
orthogonal to all $W_{j'}$ with $j'>j$), with $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_{s}\otimes e^{(t)}_{t}$
admissible;

(c) for every $M$ the $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenspace with weight $\hbar M$
has dimension $N(M)=\#\{m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}:M-m\in\{-t,\dots,t\}\}$, and the
identity $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})_{m,n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenvectors with weights
$\hbar(m+n)$;

(d) for $s=t=\tfrac12$ one has $V_{1/2}\otimes V_{1/2}=W_{0}\oplus W_{1}$ with
$\dim W_{0}=1$ and $\dim W_{1}=3$; the vector
$$\Psi:=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}-e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\bigr)$$
is a unit vector with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for every $i$, and it is
the unique unit vector in the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ up to a phase;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the internal factors of a declared
composite, the assignments of P1 and P6 and the declared diagonal
two-factor action. It asserts no spatial
two-particle model, no statistics or permutation symmetry, no interaction, no
dynamics, no measurement and no empirical correlation; in particular it does
not by itself imply the singlet correlations of a separated pair, which
belong to the composites page.
items.physical_scope: The internal-factor reading of the composition of two declared spin labels s and t under the composition postulate P1, the spin assignment P6 and the locally adopted diagonal two-factor rotation action: the total spin operators on the tensor product of the two internal factors, their commutation relations and Casimir, the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition into total-spin blocks with multiplicities, and the explicit spin-half singlet. The item concerns the internal factors only; the full two-particle spatial model, statistics, interactions and any measured correlation belong to the composites pages and are not asserted here.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 10 'Addition of Angular Momentum', Sections 1-2, printed pages 1-7: tensor-lifted addition of angular momenta and the spin-half triplet and singlet

items.title: What the angular momentum and spin page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
## Scope and empirical status

- **Adopted assumptions.** This page adopts P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the
  readings of the framework and the spin assignment P6 of
  [[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)
  ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
  [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The
  effective magnetic-moment coupling with its gyromagnetic parameter
  $\gamma_{s}$ and bounded field profile is the additional model assumption
  [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]]; like the spin
  label, mass and charge, the parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is a species parameter
  with uncertainty and is not derived on this page.

- **What is proved.** The local mathematics
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] supplies the
  bounded-perturbation flow and the lifted SU(2) rotation action with its
  coordinate generators, and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]] identifies the
  orbital Casimir on the harmonic blocks. On that basis:
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] gives the
  spectra and Born laws of the spin components;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigenstates-and-quantum-numbers]]
  describes the orbital eigenstates with the quantum numbers $l,m$ and the
  Casimir value; [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-total-conservation]] proves the
  conservation of the total angular momentum for a spin-independent
  rotation-invariant bounded-potential dynamics;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] gives the Larmor
  precession of the transverse spin expectations and the conservation of the
  field component in a uniform static field;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] supplies the
  internal-factor composition with the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition and the
  spin-half singlet; and
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]] transfers
  the conditional smooth-field force identity to the model.

- **What is not claimed.** No result of this page derives any value of
  $\gamma_{s}$, $s$, $m$, $g$-factor or $\hbar$; no spin-orbit, fine or
  hyperfine structure, relativistic spinor, anomaly or radiative correction
  is included; no spin-statistics theorem is asserted; no atomic, molecular
  or solid-state model is constructed; and no statement about the
  compositeness or internal structure of any particle is made. The internal
  factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping device, not a rotating body.

- **Experiments.** This page contains no experiment item: it records no
  apparatus, calibration, sampling, count or uncertainty. The historical
  Stern-Gerlach setup appears only as the name of the conditional model of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]], whose
  clause (b) is a prediction of the model conditional on an explicit
  preparation hypothesis. Identifying the operators and parameters of this
  page with a laboratory preparation and apparatus is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under
  [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the measurement
  statistics of sequential spin filters are treated on the measurement pages
  of the category, and agreement or disagreement with data there constrains
  the combined model and apparatus assumptions without proving them.

- **Consumers.** Composites, Bell and identical-particle pages of the
  category consume the internal-factor results of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] and the lifted rotation
  action of [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]];
  their empirical qualifications are added on those pages and are not
  inherited as certainty from this one.
items.physical_scope: The scope and empirical status of the angular momentum and spin page: which postulates are adopted, which conditional results are proved, which empirical parameters remain input data with uncertainty, and which laboratory, relativistic and interaction structures are excluded. The remark asserts no model fact, no measurement and no empirical conclusion.

items.title: Spin-half outcome probabilities along an arbitrary direction: the Bloch parametrization and worked cases
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Fix a unit vector
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and a unit internal spinor
$v=(v_{1},v_{2})\in\mathbb C^{2}$, and put
$$\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}:=\bigl(2\operatorname{Re}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}),\ -2\operatorname{Im}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}),\ |v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $\psi:=f\otimes v\in H_{1/2}$ and let $S_{n}=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$ be the
directional spin of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]]. Then:

(i) $\psi$ is a unit vector, $|\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}|=1$, and
for every unit $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1+n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}}{2},\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1-n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}}{2};$$

(ii) for the parametrization
$v=\bigl(e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2),\ \sin(\theta/2)\bigr)$ with
$\theta\in[0,\pi]$ and $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ -\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$,
and for the coordinate directions
$$\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},\ \sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad \mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr)=\frac{1\pm\sin\theta\cos\varphi}{2};$$

(iii) for the basis state $v=e_{1/2}$ (the case $\theta=0$) the component
$S_{3}$ has the laws $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and
$\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$, while
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12$ for both signs; and for
$v=(e_{1/2}+e_{-1/2})/\sqrt2$ the component $S_{1}$ has
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and
$\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$.

All quantities are model probabilities for the pure preparation $[\psi]$; no
measurement procedure, apparatus, calibration or empirical frequency is
asserted, and the example makes no claim that a laboratory device realizes
the observable $S_{n}$.
items.physical_scope: An exact computation inside the massive spin-half model of the framework: the Bloch parametrization of a unit internal spinor, the Born probabilities of the directional spin component n·S, and worked cases including the coordinate directions and the state e_{1/2}. The example uses the model's own outcome law; it involves no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measurement record and no empirical value.
