items.title: The two spin-half fermion sector: the spin-singlet and spin-triplet parts and their orbital symmetry
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the
readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Declare a
**spin-half fermionic species** with an arbitrary model-assigned mass parameter
$M_{\mathrm{sp}}>0\,\mathrm{kg}$, unused in this calculation and not assigned an
empirical value here, whose one-particle space is the completed
product $K\widehat\otimes V$ of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert
space $K$ (the orbital factor) with $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ (the internal factor of
P6 clause (ii) for $s=\tfrac12$), with $V$ carrying the orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$ of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]], and
declare $n=2$ particles in the adopted antisymmetric sector
$$\mathfrak H_2^-=\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\subseteq (K\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(K\otimes V)$$
of the declared species, with the regrouping unitary $\Theta$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]. Write
$u\wedge v:=\sqrt2\,P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ and
$u\odot v:=\sqrt2\,P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)$ for $u,v\in K$, and
$\sigma_\pm:=(e_+\otimes e_-\pm e_-\otimes e_+)/\sqrt2$ for the spin
combinations. Then, as conditional statements of the declared model:

(a) *sector decomposition*: $\Theta$ carries $\mathfrak H_2^-$ onto the
orthogonal direct sum $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$,
where $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}=\mathbb C\Psi$ is the one-dimensional
spin-singlet line spanned by the singlet $\Psi$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] clause (d) and
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}=W_{1}$ is the three-dimensional spin-triplet
space of that theorem; consequently the antisymmetric two-particle sector is
the sum of a **spin-singlet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(K)}\otimes\mathbb C\Psi$,
of dimension $\binom{m+1}2$ for $m=\dim K$, with symmetric orbital factor,
and a **spin-triplet part** $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K)}\otimes W_1$, of
dimension $3\binom m2$, with antisymmetric orbital factor;

(b) *opposite orbital symmetry*: for all $u,v\in K$ and $\chi,\chi'\in V$,
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr) =P_+^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi') +P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi');$$
the spin-singlet component therefore multiplies the symmetric orbital
component and the spin-triplet component multiplies the antisymmetric orbital
component, so within each component the orbital exchange symmetry is opposite
to the spin exchange symmetry;

(c) *parallel spins*: if $u,v\in K$ are orthonormal and $\chi\in V$ is a unit
vector, then $\Theta$ carries the ray of
$P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi)\bigr)$ to the ray
of $P_-^{(K)}(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$, whose unit representative
is $(u\wedge v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi)$; for $\chi=e_+$ this is the
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z=\hbar$ triplet component with an antisymmetric orbital
factor;

(d) *antiparallel spins*: if $u,v\in K$ are orthonormal, then $\Theta$ carries
the ray of $P_-^{(K\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes e_+)\otimes(v\otimes e_-)\bigr)$
to the ray of $\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl((u\odot v)\otimes\sigma_-
+(u\wedge v)\otimes\sigma_+\bigr)$, an equal-amplitude superposition of the
singlet component with symmetric orbital factor and the $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_z=0$
triplet component with antisymmetric orbital factor; in particular such an
antisymmetrised product of two orthonormal one-particle states has no definite
orbital exchange symmetry.

The model assignment of the antisymmetric sector is that of P6; the statements
above are conditional on it and assert no spin-statistics theorem, no
interaction, no dynamics and no measurement.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 10.1.2 printed pages 229-230 (PDF pages 237-238): for a pair of spin-half particles, the spin-triplet states have antisymmetric spatial wavefunctions and the spin-singlet state a symmetric one

D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 7 'Identical Particles', pp. 4-10: exchange symmetry, spin, and the symmetric and antisymmetric decomposition of a two-particle state; Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/dbs26/PQM/chap7.pdf

items.physical_scope: The conditional model computation for two declared spin-half fermions with a finite orbital factor: the decomposition of the antisymmetric sector into spin-singlet and spin-triplet parts, the opposite orbital symmetry in each part, and the explicit components of an antisymmetrised product of two declared one-particle states. The computation is conditional on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6 and on the declared finite orbital factor; it asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no interaction, no dynamics, no measurement and no empirical claim.

items.title: Exchange versus direct Coulomb terms: the pair-energy split of the two-orbital spin-half model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the identical-particle and spin
postulate P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare the following
**two-orbital spin-half model**:

(a) the species is a spin-half fermion with an arbitrary model-assigned mass
parameter $M_{\mathrm{sp}}>0\,\mathrm{kg}$, unused in this computation and
with no empirical value asserted; its orbital factor is
$K:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{u,v\}$ where
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\cap L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
are real-valued, normalized and orthogonal in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), with $uv\ne0$ in $L^{1}$; the internal factor is $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ with basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; the one-particle space is $K\widehat\otimes V$ and $n=2$
particles are declared in the antisymmetric sector
$\mathfrak H_2^-=\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(K\otimes V)}$
([[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]);

(b) write $E:=K\widehat\otimes K$ and let $J:E\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the restriction of the Euclidean product unitary $\Theta_6$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), so $J(a\otimes b)(x,y)=a(x)b(y)$. Here $L^2(\mathbb R^r)$ consists of almost-everywhere classes $[f]$ of complex Lebesgue-measurable functions with $\int_{\mathbb R^r}|f|^2\,dx<\infty$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). In SI units, let $x,y\in\mathbb R^3$ be spatial coordinates measured in metres and define $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ by $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$ for $z\ne0$ and $W(0)=0$. The value at zero is an arbitrary representative on a measure-zero set. Here $\kappa>0$ is an adopted parameter of unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$, with no relation to a charge assumed, so $W$ has unit $\mathrm J$. Define the multiplication operator
$$M_W:D(M_W)\subseteq L^2(\mathbb R^6)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6),\qquad D(M_W):=\{[g]\in L^2(\mathbb R^6):[(x,y)\mapsto W(x-y)g(x,y)]\in L^2(\mathbb R^6)\},\qquad M_W[g]:=[(x,y)\mapsto W(x-y)g(x,y)]$$
where $g$ is any representative. This is independent of the representative because $W$ is finite and measurable everywhere. The declared pair interaction is the compression of this multiplier to $E$: for $z,z'\in E$, set
$$q(z,z'):=\int_{\mathbb R^6}W(x-y)(Jz)(x,y)\overline{(Jz')(x,y)}\,dx\,dy.$$
The normalized position-space orbitals have units $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, and
$D$, $X$ and the pair-interaction expectations below have units $\mathrm J$.
All $Jz$ lie in $D(M_W)$, as verified below.
For the orthonormal basis $(b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4):=(u\otimes u,u\otimes v,v\otimes u,v\otimes v)$ of $E$, define
$$Az:=\sum_{j=1}^4q(z,b_j)b_j.$$
Thus $\langle Az,z'\rangle=q(z,z')$; $A$ is a bounded self-adjoint pair-energy operator on $E$, has units $\mathrm J$, and has real matrix entries in this basis. It commutes with spatial exchange. The model's sector interaction is the restriction to $\mathfrak H_2^-$ of $\Theta^{-1}(A\otimes I_{V\otimes V})\Theta$, with $\Theta$ the finite-dimensional regrouping unitary of the symmetry-decomposition theorem. This restriction is well defined because the conjugated operator commutes with total exchange. On a factored preparation with unit $\chi$ its expectation is $q(\varphi,\varphi)=\langle M_WJ\varphi,J\varphi\rangle$;

(c) the declared pair preparations are the images under the inverse regrouping
map of the symmetry-decomposition theorem
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]) of the
factored vectors
$$\Psi_{T}:=\Theta^{-1}\bigl(\varphi_-\otimes(e_+\otimes e_+)\bigr),\qquad \Psi_{S}:=\Theta^{-1}\bigl(\varphi_+\otimes\sigma_-\bigr),\qquad \varphi_\pm:=\frac{u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u}{\sqrt2},\quad \sigma_-:=\frac{e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+}{\sqrt2},$$
which are unit vectors of $\mathfrak H_2^-$ by the cited thought experiment.
$\Psi_{T}$ is the parallel-spin (spin-triplet) preparation and $\Psi_{S}$ the
spin-singlet preparation of the declared two-orbital model.

The example computes the declared pair-interaction expectations
$q(\varphi_\pm,\varphi_\pm)$ of the two preparations and shows
that the exchange integral $X$ separates them strictly.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 10 printed pages 227-235 (PDF pages 235-243): the symmetric and antisymmetric pair states of helium and the direct and exchange contributions to the electron-repulsion expectation
F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.3 pp. 11-13: two-particle operators and their direct and exchange matrix elements

items.physical_scope: A conditional computation in the declared two-orbital model of two spin-half fermions, with real, normalized, orthogonal orbitals u,v in W^{1,2}(R^3) intersect L^2(R^3) whose product uv is nonzero in L^1, and the declared pair interaction W(x-y)=kappa/|x-y|. In SI, x,y are measured in metres, kappa>0 is an adopted parameter with unit J m, and the result is the pair expectations D+X and D-X in joules with X>0. The example asserts no atomic physics, no measured energy, no apparatus and no empirical result; the orbitals and interaction form are declared idealizations of the model.

items.title: Scope of the identical-particles examples page
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**What the computations establish.** Both items are conditional statements of
declared models. [[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]
decomposes the antisymmetric two-particle sector of a declared spin-half
species with a finite orbital factor into its spin-singlet and spin-triplet
parts, exhibits the opposite orbital exchange symmetry of the two parts, and
computes the components of an antisymmetrised product of two declared
one-particle states. [[ex-nrqm-identical-particles-exchange-versus-coulomb-terms]]
specialises a two-orbital model with a declared Coulomb-form interaction and
shows, for real normalized orthogonal $W^{1,2}$ orbitals with a nonzero
product, that the declared parallel-spin (triplet)
preparation has strictly smaller pair-interaction expectation than the singlet
preparation, the difference being twice the exchange integral.

**What they rest on.** Both rest on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the assignment of the species to the antisymmetric sector and the choice of
orbital factor are model declarations, and in the second item the two orbitals
and the interaction form are declared idealizations. The spin-statistics
association is not derived, no interaction is derived from the sector and no
dynamics is introduced.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no measured energy, no count and no
apparatus response; the terms "singlet", "triplet" and "exchange" name
components and differences of the declared models. Whether a laboratory pair
of particles is described by one of the declared preparations is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], and agreement of these
conditional numbers with data would test the combined model and apparatus
assumptions rather than prove the model.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 10 printed pages 227-235 (PDF pages 235-243): the symmetry of pair states and the direct and exchange contributions in the helium discussion

D. Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 7 'Identical Particles', pp. 4-10: symmetric and antisymmetric spatial and spin parts of two-particle states; Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/dbs26/PQM/chap7.pdf

items.physical_scope: A scope remark for the examples page: it records what the two-fermion symmetry computation and the exchange-versus-Coulomb example establish in the declared models, which idealizations and model assignments they rest on, and what they do not claim about nature or about any measurement.

items.title: Moments of the exponential law on the half-line
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real
$\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda
r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and

$$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$

The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel
function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are
asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about
complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.4 pp. 229-235 (evaluation of the Laguerre normalisation integrals of the Coulomb eigenfunctions, which reduce to the moments of this lemma)
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §5.2 'Definitions' (the gamma function as an integral, and its values at positive integers: §5.2(i) and the recurrence of §5.5(i))

items.title: The three-dimensional free Schrödinger operator as the weak Laplacian on its Sobolev domain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let $H_{0}$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=3$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem.
Let $D^{2}_{j}$ denote the second weak partial derivative in the $j$-th
coordinate, defined componentwise on the locally integrable classes of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]),
write $\Delta_{w}:=D^{2}_{1}+D^{2}_{2}+D^{2}_{3}$ for the weak Laplacian
(defined on the classes whose three second weak partial derivatives lie in
$L^{2}$), and let $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_{0}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\Delta_{w}f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_{0});$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_{2}(H_{0}f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^{2}$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, the
operator $H_{0}+M_{V}$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain
$D(H_{0})$, coincides with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf$
on the same domain; in particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ the eigenvalue equation
$(H_{0}+M_{V})\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorem 7.8, printed page 168 (the free Schrödinger operator and its domain), and Section 10.1, printed pages 221-222 (the weak Laplacian of the hydrogen Hamiltonian)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.2, printed pages 104-105 (the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation with a central potential and its spherical Laplacian)

items.title: The declared central-potential model: state space, assigned energy operator, spherical reading and bound-state vocabulary
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared central-potential model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **central-potential model**. Its declared
state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of clause (a), with the
position and momentum families $Q_{j}$, $P_{k}$ of that clause
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). A **declared central
potential** of the model is a function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ of the
form $V(x):=v(|x|)$ for $x\ne0$, where $v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is real,
bounded and measurable and $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\|v\|_{\infty}=\sup_{r>0}|v(r)|$ is
finite; the assignment $V(0):=0$ is a declared convention that does not affect
the $L^{2}$ theory. The potential energy is read in joules. The model declares
the **Born position law** of the framework for a unit class $\psi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}),$$
the spin-zero reading of clause (b) of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]. The pair asserts no derivation
of a central force law from $H_{0}$ or from P5: the restriction to a declared
central potential is an assumption of the model, and an assignment of a
concrete material system to the model is an identification in the sense of
clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$. With $M_{V}$ the
bounded multiplication operator of clause (a) of the same theorem, the
**assigned energy operator** of the model with central potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. By clause (c) of the cited theorem
$H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{V})$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$\Delta_{w}=D_{1}^{2}+D_{2}^{2}+D_{3}^{2}$ the weak Laplacian of that lemma. If
$\psi\in D(H_{V})\setminus\{0\}$ and $E\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$H_{V}\psi=E\psi$, the time-independent equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ is an equality in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and hence in distributions; it is a partial
differential equation in the three spatial variables. If $V\in C^{2}(\Omega)$
on an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, then the class $\psi$ has a
representative in $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for every
$0<\alpha<1/2$, and the equation holds pointwise there. To justify this,
write $f:=(2m/\hbar^{2})(E-V)\psi$, so $-\Delta\psi=f$ in distributions.
On every relatively compact open subset of $\Omega$, the weak product rule
(obtained by local smooth mollification of the $C^{2}$ factor and passage to
the $L^{2}$ limit) gives, for every multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$,
$$D^{\beta}f=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}\sum_{\eta\le\beta}\binom{\beta}{\eta}D^{\eta}(E-V)D^{\beta-\eta}\psi\in L^{2};$$
the factors $D^{\eta}(E-V)$ are bounded on compact subsets and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3})$, so $f\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.
Integration by parts against compactly supported smooth test functions makes
$\psi\in H^{1}(\Omega)$ a local weak solution in the sense of
[[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]] for
$L=-D_i(\delta_{ij}D_j)=-\Delta$, whose divergence coefficients are
$a^{ij}=\delta_{ij}$ and $b^{i}=c=0$. They satisfy the uniform ellipticity
condition of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$\theta=1$ and have the required local coefficient derivatives of every
order. The interior regularity theorem
[[thm-interior-h-k-plus-two-elliptic-regularity]] with $k=2$ therefore gives
$\psi\in H^{4}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. Every ball compactly contained in
$\Omega$ is a bounded smooth domain and hence a $W^{4,2}$ extension domain by
[[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]. The higher-order Sobolev
embedding [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] with $n=3$, $k=4$, $p=2$
then gives a representative with continuous derivatives through order two and
locally Hölder-continuous second derivatives of every exponent
$0<\alpha<1/2$; this is the meaning of
$C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ here. These representatives agree on
overlaps because they are continuous and represent the same almost-everywhere
class. Both sides of the equation are then continuous and agree almost
everywhere, so they agree pointwise. The model adopts
$(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its declared energy observable; its self-adjointness is
the cited theorem's, and no further spectral property is presupposed here.

**(d) The declared spherical reading.** Let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from
$H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,\bar m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$, written
$U\psi=(u_{l\bar m})_{l\ge0,-l\le\bar m\le l}$, and let $(Y_{l\bar m})$ be the complete
orthonormal family of that theorem; $l,\bar m$ are integers, while $m>0$
continues to denote the mass. For a fixed $(l,\bar m)$, let
$\iota_{l\bar m}:L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)\to K$ insert its argument
in that coordinate and zero in every other coordinate, and define the
isometric **spherical lift** $J_{l\bar m}:=U^{-1}\iota_{l\bar m}$, so that
$$J_{l\bar m}u(x)=\frac{u(r)}{r}Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega,\ r>0).$$
The **spherical sector** $(l,\bar m)$ is the range of this lift. Its
**admissible reduced domain** is fixed by the assigned energy domain:
$$\mathcal D_{l\bar m}:=\{u\in L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C):J_{l\bar m}u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\}.$$
Thus every weak Cartesian derivative through order two of the lift must
belong to $L^{2}$ on all of $\mathbb R^{3}$, including neighbourhoods of the
origin. This condition and the global square integrability specify
admissibility at both endpoints; no independent half-line boundary parameter
is part of the model. In particular $C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)
\subseteq\mathcal D_{l\bar m}$ by clause (d) of the cited theorem. The
**effective potential** is
$$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r):=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\qquad(r>0),$$
whose second summand is called the **angular-momentum barrier**; both
summands, and $v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}$, are read in joules. For $E\in\mathbb R$,
the model's **declared radial equation** in the sector $(l,\bar m)$ is
$$u\in\mathcal D_{l\bar m},\qquad H_VJ_{l\bar m}u=EJ_{l\bar m}u\quad\text{in }L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
A **radial eigenpair** additionally requires $u\ne0$. The associated
one-dimensional differential expression is
$$u\longmapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u,\qquad u:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C,$$
where $u''$ means the distributional second derivative on $(0,\infty)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). The expression
alone, without the specified lifted domain, does not define a radial
eigenvalue problem. On $C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, its equation
with right-hand side $Eu$ is equivalent almost everywhere to the declared
radial equation above by the spherical-reduction theorem of this page;
pointwise equivalence additionally requires continuity of $v$. No full-domain
differential reduction or endpoint classification is presupposed here.
The angular-momentum quantum numbers $l$ and $\bar m$
appearing in the reading are labels of the orthonormal family $(Y_{l\bar m})$; the
identification of $l$ with a total angular momentum of a material system is a
separate assignment of the framework's angular-momentum items and is not made
here.

**(e) Stationary and bound-state vocabulary.** A **stationary vector** of the
model with potential $V$ and **energy** $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
vector with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalised, $\|\psi\|=1$; its
eigenvalue is its **binding energy**, read in joules, relative to the
chosen **energy reference** $0$. Here $E<0$ is a vocabulary convention;
no assertion that $0$ is a spectral continuum threshold follows for an
arbitrary bounded central potential. A continuum threshold requires a
separate spectral determination for the particular operator. In particular,
adding a constant potential shifts the free operator and its spectrum by
that constant without changing its eigenvectors. The model reads the energy
outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$
as the point mass $\delta_{E}$, the reading of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
position density of that preparation as $|\psi|^{2}$ by
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b), with $s=0$
and the state, position and choice hypotheses of (a). These are
declarations of the model under P2; they construct no sample, detector or
measured value, and they assert no stability, decay or formation claim.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
state space, position and momentum assignments, an assigned energy operator
for a real bounded measurable central potential, a declared spherical reading
with its effective potential and radial equation, and a stationary-state and
bound-state vocabulary. They adopt P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematics, and the additional central-potential model assumption and
spherical reading of clauses (b) and (d); in particular the central form of the
potential, the model's use of the full three-dimensional space as its state
space and the identification of the spherical sectors with angular-momentum
labels are declarations of the pair. The model excludes from its scope, until
their own items introduce them: the Coulomb potential $\propto-1/r$ and other
unbounded or singular potentials; spin and magnetic couplings; relativistic
corrections; finite nuclear size; the radiation extension, spontaneous
emission and radiation reaction; external electromagnetic fields; and any
many-body or shielding modification of a central potential. No numerical value
of $m$, $\hbar$ or of any potential is fixed here, and no empirical result is
asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.2, printed pages 104-110 (central potentials, the radial equation, the effective potential, the boundary condition at the origin and three-dimensional bound states) and Section 4.3, printed pages 111-114 (the hydrogen atom)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 182-189 (the gross-structure model of a hydrogen-like ion, the effective potential and the radial Hamiltonian)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.1 printed pages 221-222 (Schrödinger operators with singular potentials on H^2) and Section 10.2 printed pages 222-225 (spherical coordinates and separation)
J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations, Section 4.11, Theorem 4.28, printed page 114 (higher interior Sobolev regularity and the C^2 consequence when k>n/2)

items.physical_scope: The pair's declared central-potential model for one spinless massive particle: its state space, its position and momentum assignments, its assigned energy operator for a real bounded measurable central potential, its declared spherical angular-radial reading and effective potential, and its stationary-state, bound-state and energy-reference vocabulary. The model is an additional assumption of the pair, not a derivation from the three-dimensional massive-particle model P5; the Coulomb and other unbounded or singular potentials, spin, relativistic and radiative corrections, finite nuclear size and external fields are excluded and are introduced only by their own later items. No identification of a concrete material system with the model, no empirical value and no measured energy are asserted.

items.title: The declared central-potential model: spherical reduction of smooth compactly supported radial states
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared
central-potential model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=0$, a real bounded measurable central potential
$V(x)=v(|x|)$ and assigned energy operator $H_{V}$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $l\ge0$, $-l\le \bar m\le l$, let
$u\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, and define
$$\psi(x):=\frac{u(r)}{r}Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega,\ r=|x|>0),$$
with $(Y_{lm})$ the complete orthonormal family and $U$ the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]]. Then:

(a) $\psi$ lies in $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\})\subseteq
H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=D(H_{V})$, its image under $U$ is the
finite-support vector whose only potentially nonzero entry is the $(l,\bar m)$-entry $u$,
and $B\mapsto\int_B|\psi|^2dx$ is its position quadratic measure. For $u\not\equiv0$, the unit vector $\widehat\psi:=\psi/\|\psi\|$ represents its pure preparation and has position outcome law
$$\mu^G_{\widehat\psi}(B)=\|\psi\|^{-2}\int_B|\psi|^2dx;$$

(b) for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$,
$$H_{V}\psi(x)=\frac{1}{r}\Bigl[-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u(r)\Bigr]Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega),$$
the two sides being equal as $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ classes; thus
the model's assigned energy acts on the smooth spherical sector by the
declared radial differential expression with effective potential
$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r)=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}$;

(c) if $E\in\mathbb R$ and $u$ satisfies the declared radial equation
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u(r)=Eu(r)\qquad(0<r<\infty)$$
pointwise on $(0,\infty)$, then $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$, when $u\not\equiv0$, $\psi$ is a nonzero stationary vector of the model with energy $E$ and the pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, every assigned sharp observable having a time-independent outcome law in it. For $u=0$, only the linear identity $H_V0=E0$ is asserted and no pure preparation is assigned;

(d) for every $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, including $u=0$,
the radial equation
$$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}u^{\prime\prime}(r)+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^2l(l+1)}{2mr^2}\Bigr)u(r)=Eu(r)$$
holds for almost every $r>0$ if and only if $H_V\psi=E\psi$ as Hilbert-space vectors. If $v$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$, this radial equality is also equivalent to its pointwise version. For general measurable $v$, no pointwise converse is asserted.

The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared model; it
asserts no converse for general reduced functions, no completeness of any
family of radial solutions, no discrete spectrum, and no measured energy, and
it does not apply to the Coulomb potential, whose self-adjointness and spectral
theory are supplied separately.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.2, printed pages 104-110 (separation of the three-dimensional central-potential equation into radial and angular parts, the effective potential and the reduced radial equation (4.21))
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 183-185 (the radial Hamiltonian H_l and the effective potential V_eff(r) for a hydrogen-like ion)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.2, printed pages 222-225 (spherical coordinates and the separation of the Coulomb eigenvalue equation)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared central-potential model of this pair: a smooth reduced function u compactly supported away from the origin, transported to the three-dimensional vector psi = u(r)Y_lm(Omega)/r of the spherical sector (l,m), lies in the model's energy domain, and the model's assigned energy acts on psi by the declared radial differential expression with the effective potential v(r) + hbar^2 l(l+1)/(2 m r^2); consequently the radial equation holds almost everywhere exactly when the linear operator equation holds on that vector, including the zero vector. A nonzero reduced function alone defines a pure preparation, whose position law is normalized and which is stationary when the radial equation holds. The statement is an exact identity for the declared model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no converse for arbitrary reduced classes, no completeness of any family of radial solutions, no spectral classification, no measured energy and no empirical result, and it excludes the Coulomb potential from its hypotheses, which are treated by the following items of the page.

items.title: The declared Coulomb and two-body hydrogen model: one-centre operator, relative problem, reduced mass and scope exclusions
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data of clause (a) of the declared
central-potential model [[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]
with a declared mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, the state space
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the componentwise position and momentum
families and the action constant $\hbar>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared one-centre Coulomb model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix a real **coupling** $\kappa>0$ with the declared
unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and put
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{m^{-1}}),\qquad C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\ \text{ on }\ D(C_{\gamma})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
the self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] clause (c). The **assigned
energy operator** of the one-centre Coulomb model is
$$H_{\kappa}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,C_{\gamma},$$
with domain $D(H_{\kappa}):=D(C_{\gamma})$; by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a)
and (b) it is self-adjoint with the same domain, and by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] together with
the action formula of the cited theorem it acts by
$$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa\frac{f}{|\cdot|}\qquad(f\in D(H_{\kappa})),$$
where $\Delta_{w}$ is the weak Laplacian. The model declares the **length
scale** $a_{\kappa}:=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, read in metres, and the **energy
scale** $\mathcal E_{\kappa}:=m\kappa^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})=\hbar^{2}/(2ma_{\kappa}^{2})$,
read in joules. The model adopts $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ as its declared
energy observable for the one-centre problem; the self-adjointness is the
cited theorem's and no spectral property is presupposed here.

**(c) The declared radial reading of the one-centre model.** Let $U$ and
$(A_{l})_{l\ge0}$ be the unitary and the radial operators of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] clauses (a)-(d):
$U$ maps $H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$ with
$UH_{\kappa}U^{*}=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$, and each $A_{l}$ is self-adjoint
with form domain $V_{l}$ and domain $D(A_{l})$. The model declares the
**sector $(l,m)$ radial energy operator** $A_{l}^{(\kappa)}:=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$,
read in joules, and, for a class $u\in D(A_{l})$, the **declared radial
equation** is the distributional identity
$$-u''(r)+\Bigl(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}-\frac{\gamma}{r}\Bigr)u(r)=A_{l}u(r)\qquad\text{on }(0,\infty),$$
which by clause (c) of the cited theorem is an ordinary differential equation
with $C^{2}$ representative whenever $A_{l}u=\lambda u$ for a constant
$\lambda$ (unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$); its physical energy is
$E=(\hbar^{2}/2m)\lambda$ in joules. For an **inverse-length parameter**
$k>0$ (unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$), put $\lambda=-k^{2}$ and
$E(k):=-\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ (unit $\mathrm J$). The
**regular reduced solution** at this parameter is the function
$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$ of clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]], with $v$ the regular
power series of clause (b) and dimensionless argument $2kr$; the pair uses it as the declared radial template
of the model, not as a physical state, until the normalisation and spectral
theorems of the page identify it.

**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries charge $-q_{-}$ and particle 2 carries charge $+q_{+}$, where the
charge magnitudes $q_{-},q_{+}>0$ are read in coulombs. Declare the **pair
coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q_{-}q_{+}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ is a constitutive assumption of the
model, and $\kappa$ is read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$. Its equal-magnitude,
net-neutral submodel is $q_{-}=q_{+}=q>0$, with charges $-q,+q$ and
$\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$; this is the branch used by the later
relative-dipole consumers. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The energy operators $H_{2}$, $T_{R}$ and
$C_{\mu}$ are each read in joules. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

**(e) The hydrogen-like identification.** A **hydrogen-like ion** assignment of
the two-body model is the choice $m_{1}=m_{\mathrm e}$ (electron mass
parameter), $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm n}$ (nuclear mass parameter), $q_{-}=e$ (the
elementary charge of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) and $q_{+}=Ze$ (nuclear charge
magnitude), so that $\kappa=Ze^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ for a declared
positive integer $Z$. The **hydrogen assignment** is the specialization
$Z=1$, $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm p}$, for which $q_{-}=q_{+}=e$ and the pair is
net-neutral. These assignments use empirical mass and charge parameters; any
comparison of the model's consequences with a laboratory hydrogen atom is a
tested identification in the sense of clause (iii) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and carries the
uncertainty of that identification. The model declares no numerical value of
$m_{\mathrm e},m_{\mathrm n},e,\mu_{0}$ or $\hbar$; numerical evaluations, when
made, use their declared or measured values as explicitly qualified empirical
inputs.

**(f) Scope exclusions.** Until their own items introduce them, the Coulomb
and hydrogen models exclude: spin, magnetic moment couplings and
spin–statistics assignments beyond the trivial spin-zero factor; relativistic
corrections, in particular any fine-structure splitting of the degeneracy of
the gross-structure levels; finite nuclear size, nuclear recoil beyond the
two-body reduction of clause (d), and nuclear structure; QED corrections such
as vacuum polarisation and the Lamb shift, and hyperfine structure; shielding
and many-body modification of the $1/r$ potential; the radiation extension,
spontaneous emission, radiation reaction and any photon, transition-frequency
or line-intensity statement; external electromagnetic fields; and any
scattering, ionisation or continuum process, which belongs to the scattering
items of the quantum-mechanics track. The model asserts no empirical result
and fixes no measured quantity.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3, printed pages 111-117 (the hydrogen atom: the Coulomb potential -e^2/(4 pi eps_0 r), the radial equation and energy spectrum, the Bohr radius and the fine-structure exclusion) and Section 4.2.3, printed pages 110-111 (the boundary condition at the origin and self-adjointness)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 182-185 (equation (8.1) gives the pair potential -Ze^2/(4 pi epsilon_0 r) for charges -e,+Ze, and equations (8.3)-(8.10) give the centre-of-mass and relative coordinates, reduced mass and radial Hamiltonian)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.1 printed pages 221-222 (the Coulomb Hamiltonian -Delta - gamma/|x| as a self-adjoint operator on H^2) and Section 10.2 printed pages 222-225 (the one-particle reduction and separation)

items.physical_scope: The pair's declared Coulomb model, in a one-centre form for a spinless particle of declared mass and coupling in a fixed centre, and in a two-body form for two distinguishable spinless massive particles with charges -q_- and +q_+ and pair potential -kappa/|x1-x2|, where kappa is determined by the product q_-q_+; the equal-magnitude branch -q,+q is retained for the dipole consumers. It includes the declared centre-of-mass/relative decomposition with reduced mass mu, the hydrogen-like-ion identification for nuclear charge +Ze, and the model's scope exclusions. The item fixes model assumptions and readings of P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and P7 together with cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical identification, no measured constant, no transition, photon or line-intensity claim, and no spectral or scattering consequence, which are supplied by the theorems of the page or by later radiation and scattering items. Spin, relativistic and QED corrections, finite nuclear size, external fields, many-body and shielding effects and radiation reaction are excluded.

items.title: The one-centre Coulomb model: energy observable, flow, stationary states and spectral support
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared one-centre
Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ on $D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
assigned sharp-observable reading
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the flow and
preparation reading [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and
the spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model:
$H_{\kappa}$ is densely defined, self-adjoint and bounded below on
$D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, acts by
$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa f/|\cdot|$, and
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=[0,+\infty);$$
every point of $\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ is an eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity, isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of negative eigenvalues is
at most countable;

(b) *Flow.* The family $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is the model's
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{0}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure preparation
$[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and only if
$\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$; in that case, with eigenvalue $E$,
one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ for a normalised $\psi$, and every bounded assigned sharp
observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in
this preparation;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

(e) *Spectral support and exact values.* For every preparation $\rho$ one has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$, and an exact energy value
$\lambda$ has $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue, in which case the probability is the total weight of the
eigenspace; in particular no exact value in $\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(H_{\kappa})$
is admissible, and the item asserts neither that $0$ is an eigenvalue nor any
statement about eigenvalues in the positive half-line, which are excluded by
the following radial items;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no eigenvalue list, no
degeneracy, no transition, radiation or line-intensity statement, no
identification of $\kappa$, $m$ or $\hbar$ with measured constants, and no
empirical result.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.1, printed pages 221-222 (self-adjointness of -Delta - gamma/|x| on H^2 and sigma_ess = [0,infinity)), and Section 5.1, printed pages 123-125 (Stone's theorem and the time evolution)

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.2.3, printed pages 110-111 (self-adjointness of the radial Coulomb Hamiltonian and the admissible states) and Section 4.3, printed pages 111-112 (the Coulomb problem and its negative-energy bound states)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 182-185 (the stationary states of the hydrogen-like model and their energies)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared one-centre Coulomb model and the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5: the model's assigned energy is a sharp observable on H^2 with essential spectrum [0,infinity) and negative spectrum consisting only of isolated finite-multiplicity discrete eigenvalues; its flow is the strongly continuous unitary group of P4 with the norm-differentiable Schroedinger equation exactly on the domain; its stationary preparations are exactly the eigenrays with point-mass energy law; and position and energy readings coexist. The item asserts no measured energy, no apparatus, no eigenvalue list or degeneracy, no transition or radiation statement and no empirical result; it does not identify the coupling, mass or charge with any measured constants.

items.title: The one-centre Coulomb model: bound energies, n^2-degeneracy, completeness of the bound states in the negative spectral subspace and the continuum
items.statement:
Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ with length scale $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and
the energy-observable content of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For integer labels $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le\bar m\le l$
(the magnetic label $\bar m$ is distinct from the mass $m$), let
$\psi_{nl\bar m}$ be the regular bound solutions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] and put
$\Psi_{nl\bar m}:=\psi_{nl\bar m}/\|\psi_{nl\bar m}\|$, and put
$$E_{n}:=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}\qquad(n\ge1).$$
Then:

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nl\bar m}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nl\bar m}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nl\bar m}=E_{n}\Psi_{nl\bar m}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nl\bar m}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(b) the eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $E_{n}$, $n\ge1$;
the eigenspace of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ is exactly
$\operatorname{span}\{\Psi_{nl\bar m}:0\le l\le n-1,\ -l\le\bar m\le l\}$, so the model
assigns to the level $n$ the **model degeneracy** $n^{2}$; in particular
$H_{\kappa}$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,+\infty)$, whose spectral content is
entirely essential spectrum $[0,+\infty)$ in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] (a);

(c) the family
$(\Psi_{nl\bar m})_{n\ge1,\,0\le l\le n-1,\,-l\le\bar m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal
family of the negative spectral subspace
$E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: their closed
linear span is that subspace, whose unit vectors give exactly the pure
preparations with negative energy outcomes almost surely;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nl\bar m}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The values $E_{n}$ are model
parameters determined by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; no numerical value, no measured
line, no transition rate, no photon or light-matter coupling and no empirical
result is asserted. The absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace
is recorded by the cited mathematics for the unscaled operator and is not
restated for the scaled model here.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.4 printed pages 229-235 (Theorem 10.9: the bound states psi_(n,l,m), the eigenvalues E_n = -(gamma/(2n))^2 and the n^2-dimensional eigenspace) and Section 10.4 p. 233 (the non-terminating solution is not square integrable)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 185-186 (the energy spectrum E = -Z^2 mu e^4/(2 n^2 (4 pi eps_0 hbar)^2), the n^2-fold degeneracy and the series limit) and Section 8.1.1, printed page 186 (the Lyman, Balmer and Paschen series as model consequences)

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3.1, printed pages 112-116 (the terminating-series argument, the spectrum (4.30), the Bohr radius (4.31), the n^2 degeneracy and the fine-structure exclusion)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared one-centre Coulomb model with parameters hbar, m, kappa: the model's bound energies are exactly E_n = -m kappa^2/(2 hbar^2 n^2), the level n carrying an n^2-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the transported Laguerre solutions, the bound states forming a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace, and the nonnegative spectral subspace containing no eigenvectors and being infinite dimensional, so the bound states alone do not exhaust the model's state space. The item asserts no measured spectral line, no transition rate, no photon, no light-matter coupling and no empirical result, and it does not assert absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace of the scaled model, which is recorded for the unscaled operator by the cited mathematics.

items.title: The one-centre Coulomb model: position and radial distributions of the bound states, with the ground-state density and its scales
items.statement:
Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5, the readings of the declared
one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, $\kappa>0$ and length scale
$a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, the energy-observable reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]], the bound-state data
of [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], and the
spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For the integer labels $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le\bar m\le l$
with magnetic label $\bar m$ distinct from mass $m$, let $\psi_{nl\bar m}$ and
$\Psi_{nl\bar m}=\psi_{nl\bar m}/\|\psi_{nl\bar m}\|$ be the bound vectors of the cited
theorem, and write $u_{nl}$ for the reduced regular solution with
$\psi_{nl\bar m}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)/r$. Then:

(a) for every label and every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ the position
outcome law in the unit preparation $[\Psi_{nl\bar m}]$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nl\bar m}}(B)=\|\psi_{nl\bar m}\|^{-2}\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)\,|Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr;$$
in particular, for a **radial** set $B=\{x:a<|x|<b\}$ with
$0\le a<b\le+\infty$ one has
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nl\bar m}}(B)=\frac{1}{\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\,dr,$$
so the **radial density** $p_{nl}(r):=|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$ is a
probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p_{nl}\ge0$ and
$\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}(r)\,dr=1$;

For a general unit **bound eigenvector** $\chi$ with $H_\kappa\chi=E_n\chi$, write
$\chi=\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}\sum_{\bar m=-l}^{l}b_{l\bar m}\Psi_{nl\bar m}$,
where $\sum_{l,\bar m}|b_{l\bar m}|^2=1$, and set
$\widehat u_{nl}:=u_{nl}/\|u_{nl}\|_2$. Then
$$\mu^G_\chi(B)=\int_0^\infty\int_{S^2}\mathbf1_B(r\Omega)\left|\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}\sum_{\bar m=-l}^{l}b_{l\bar m}\widehat u_{nl}(r)Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)\right|^2d\sigma(\Omega)\,dr,$$
and its radial marginal has density
$$p_\chi(r)=\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}\sum_{\bar m=-l}^{l}|b_{l\bar m}|^2p_{nl}(r).$$
The general position density includes interference terms and need not factor
as a single $p_{nl}$ times one spherical-harmonic weight.

(b) for $n=1,l=\bar m=0$ the normalized vector $\Psi_{100}$ has a representative
of the form
$$\Psi_{100}(x)=\zeta_{100}(\pi a_{\kappa}^{3})^{-1/2}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}},\qquad |\zeta_{100}|=1,$$
and its radial density is
$$p_{10}(r)=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}};$$
the mean of $p_{10}$ is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{10}(r)\,dr=3a_{\kappa}/2$, the
unique maximum of $p_{10}$ is at $r=a_{\kappa}$, the spatial density
of this representative is $|\Psi_{100}|^{2}=\frac{1}{\pi a_{\kappa}^{3}}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}}$,
strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin,
and for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{100}}\bigl(\{|x|<\varepsilon\}\bigr)=\frac{1}{6}\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^{3}+O\Bigl(\bigl(\frac{\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\bigr)^{4}\Bigr)>0,$$
which tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$: the density maximum at the
origin is not an atom of probability at any point;

(c) for every label the reduced solution has the polynomial-exponential form
$$u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}\,r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na_{\kappa})}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}\bigl(2r/(na_{\kappa})\bigr)\qquad(c_{nl}\ne0),$$
with $L_{j}^{(a)}$ the Laguerre polynomial of integer order, so the radial
density of the level $(n,l)$ is a polynomial times $r^{2l+2}$ times a
decreasing exponential, and its normalisation constant is fixed by
$\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}|^{2}dr=\|\psi_{nl\bar m}\|^{2}$;

(d) *Reading and scope.* The statements are conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the
declared Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The radial density is the
reading of the model's position observable on radial sets; it is not a
trajectory, an orbit or a definite distance, and the model assigns positive
probability to every open ball around the origin and to arbitrarily large
radii. No measured radius, no measured density and no identification of
$a_{\kappa}$ with a laboratory length is asserted; numerical comparison
requires the measured constants as qualified empirical inputs and is deferred.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3.2, printed pages 116-117 (the hydrogen wavefunctions r^l f_(n,l)(r) e^(-beta r/2n) Y_lm with generalised Laguerre polynomials, the ground state psi = (1/sqrt(pi r_B^3)) e^(-r/r_B) and its nodes)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1.2, printed pages 187-190 (the radial eigenfunctions u_n^l, the ground-state radial function, the r-expectation values and the probability outside classically allowed radii)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.4, printed pages 229-235 (the explicit normalised bound states and the lowest eigenvalue, with the ground-state formula)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared one-centre Coulomb model: the position outcome law of any normalised bound eigenvector, the radial density |u_nl|^2/||u_nl||^2 times the angular spherical-harmonic weight for each labelled separated vector, the finite-superposition law and radial mixture for a general bound eigenvector, and the explicit ground-state density, its mean radius 3 a_kappa/2, its mode a_kappa, the positivity of the probability in every ball around the origin and the absence of an atomic probability at the origin. The scales a_kappa and the density are model data; the item asserts no measured radius, no orbit, no trajectory, no formation or decay process, and does not identify a_kappa with any measured length.

items.title: The declared two-body Coulomb model: reduced-mass decomposition, relative levels as thresholds and the absence of stationary total states
items.statement:
Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared two-body Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a), (b),
(d) and (e) with declared masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, opposite charge magnitudes
$q_{-},q_{+}>0$, and coupling
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ (the equal-magnitude branch
$q_{-}=q_{+}=q$ has $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$), reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map
$\Phi$, its unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the total operator $H_{2}$ on
$H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$, the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}$
and the relative operator $C_{\mu}$, together with the one-centre results
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] applied with mass
parameter $\mu$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the identity $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$
holds on the tensor product, and $C_{\mu}$ is exactly the one-centre Coulomb
operator of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
parameter $\mu$; the model's relative problem is therefore the declared
one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$;

(b) the relative bound energies are
$$\mathcal E_{n}:=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu a_{\mu}^{2}n^{2}},\qquad a_{\mu}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{\mu\kappa}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
with model degeneracy $n^{2}$ within the relative problem and the same radial
and position readings as in
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] with $m$
replaced by $\mu$;

(c) the total operator $H_{2}$ has no eigenvalues at all:
$\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},+\infty)$, the whole negative
part $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},0)$ of the spectrum is continuous,
and each relative bound energy $\mathcal E_{n}$ is the lower endpoint of its
continuous centre-of-mass channel $[\mathcal E_{n},+\infty)$, hence a channel
threshold rather than an eigenvalue of $H_{2}$;

(d) let $P_{R,j}:=-i\hbar\partial_{R_j}$ on the factor domain
$$D(P_{R,j})=\{\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)\text{ as a weak derivative}\},$$
and define the lifted total-momentum component on the composite state space by
$$\widetilde P_{R,j}:=U_{\Phi}^{-1}(P_{R,j}\otimes I)U_{\Phi},\qquad D(\widetilde P_{R,j})=U_{\Phi}^{-1}\{F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R}\times\mathbb R^{3}_{r};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}F\in L^{2}\text{ as a weak derivative}\};$$
it is self-adjoint on this maximal weak-derivative domain, has momentum unit
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and has no nonzero eigenvectors in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$. A state of definite total momentum would
be a simultaneous eigenvector of the three lifted components, so the model
has no such normalisable state. Since $H_{2}$ has no
eigenvalues, for every $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$ and
nonzero relative bound vector $u$ with $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$, any
nonzero tensor product $\varphi\otimes u$ in the transformed $(R,r)$ tensor
space, equivalently $U_{\Phi}^{-1}(\varphi\otimes u)$ in the composite
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})$ state space, is not an eigenvector; the
stationary-state criterion therefore excludes its pure preparation as a
stationary state;

(e) *Reading.* The reduced mass obeys $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$ and
satisfies $\mu\le\min\{m_{1},m_{2}\}$ with $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$
at fixed $m_{1}$; the model reads the one-centre model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
$m_{1}$ as the fixed-nucleus limiting description, and the relative energies
$\mathcal E_{n}$ are strictly weaker in magnitude than the fixed-nucleus
energies $-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
two-body model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured mass, charge
or level, no transition, photon or radiation statement, no binding or
formation dynamics, and no identification of the model with a laboratory
atom beyond the tested identification of clause (e) of the model definition.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 8.1, printed pages 182-185 (equations (8.3)-(8.10): the centre-of-mass and relative coordinates, the reduced mass mu = m_e m_n/(m_e+m_n), the separated Hamiltonians and the product eigenfunctions)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.1-10.2, printed pages 221-225 (the one-particle reduction of the two-body Coulomb problem and the parameters of the relative equation)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.3, printed pages 111-112 (the hydrogen atom as a two-body Coulomb problem with the electron mass in the relative equation)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the declared two-body Coulomb model with masses m1, m2, opposite charge magnitudes q_- and q_+, and coupling kappa=q_-q_+/(4 pi epsilon_0), including its equal-magnitude neutral branch: the centre-of-mass/relative decomposition U_Phi H_2 U_Phi^(-1) = T_R tensor I + I tensor C_mu, the identification of the relative problem with the one-centre Coulomb model of mass mu, the relative gross-structure levels E_n^mu = -mu kappa^2/(2 hbar^2 n^2) with degeneracy n^2 within the relative problem, the fact that the total two-body Hamiltonian has no eigenvalues and continuous negative spectrum with the relative levels as channel thresholds, and the absence of normalisable total-momentum eigenstates on the composite L2(R6) state space. H2, T_R and C_mu are energy operators in joules; the lifted total-momentum components have unit kg m s^-1. The item asserts no measured level, no transition, no photon, no external-field or many-body effect and no empirical result; it does not model binding or formation dynamics and does not identify the parameters with measured masses or charges.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the central-potential and hydrogen page
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page establishes.** The pair declares a central-potential model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]) and a Coulomb and
  two-body hydrogen model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]]), proves the
  spherical reduction of smooth compactly supported vectors, with the radial
  equation read almost everywhere and pure-preparation readings only for
  nonzero vectors after normalization
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-spherical-reduction-of-smooth-states]]), and derives
  the energy-observable and flow reading
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]), the bound
  energies $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ with $n^{2}$-fold
  model degeneracy and the completeness of the bound states in the negative
  spectral subspace with a nonzero continuum
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]]), the radial
  and ground-state position readings
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]]), and the
  two-body reduced-mass decomposition with the relative levels as thresholds
  and the absence of stationary total states
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]]). Every
  item is conditional on the cited postulates, the declared model and the
  cited mathematics; none establishes that the model or its postulates
  describes nature.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no reported spectral
  line, no count, no calibration, no detector model, no sampling assumption
  and no statistical inference appears on the page, and no numerical value of
  $\hbar$, $m$, $\kappa$, $q$, $m_{1}$, $m_{2}$ or $\varepsilon_{0}$ is fixed
  by any item. The transition frequencies, line intensities and selection
  rules of a hydrogen-like system require the radiation extension and the
  light-matter coupling of later items, and the scattering, ionisation and
  continuum processes require the three-dimensional scattering pair; neither
  is built or assumed here. The dipole matrix elements and their angular
  selection rules are reserved to the light-matter pair, and the numerical
  comparison with measured spectra to a future experiment item with its own
  preparation, calibration, sampling and uncertainty record; no such item
  exists in this batch.

- **Excluded physics.** The gross-structure model excludes spin and magnetic
  couplings, relativistic fine structure and the splitting of the
  $n^{2}$-fold degeneracy, finite nuclear size and nuclear structure,
  recoil corrections beyond the two-body reduced-mass formulation, QED
  corrections including the Lamb shift, hyperfine structure, shielding and
  many-body modifications of the $1/r$ potential, external fields, and
  radiation reaction. The source treatments describe several of these
  corrections as small compared with the gross-structure energies; no such
  magnitude comparison is a premise of any item on this page, and none of the
  excluded effects is claimed to be negligible by this page.

- **Empirical status of the model's numbers.** Statements such as "the
  hydrogen ground-state binding energy is about $13.6$ electronvolts" are
  conditional evaluations of the model's formula with measured constants
  (such as the fine-structure constant, the electron-to-proton mass ratio or
  the Rydberg constant) as inputs; they carry the uncertainties, conditions
  and conventions of those inputs and are not measurements of hydrogen by
  this page. Agreement of a computed transition frequency with a measured
  line would test the combined model, apparatus and constant assumptions; it
  would not be a deductive proof of the model.

- **Physical-interface note.** The model declarations, the readings and the
  scope exclusions above are the public physical interface of the pair;
  changing them requires the ordinary direct and indirect consumer review
  under the workflow rules, and the empirical qualifications carried here
  must be preserved by every later item that consumes these results.
