Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.2 printed pages 206-208 (PDF pages 214-216): the degenerate-subspace diagonalisation of the perturbation, together with the conjecture that the system 'jumps' to the lowest branch, which is not imported as a deduction

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.3 printed pages 117-119 (PDF pages 129-131) and Section 6.6 printed pages 153-159 (PDF pages 165-171): the min-max theorem and the bounded-perturbation resolvent estimates on which the page's conditional statements rest

items.physical_scope: A scope and status record for the controlled-approximations page: the adopted model clauses, the proved conditional statements with their gap, smoothness and boundedness hypotheses, the explicit exclusions (equilibration and branch selection, unbounded and static-field perturbations, rectangular and coalescing turning-point configurations, detectors and measurements), and the absence of any empirical record on this page.

items.title: A two-level finite-gap model: exact eigenvalues, the second-order correction and a finite check of the cubic remainder bound
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 for a declared **two-level system**
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) with state space
$\mathfrak H=\mathbb C^{2}$ in the standard orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$
and with the observable reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; read all
energies in joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Fix
real **gap** and **coupling** parameters $g>0$ and $c>0$, and declare the
model's energy observable family by the perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with
$$H_{0}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&g\end{pmatrix},\qquad V:=\begin{pmatrix}0&c\\c&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V\quad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).$$
Then $H_{0}$ has the isolated simple eigenvalue $E=0$ with gap $g$,
$v=\|V\|=c$, $\psi_{0}=e_{1}$, and the reduced inverse of the model clause
(c)(iii) is $S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1/g)$ on $Q_{0}\mathfrak H=\mathbb
Ce_{2}$. Then:

(a) for every real $\lambda$ the matrix $H(\lambda)$ is Hermitian with exactly
two eigenvalues
$$E_{\pm}(\lambda)=\frac{g\pm\sqrt{g^{2}+4\lambda^{2}c^{2}}}{2},$$
both simple for $\lambda\ne0$ and spanning the spectrum for every $\lambda$;
in the model's valid contour range $2|\lambda|c/g<1$, its distinguished
label is $E_{\lambda}=E_{-}(\lambda)$. The formula $E_-$ remains an exact
continuous lower spectral branch for all real couplings, even beyond that
fixed-contour range;

(b) the exact perturbation coefficients are
$$E'(0)=0,\qquad E''(0)=-\frac{2c^{2}}{g},\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0}=-\frac{c}{g}e_{2},\qquad \psi_{0}=e_{1},$$
and the exact eigenvalue has the convergent expansion
$$E_{-}(\lambda)=-\frac{\lambda^{2}c^{2}}{g} +\frac{\lambda^{4}c^{4}}{g^{3}}-\frac{2\lambda^{6}c^{6}}{g^{5}}+O(\lambda^{8});$$

(c) the cubic remainder bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-approximations-nondegenerate-perturbation-expansion]] clause (e)
holds in this model for every $|\lambda|<R=g/(8c)$, and at the test point
$\lambda=R/2=g/(16c)$ the exact remainder and its bound are
$$E_{-}\!\left(\frac{g}{16c}\right)+\frac{g}{256} =\frac{g}{2}\Bigl(1-\frac{\sqrt{65}}{8}\Bigr)+\frac{g}{256}\approx1.51\cdot10^{-5}g \le\frac{g}{32},$$
so the finite check is satisfied with a wide margin;

(d) the exact spectrum computed in (a) is a spectral statement about the
declared two-level family; it identifies no physical system, asserts no
measured splitting, and asserts nothing about which of the two spectral
subspaces a preparation occupies (that is fixed by the preparation and the
evolution of P4, not by the perturbative expansion).

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1 printed pages 203-205 (PDF pages 211-213): the perturbative expansion, the first-order coefficient (9.6) and the second-order coefficient (9.11) for a non-degenerate level

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 5 'Ammonia molecule in an electric field' printed and PDF pages 11-16: the exactly solvable two-state Stark family with eigenvalues E0 +/- sqrt(mu^2 E^2 + Delta^2), the closed analogue of the check performed here

items.physical_scope: A conditional two-level computation inside the declared perturbed-family model with a finite gap: the exact eigenvalues of the family, its second-order coefficient, the exact quartic expansion, and a finite numerical check of the page's cubic remainder bound at half the perturbation radius. The example is a model computation in the declared finite-dimensional subspace; it asserts no physical system identification, no measured splitting and no transition.

items.title: A finite-level static Stark model: vanishing first-order shift, exact splitting with leading quadratic shift and a finite check of the remainder bound
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 for the declared two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d), in the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the dipole
operator $D_{j}=-qQ_{j}$ and the compressed finite-level coupling of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]. Use
the Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$ and
$a_{\mu}:=\hbar^{2}/(\mu\kappa)>0$. Choose as
the finite-level subspace the **declared two-dimensional subspace**
$$W:=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
where $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ are normalized bound states of the model with
angular labels $(n,l,m)=(1,0,0)$ and $(2,1,0)$ supplied by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], so that
$H_{\kappa}\psi_{1}=E_{1}\psi_{1}$, $H_{\kappa}\psi_{2}=E_{2}\psi_{2}$ with
$$E_{1}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},\qquad E_{2}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}},\qquad \Delta:=E_{2}-E_{1}=\frac{3m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}}>0 .$$
Choose the external field along the third axis of the declared frame,
$\mathbf E_{\rm ext}=(0,0,\mathcal E)$ with $\mathcal E>0$ in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, and use the dimensionless coupling
$$\lambda:=\frac{\mathcal E}{1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}},\qquad V:=-(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})\,D^{W}_{3},$$
so that the Stark model of the postulate reads
$$H_{S}(\mathcal E)=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad H_{0}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&0\\0&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}$$
in the declared orthonormal basis. Then:

(a) the compression of the dipole matrix has the form
$$D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0,\qquad D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_{\rm rel}:=|\langle\psi_{2},D_{3}\psi_{1}\rangle|>0,$$
with unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$, where the phase of $\psi_{2}$ is chosen to make
the off-diagonal entry positive. The local computation below gives
$D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2\,q a_{\mu}/243>0$ from the declared model parameters;
this is an exact model identity, with no measured value of any parameter.
The diagonal entries vanish by angular degree selection, and only $Q_{0}$
can contribute between the chosen $m=0$ states; nonvanishing is proved by
explicit radial and angular integration;

(b) $v=\|V\|=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ in joules and the family
$H_{S}$ has the exact eigenvalues
$$F_{\pm}(\mathcal E)=\frac{E_{1}+E_{2}}{2} \pm\sqrt{\Bigl(\frac{\Delta}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+\bigl(D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E\bigr)^{2}},$$
the lower branch $F_{-}$ being the model's followed label for
dimensionless couplings $0\le\lambda<R:=\Delta/(8v)$, equivalently
$0\le\mathcal E<\Delta/(8D_{\rm rel})$, with $\Delta$ playing the role of the gap $g$;

(c) the page's perturbation theorem applies with nondegenerate label
$E_{1}$ (gap $\Delta$), and gives the vanishing first-order shift
$$E'(0)=0$$
and the exact second derivative at zero
$$E''(0)=-\frac{2D_{\rm rel}^{2}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})^{2}}{\Delta},$$
equivalently the quadratic Stark shift
$$F_{-}(\mathcal E)=E_{1}-\frac{D_{\rm rel}^{2}\mathcal E^{2}}{\Delta} +O(\mathcal E^{4});$$

(d) the finite remainder check at half the perturbation radius
$\lambda=R/2$, equivalently $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$, gives the exact remainder
$$\Bigl|F_{-}+\frac{\Delta}{256}-E_{1}\Bigr|=\Delta\,\frac{129-16\sqrt{65}}{256}=\frac{\Delta}{256(129+16\sqrt{65})}<\frac{\Delta}{32768}<\frac{\Delta}{32},$$
so the page's cubic bound is satisfied at this coupling with a wide margin;

(e) scope: the computation is conditional on the declared truncated
two-state model and the adopted coupling; it identifies no laboratory atom,
reports no measured shift and no polarizability value, asserts no transition
rate, and does not treat the uncompressed linear potential
$-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$. The postulate excludes that model and
proves its common-test-domain expectations unbounded below for every nonzero
uniform field; no full energy-form domain is used here.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.1 printed pages 205-206 (PDF pages 213-214): the quadratic Stark effect of the hydrogen ground state, Eb = eE<100|z|100> = 0 by parity and the second-order formula (9.16)-(9.17); and Section 9.1.2 printed pages 206-208 (PDF pages 214-216): the linear Stark effect from the diagonalisation of eEz within the degenerate n=2 subspace

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Section 5 'Ammonia molecule in an electric field' printed and PDF pages 11-16: the two-state ammonia Stark family H = E0 I - Delta sigma1 + muE sigma3 and its exact eigenvalues E0 +/- sqrt(mu^2E^2 + Delta^2), the exact template for the closed form used here

items.physical_scope: A conditional finite-level computation in the declared two-body Coulomb model with the adopted static finite-level dipole coupling: the compressed two-state Stark family built from the model's 1s-like and 2p-like relative states, the vanishing diagonal dipole matrix elements by the angular selection rule, the exact closed-form eigenvalues of the two-state family, the vanishing first-order shift and the exact second derivative at zero from the page's non-degenerate theorem, and a finite numeric check of the cubic remainder bound. The example identifies no laboratory atom, asserts no measured Stark shift or polarizability value, and states no transition or lifetime; the uncompressed linear-potential model is explicitly outside its scope.

items.title: A spin-one multiplet in a uniform field: the exact Zeeman spectrum and degenerate first-order check
items.statement:
Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P6 for the massive spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), together with the
effective magnetic-moment coupling
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with real
gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma:=\gamma_{1}$ and the spin-one internal factor
$\mathbb C^{3}$ with spin operators $S_i=\hbar J_i$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] at $s=1$; read energies in
joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Declare the
**finite-level Zeeman model** by the perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with
$$\mathfrak H:=\mathbb C^{3},\qquad H_{0}:=\varepsilon I_{3},\qquad V:=-\gamma B_{z}S_{3},$$
where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ is a declared multiplet energy, $B_{z}>0$ is
the field magnitude in tesla of the uniform field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$,
so that the family is $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ with real coupling
$\lambda$ (dimensionless, equal to $1$ for the physical field) and
$v=\|V\|=|\gamma|B_{z}\hbar$. For the physical value $\lambda=1$ the family is
the model's Zeeman operator on the internal multiplet. Then:

(a) the perturbation preserves the multiplet: $[H_{0},V]=0$, the
first-order operator is $V_{E}=V$, and its eigenvalues counted with
multiplicity are $-\hbar\gamma B_{z},0,+\hbar\gamma B_{z}$ in joules. If
$\gamma\ne0$, these are three distinct simple eigenvalues; if $\gamma=0$,
the only eigenvalue is $0$ with multiplicity three. Thus the first-order
operator describes a triply degenerate level when the adopted magnetic
coupling vanishes;

(b) the exact energy eigenvalues of the family, counted with multiplicity,
are
$$\varepsilon-\lambda\hbar\gamma B_{z},\qquad \varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon+\lambda\hbar\gamma B_{z}.$$
They are three distinct simple levels exactly when $\lambda\gamma\ne0$;
when $\lambda=0$ or $\gamma=0$, the only energy is $\varepsilon$ with
multiplicity three. Each eigenvalue is affine in $\lambda$, so its
second-order and higher Taylor coefficients vanish identically;

(c) when $v>0$, the page's degenerate theorem applies for every $g>0$ (the
gap condition is vacuous because the spectrum of $H_{0}$ is the single value
$\varepsilon$) and every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g/4$; each
eigenvalue $z$ then satisfies
$\operatorname{dist}(z,\varepsilon+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E}))
\le 4\lambda^{2}v^{2}/g$, and the exact spectrum in (b) shows that this
distance is $0$. If $v=0$, equivalently $\gamma=0$, then
$H(\lambda)=\varepsilon I_{3}$ for every real $\lambda$, so the same
distance is $0$ directly, without invoking the theorem's positive-norm
hypothesis. In both cases the first-order eigenvalue set is exact, with
multiplicity retained as in (a)-(b);

(d) for a unit preparation vector $u\in\mathbb C^3$, put
$u(t)=e^{-itH(\lambda)/\hbar}u$ and $s_i(t)=\langle S_i u(t),u(t)\rangle$.
With $\omega=\lambda\gamma B_z$ (in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$),
$$s_3(t)=s_3(0),\qquad s_1(t)=\cos(\omega t)s_1(0)+\sin(\omega t)s_2(0),\qquad s_2(t)=\cos(\omega t)s_2(0)-\sin(\omega t)s_1(0).$$
Thus the transverse means rotate by $-\omega t$, with the signed Larmor
parameter $\omega$ equal to $\gamma B_z$ at $\lambda=1$;

(e) no branch selection: the energy eigenspaces of (b) are spectral data of
the family; a preparation in any eigenstate is stationary, and a superposition
evolves with the relative phases of (b). The example asserts
no instantaneous transition of any preparation to the lowest sublevel, no
relaxation and no measurement; which sublevel a preparation occupies is
fixed by the preparation and by P4.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.1.3 printed pages 208-211 (PDF pages 216-219), Eq. (9.25): the perturbation HBs = mu_B B(Lz + 2Sz) = mu_B B(Jz + Sz), its diagonalisation in the m_l, m_s labels and the Zeeman/Paschen-Back splitting patterns

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 2-4 printed and PDF pages 2-10: spin precession in a magnetic field (Section 2), the general two-state system viewed as a spin system (Section 3), and the ammonia molecule as a two-state system (Section 4); the spin operator along a field direction, its two eigenvalues and the magnetic-dipole energy are read in this range

items.physical_scope: A conditional finite-level computation for the declared spin-one internal multiplet of the massive spin-s model with the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling: the Zeeman family H0 + lambda V with H0 = epsilon I on the three-dimensional multiplet and V = -gamma B S3, its three energy eigenvalues counted with multiplicity (three distinct levels occur exactly when lambda gamma is nonzero), the first-order operator P0VP0 = V and the corresponding degenerate-perturbation localisation, and the absence of any relaxation or branch selection statement. The example identifies no laboratory species, reports no measured splitting or gyromagnetic ratio, and asserts no detector record.

items.title: Tunnelling asymptotic limits: the smooth-barrier semiclassical limit and the exact rectangular prefactor comparison
items.statement:
Adopt the declared one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] and the WKB regime model
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with their framework
postulates
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]),
with units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *Smooth-barrier semiclassical limit.* Let $V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,E,W,
\lambda,h$ be data of the WKB regime model satisfying its hypothesis (W2),
with exponent $S=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W-\lambda}\,d\xi$ and declared
transmission coefficient $T(h)$. At fixed dimensionless barrier data $(W,\lambda)$, there are $h_0>0$,
$0\le\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$ for $0<h<h_0$, and $0\le C_{0}<\infty$,
depending only on the fixed barrier data and matching sections, such that
$$\Bigl|T(h)e^{2S/h}-1\Bigr| \le\frac{C_{0}[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}]}{1-C_{0}[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}]}$$
for $0<h<h_0$ whenever the denominator is positive; in particular
$$\lim_{h\downarrow0}T(h)e^{2S/h}=1,$$
and the physical reading of the limit is the exponential law
$T\approx\exp\bigl(-\frac2\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx\bigr)$
with prefactor tending to one;

(b) *Rectangular thick-barrier limit.* Fix $m,\hbar,E,U$ with $U>E>0$ and vary
the wall width $a\to\infty$ (equivalently, $\kappa a\to\infty$). For the
**rectangular wall model**
excluded by the smooth theorem, take the exact scattering solution of the
line model with $V(x)=U$ for $0<x<a$ and $V=0$ otherwise, $U>E>0$,
$k=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar$, $\kappa=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar$ and exact transmission
$$T_{\rm rect}=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^{2}\sinh^{2}(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1};$$
then, in this fixed-parameter limit,
$$\frac{T_{\rm rect}}{e^{-2\kappa a}}\longrightarrow \frac{16E(U-E)}{U^{2}}=\frac{16k^{2}\kappa^{2}}{(k^{2}+\kappa^{2})^{2}},$$
so in the rectangular model the exponential law holds with the profile-dependent
prefactor $16E(U-E)/U^{2}$; the exponent $2\kappa a$ equals the classical
WKB exponent $2B/\hbar$ of the rectangular barrier, and the limit shows that
the exponential alone does not determine the prefactor;

(c) *Reading of the comparison.* Statement (a) is a theorem about smooth
compactly supported barriers with separated simple turning points, and its
prefactor-one conclusion uses the Airy matching of that class; statement (b)
is an exact model computation for a piecewise constant wall, whose sharp
discontinuities are precisely why it is excluded from (a). Neither statement
asserts a measured transmission, a detector response, a wave packet or an
apparatus; both are conditional statements about the declared
one-dimensional models.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Sections 5.3-5.6 printed and PDF pages 64-75: 5.3 Square Potential Barrier p. 64 (the exact rectangular transmission), 5.4-5.6 (the WKB barrier exponent)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 5.3 printed pages 87-89 (PDF pages 95-97): tunnelling through a potential barrier and the thick-barrier exponential suppression

items.physical_scope: Two asymptotic statements about declared one-dimensional barrier transmission data: the semiclassical limit of the smooth compactly supported barrier of the WKB regime model, in which the ratio of the declared transmission coefficient to exp(-2S/h) tends to one; and the exact thick-barrier limit of the rectangular wall model, whose profile-dependent limit prefactor is 16E(U-E)/U^2 and can differ from one, showing that the exponential law alone does not determine the prefactor and that rectangular walls are outside the smooth-barrier theorem. No measured transmission, detector, sample or apparatus is asserted.

items.title: What the controlled-approximations examples establish and what they do not
items.statement:
- **What the page contains.** Four conditional computations of the declared
  models of the companion A page: the exact two-level finite-gap family with
  its second-order coefficient and a finite check of the cubic remainder
  bound
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-two-level-finite-gap-correction]]); the finite
  level static Stark model of the declared Coulomb pair with vanishing
  first-order shift, the exact square-root eigenvalue separation, its leading
  quadratic small-field correction and a finite check of the
  remainder bound
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-level-shift]]); the spin-one
  multiplet in a uniform field with its three exact eigenvalues counted with
  multiplicity, distinct splitting only for nonzero coupling, and the
  degenerate first-order check
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-zeeman-multiplet-splitting]]); and the two
  tunnelling asymptotic limits, the smooth-barrier semiclassical limit and
  the exact rectangular thick-barrier prefactor
  ([[ex-nrqm-approximations-smooth-barrier-tunnelling-limits]]). Each
  computation states its model and its sources and cites the page's theorem
  it checks.

- **What the checks are.** The first two examples verify the quantitative
  remainder bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-nondegenerate-perturbation-expansion]] on
  exactly solvable two-state families, one with a finite gap and a
  second-order shift, one with the compressed dipole coupling of
  [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]; the
  third verifies the first-order localisation of
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-degenerate-first-order-splitting]] in the
  exactly diagonalizable Zeeman family; the fourth compares two asymptotic
  limits, one covered by
  [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-barrier-transmission-asymptotics]] and one
  explicitly excluded by it. These are mathematical checks inside declared
  models, not tests of the models against data.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no measured Stark or
  Zeeman shift, no splitting value, no gyromagnetic ratio, no measured matrix element
  or polarizability value, no transmission count, no detector response, no
  apparatus, no calibration, no sampling model and no uncertainty record
  appears; the radial dipole parameter $D_{\rm rel}$ of the Stark example is
  computed exactly from the declared charge and Coulomb length scale,
  and is not measured. The examples
  assert no transition rate, no lifetime and no branch-relaxation process;
  see [[rem-nrqm-approximations-scope-and-empirical-status]] for the
  corresponding scope record of the A page.

- **Deferred content.** Empirical numerical matrix-element comparisons for concrete Coulomb
  systems, time-dependent driving, transition rates, adiabatic evolution, and
  any comparison with measured spectra belong to the driven-dynamics and
  light-matter pairs of the track; the uncompressed static-field model is
  outside the present scope by the postulate's exclusion clause.

items.title: The declared driven model: prescribed time-dependent energy families, propagator evolution and the two-level drive models
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

On a singleton interval $I=\{a\}$, the evolution declaration consists only of $U(a,a)=I$; all differential assertions in these class readings apply only when $a<b$, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints.

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The real parameters $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ represent angular frequencies of dimension duration$^{-1}$, read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; their numerical values are expressed in that unit, so $\omega t$ is dimensionless and $\hbar\omega_{0}$ and $\hbar\Omega_{1}$ have energy units; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

items.physical_scope: The driven-dynamics model of a declared system of the framework: a prescribed time-dependent family of self-adjoint energy operators in one of three declared regularity classes (bounded norm-continuous on a compact interval; a fixed self-adjoint part plus a strongly continuous bounded self-adjoint control; a common-domain C^1 family), the unitary two-time propagator declared to carry the state evolution, the reading of preparations and outcome laws at the running time, the energy-basis transition amplitudes and level populations, and the two declared two-level drive models (circular and linear polarization). The definition fixes terminology and readings only: it adopts the driven-evolution assumption as an additional model assumption beyond P4, and asserts no existence theorem (supplied by the cited mathematics in each class), no laboratory realization, no measurement, no open system, no equilibration and no empirical result.

items.title: The interaction picture of the declared driven model: readings, the interaction propagator and picture equivalence of outcome laws
items.statement:
**(a) Setting.** Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of its clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of clause (c)(ii) constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. The readings of P1 and P2 are those of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; all times lie in $I$ and are read in seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The free-flow factor.** The **free-flow factor** of the model is the autonomous flow of the unperturbed part,
$$E(t):=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] applied to the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$; it is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on all real arguments. This auxiliary group supplies $E(-t)$ and $E(t-s)$ even when those arguments lie outside $I$; the physical driven evaluation times $s,t$ remain in $I$. The **interaction-picture control** is the family $V_{I}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$,
$$V_{I}(t):=E(-t)V(t)E(t),$$
which is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. The **interaction propagator** is
$$U_{I}(t,s):=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)\qquad(s,t\in I),$$
and the model's clause (c)(ii) supplies, as the cited theorem proves, the decomposition
$$U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s).$$
The interaction propagator is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, satisfies $U_{I}(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U_{I}(t,r)=U_{I}(t,s)U_{I}(s,r)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H),$$
all as supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; these are readings of that theorem in the model's vocabulary, not new assumptions.

**(c) Interaction states and preparations.** For a Schroedinger-picture state vector $\psi(t)=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ the **interaction-picture state** is
$$\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)\psi(t),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s),$$
and for a preparation $\rho$ with $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ the **interaction-picture preparation** is
$$\rho_{I}(t):=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
which is again a preparation of the model by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; for a pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$, $[\psi_{I}(t)]$ is pure. The map $\psi(t)\mapsto\psi_{I}(t)$ is unitary at every $t$, so $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|$.

**(d) The two pictures assign the same outcome laws.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded and let $A_{I}(t):=E(-t)AE(t)$ be its interaction-picture representative, which is again a bounded self-adjoint observable with $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ for every Borel set $B$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint $T=-H_{0}/\hbar$. Then for every preparation $\rho$ specified at $s$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
because $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)\bigr)$ by cyclicity of the trace; equivalently, for a pure preparation, $\|E_{A}(B)\psi(t)\|=\|E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)\psi_{I}(t)\|$. This identity is the precise sense in which the two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; it is a reading of P2 together with the cited mathematics, not a claim about apparatuses.

**(e) Energy-basis transition amplitudes.** Let $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\in D(H_{0})$ be unit eigenvectors, $H_{0}\varphi_{a}=E_{a}\varphi_{a}$, $H_{0}\varphi_{b}=E_{b}\varphi_{b}$, and let $A_{ba}(t,s)$ and $p_{ba}(t,s)$ be the transition amplitude and probability of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]. Then
$$A_{ba}(t,s)=e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle ,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
by the decomposition of clause (b) and $E(-s)\varphi_{a}=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\varphi_{a}$, $\langle E(t)\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle=e^{-itE_{b}/\hbar}\langle\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle$; the phases are of modulus one ([[def-inner-product-space]]). The transition probability is therefore computable in either picture, and the definition records this as the reading used by the page's amplitude theorem; no measurement frequency or rate is defined.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are readings of the declared driven model, of clauses (b)-(e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], and of P1 and P2, in the vocabulary of the cited mathematics. The interaction picture is a change of description of the same model: it adds no assumption, no physical process, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about detectors, records or the laboratory realization of the model.
