items.title: The declared ideal counting, energy-window and analyser detection models of the radiation sector
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the measurement vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]].
Assume Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
including the hypotheses inherited from the radiation postulate and the cited
measurement mathematics.

**(b) Declared ideal total-number detector.** The **declared ideal
total-number detector** of the radiation sector is the declared ideal sharp
measurement with outcome set $\mathbb N$, outcome projection
$$P_{n}:=\Pi_{n}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the sector projections of the Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$; the family
$(\Pi_{n})$ consists of mutually orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong
sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses
(a),(b),(c)). Its **count law** in a declared radiation preparation $\rho$ is
the reading of clause (ii) of P2,
$$p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n}),\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}p_{n}(\rho)=1,$$
and its **number readout** is the assigned total-number observable $(N,1)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] read through the atom
law of P2. The conditional post-count state and the discarded-outcome state are
the Lueders updates of the measurement definition
([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]],
[[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]). The word "count" refers to
the quanta of the declared model; no laboratory counter, no absorption
process, no detection efficiency, no dark count, no dead time and no
background is declared here.

**(c) Declared ideal energy-window detector.** For a Borel set
$B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window
detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome
structure
$$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$
where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned
free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the
preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its
complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading
of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a
declared finite or countably infinite family $(B_a)_{a\in A}$ of pairwise
disjoint Borel windows covering $[0,\infty)$, with outcome projections
$(E_{H_f}(B_a))_{a\in A}$. Countable additivity of the spectral PVM and
$E_{H_f}([0,\infty))=I$ give their strong sum $I$, so this is an admissible
declared ideal sharp measurement. The
statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what
resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7.

**(d) Declared analyser detection.** The **declared polarisation-analyser
detection** of the fixed propagation mode is the analyser family
$\{P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\}$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], read as a
declared ideal sharp measurement of the polarisation factor; its law and its conditional update are proved on this page. It detects the polarisation alternative of the model and is not a photon counter.

**(e) Repetition requires a separate sampling model.** The declaration of a
detector gives the outcome law of a single declared measurement. A prediction
for repeated trials, a count rate, or any statistical comparison with data
requires in addition a declared preparation-and-apparatus model and a sampling
model in the sense of P7 -- for instance an identically-and-independently
repeated preparation with a declared number of trials -- which this page does
not supply. A single measurement outcome law is not a frequency and no
frequency is asserted.

**(f) Destructive detectors are outside the declared class.** A
photoabsorption detector that destroys the absorbed quantum, and any detector
whose post-outcome state of the radiation field is not the Lueders update,
requires its own declared instrument, that is its own outcome effects together
with its own conditional updates (clause (v) of P3, clause (d) of the
measurement definition). No such instrument is declared on this page, and the
"blocked" outcome of the analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome
law.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (b)-(d) fix vocabulary and read the cited postulates;
they add no physical assumption beyond P1-P3, P7 and the radiation model, and
they assert no detection mechanism, no response function and no empirical
result. In particular, the declaration of an ideal counting model is not a
claim that any physical device counts photons, and the energy-window model is
not a claim that any physical spectrometer measures exact energy.
items.physical_scope: The declared ideal detection models of the radiation sector: the ideal total-number counting model with the Fock sector projections as outcome structure and the Born law of P2, the ideal energy-window model with the spectral projections of the free-field energy, and the polarisation analyser of the fixed-mode model. The declaration fixes vocabulary only; it asserts no laboratory counter, no absorption instrument, no efficiency, no dark counts, no dead time, no background, no calibration and no sampling model, and repeated trials require a separately declared statistical model.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.3.6 printed pages 14-15 (PDF pages 22-23): individual photons either passing or being absorbed by an analyser, read as the outcome structure of an idealised polarisation measurement
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50: number states of a field mode and the number operator

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Section 1.2 printed pages 3-6 (PDF pages 4-7): occupation-number states and the number operator of a bosonic Fock space

items.title: Number and energy statistics of a declared mode: number states, coherent states and the continuum thermal limitation
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, a
dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $U:=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. Then:

(a) for every $n\in\mathbb N$ the $n$-quanta mode vector $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$
is a unit vector of the $n$-photon sector; the count law of the declared ideal
total-number detector in the preparation of its ray is
$p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$, and the number readout is $n$ with probability one;

(b) the count law of the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ of label $z$ is
the Poisson law
$$p_{n}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
with mean and variance
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}=|z|^{2},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^{2}p_{n}-\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}\Bigr)^{2}=|z|^{2};$$
in particular the mode-coherent preparation is not a number state unless
$z=0$;

(c) if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, with unit-mode coordinates
$\varphi(k)$ in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ as in clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], and writing
$\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\,\|\varphi(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$,
the energy means of the assigned free-field energy observable are
$$\langle H_f\rangle_{Ue_{n}}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,\qquad \langle H_f\rangle_{U\psi_{z}}=|z|^{2}\,\bar\varepsilon ;$$

(d) under the same condition $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing
$\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^2$,
the energy variances are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{Ue_{n}}(H_f)=n\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{U\psi_{z}}(H_f)=|z|^{2}\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$
the first is strictly positive for every $n\ge1$ and the second is strictly
positive for every $z\ne0$. Thus $Ue_n$ has non-sharp energy for $n\ge1$
and $U\psi_z$ has non-sharp energy for $z\ne0$. At $n=0$ or $z=0$ the
corresponding preparation is the vacuum $\Omega$, with $H_f\Omega=0$ and
energy law $\delta_0$;

(e) *full-sector Gibbs limitation*: let $\beta>0$ have SI unit
$\mathrm J^{-1}$, so that $\beta H_f$ is dimensionless. The bounded operator
$e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and hence not trace class; therefore it does
not define a density operator by trace normalization on the full transverse
continuum sector. This conclusion rules out only that trace-normalized
full-sector Gibbs form. Other mode-selected, regularized or otherwise
separately defined preparations are outside this theorem; no identification of
$\beta$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature and no thermal interpretation
of any state is asserted here;

(f) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model
and use only the declared ideal counting model. No measured count, frequency,
efficiency or temperature is asserted, and no sampling model is introduced.
items.physical_scope: The conditional number and energy statistics of a declared normalisable mode of the adopted radiation sector: the n-quanta mode state has sharp count n; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law of dimensionless parameter |z|^2 with mean and variance |z|^2; the energy means and variances of these preparations are computed from the mode profile, are strictly positive in variance for n>=1 and z!=0 (the vacuum cases have zero variance), and the full-sector Gibbs operator e^(-beta H_f) is not trace class for beta>0 in J^-1. This excludes only its trace-normalized Gibbs density form; other preparations are outside the theorem. The result is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, uses the ideal counting model only, reports no measured count and asserts no thermalisation or temperature identification.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50 and Section 4 printed pages 26-41: number states with energy increment hbar*omega, coherent states with mean photon number |alpha|^2, and the Poisson number distribution of a coherent state

S. Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; retrieved via the Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 14 Section 14.2 printed pages 220-222: coherent states as preparations without definite particle number, their normalization and their number expectation and variance

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the photons and radiation modes page
items.statement:
**What the page adopts.** The page adopts the radiation extension of the
framework, [[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]:
a fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model with a two-dimensional
transverse internal space, a quantised free transverse radiation sector with
bosonic Fock space, and the mode assignments $\omega=c|k|$,
$E=\hbar\omega$ and $p=\hbar k$ in a declared inertial chart. These are
additional model assumptions of the framework; they are not derived from P1-P7,
not derived from classical Maxwell theory or special relativity, and not
obtained as a limit of the massive one-particle model. The page also adopts the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
for every reading of a detector outcome.

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] fix the
model vocabulary, units and domains.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] proves the Born
outcome law $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$, $\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the
declared ideal analyser, its affinity over mixtures, its phase invariance and
the conditional update of a repeated ideal analyser.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]] proves that a
normalisable one-photon preparation has the sharp number readout one, the
frequency and energy laws given by the push-forwards of $\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$
under $c|k|$ and $\hbar c|k|$ (a unit packet coordinate $f(k)$ has units
$\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$), their means under the first-moment condition, and
the corresponding momentum-component laws and means under absolute
first-moment integrability. Frequency, energy and momentum variances are
strictly positive and finite on the corresponding multiplier domains; the
singleton probabilities vanish for every normalisable unit vector without a
moment-domain hypothesis.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] proves the sharp
count of the $n$-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law and moments of the
mode-coherent preparation, the energy means and variances of those
preparations, and that $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not trace class for the full
continuum sector when $\beta>0$ has unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Thus its
trace-normalized full-sector Gibbs density is unavailable; other preparations
are outside the theorem. All these are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and
the adopted radiation model in the declared measurement models. The repeated
ideal-analyser conditional update additionally adopts P3
([[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]); its use is restricted
to outcomes of positive probability. Their units are recorded in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] and in the assigned observables
of the model.

**What the page does not claim.** The page does not derive the radiation
extension from Maxwell's equations, does not derive a Lorentz transformation
law for mode labels, polarisations or energies, and does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector; the two polarisation states of the photon
are adopted, and their relativistic description by Lorentz-group
representations is outside this non-relativistic extension. It does not
introduce a photon position wave function, a photon localisation operator or a
general photon-position distribution; the sharp-mode label $k$ is a spectral
parameter and not a state, and no normalisable one-photon vector has sharp
frequency, energy or momentum. It does not supply a light-matter Hamiltonian, a
dipole coupling, selection rules, absorption or stimulated emission, and it
does not supply vacuum spontaneous emission; those belong to the later pair
on light-matter and spectral transitions, where the coupling and environment
assumptions are declared separately.

**What the page's idealisations are.** The declared analyser, the declared
total-number detector and the declared energy-window detector are ideal
projection-valued measurements of the model
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]). No
laboratory polariser, counter or spectrometer is identified with them; no
efficiency, dark count, dead time, background, calibration or resolution is
declared, and a destructive absorption detector would require its own
instrument. A single measurement law is not a frequency: repeated trials
require a separately declared preparation and sampling model in the sense of
P7, which this page does not supply.

**Empirical status.** The page records no experiment, no measured count, no
calibration, no uncertainty budget and no statistical test, and none is
invented. The Born ratio $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the declared analyser
coincides with the intensity ratio of the declared classical transverse-field
model of the companion page; the coincidence is a property of the two declared
models and does not establish field quantisation, and classical
electromagnetic waves also interfere. Whether a given source, polariser or
detector is described by the declared fixed-mode model is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7; agreement of the model's conditional
predictions with reported data would be evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions, not a deductive proof of the model or of the framework.

**Mathematical hypotheses.** The conditional deductions summarized here retain the choice hypotheses of their mathematical suppliers; in particular, the transverse free-field Fock supplier assumes Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice. [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]] record these assumptions.
items.physical_scope: The scope and empirical status of the photons and radiation modes page: the adopted radiation extension, the conditional results proved on the page with their units, and the physical comparisons, laboratory identifications and extensions that the page does not claim.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.3.6 printed pages 14-15 (PDF pages 22-23): photon polarisation, the agreement of the transmitted fraction with the classical Malus law, and the warning that the classical and quantum descriptions coincide in this respect

Skinner, Principles of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge Part II, Michaelmas 2021), Chapter 5 'Angular Momentum', printed page 15 footnote 55: the photon has two states and requires Lorentz-group representations, omitted from the non-relativistic course; Internet Archive copy of the original DAMTP-hosted Chapter 5 PDF

row.title: Qm Photons And Radiation Modes — Examples

items.title: Malus and Jones ratios of the declared analyser: the same cos^2 from the Born law and from a classical transverse amplitude
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$, orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$ and analyser projections
$P_{\theta}$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an angle
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. This example compares two declared models of the same
analyser:

**(a) The quantised-model ratio.** Consider the pure one-photon polarisation
preparation of the ray $[e_{1}]$ and the declared ideal analyser at angle
$\theta$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] the outcome law of
the analyser is
$$p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta,\qquad p_{-1}=\sin^{2}\theta,$$
so the **transmitted Born probability** is $\cos^{2}\theta$ in the unit $1$ of
dimensionless probabilities.

**(b) The declared classical transverse-amplitude model.** Declare the
following elementary model, with no claim that it is Maxwell theory: its
**field data** are complex vectors $E\in V$ whose coordinates are dimensionless
amplitude ratios relative to one fixed reference amplitude $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$;
no absolute field strength is assigned. The **analyser at angle $\theta$**
acts on the field data by the orthogonal projection
$$E\longmapsto P_{\theta}E;$$
the model's **declared dimensionless relative intensity** of a field datum is
$$I(E):=\|E\|^{2},$$
and the **transmitted intensity fraction** is $I(P_{\theta}E)/I(E)$ for
$E\ne0$.
This is a declared idealisation of the classical description of a
polariser as projecting the transverse field amplitude (the Jones-vector
reading); it imports no Maxwell equation and makes no detector claim.

The example computes both ratios for the same declared data and compares them.
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional model comparison on the declared fixed propagation-mode polarisation space: the Born probability cos^2(theta) of the quantised model's ideal analyser for the preparation along e_1, and the dimensionless relative-intensity ratio cos^2(theta) of a declared normalized classical transverse complex amplitude passed through the same projection. The example establishes that the two declared models agree on this ratio and asserts no field quantisation, no detector claim, no Maxwell derivation and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.3.6 printed pages 14-15 (PDF pages 22-23): the electric vector component transmitted by a polaroid with factor cos(theta), the energy fraction cos^2(theta), the individual-photon amplitude reading, and the remark that the transmitted fraction agrees with classical physics

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 3 'Linear algebra: vector spaces and operators', Section 5 'Orthonormal basis and orthogonal projectors': finite-dimensional orthogonal projection formulas, ranges and eigenspaces

items.title: Number statistics of a single declared mode: sharp, Poisson and geometric preparations
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ with
coordinate representatives in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ by clause (b)
of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]];
write $U=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] and let the dimensionless label
$z\in\mathbb C$ and a
**declared effective mode energy** $E_{0}>0$ in joules (equivalently a
declared effective frequency $\omega_{0}=E_{0}/\hbar>0$ in
$\mathrm s^{-1}$) be given parameters of this example. The example compares the
count statistics of the following three **declared preparations** of the mode
subspace, all read with the declared ideal total-number detector:

**(a) The $n$-quanta mode state.** For $n\in\mathbb N$, the pure preparation of
the ray of $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$.

**(b) The mode-coherent state.** The pure preparation of the ray of
$U\psi_{z}$, with dimensionless coherent-state label $z$ and
$\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{m}\frac{z^{m}}{\sqrt{m!}}e_{m}$.

**(c) The declared effective-energy mode preparation.** For a parameter
$\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$, the density operator
$$\rho_{\beta,E_{0}}:=(1-q)\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}q^{n}\,T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}},\qquad q:=e^{-\beta E_{0}}\in(0,1),$$
the transfer to the mode subspace of the single-mode weights of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] with its parameter
$\omega$ set equal to the declared effective energy $E_{0}$. This is
a declared conditional preparation of the model, not a derivation from any
radiation-matter interaction and not a statement that the mode is in thermal
equilibrium.

The example computes the count law, mean and variance of the three
preparations. It compares (b) and (c) at equal positive mean, and includes
(a) in that comparison when the common mean is a positive integer and $n$
is chosen equal to it.
items.physical_scope: A conditional computation of the count statistics of three declared preparations of one normalisable mode: the sharp count of an n-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law of the mode-coherent preparation, and the geometric count law of a declared effective-mode-energy Gibbs-type preparation. The example is conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model, declares its mode-energy parameter explicitly, records no measurement, no sampling model and no temperature identification, and asserts no thermalisation.

Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; retrieved via the Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 14 Section 14.2 printed pages 220-222: coherent states as eigenstates of the destruction operator, their normalization, and the mean and variance of the number operator in a coherent state

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50: number states with energy increment hbar*omega and coherent states with mean number |alpha|^2

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Section 1.2 printed pages 3-6 (PDF pages 4-7): occupation-number states, the number operator and single-mode oscillator algebra

items.title: A two-bin comparison of a declared classical field model and the quantised model: identical normalised laws do not discriminate
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate clause (i)
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the declared fixed-mode polarisation model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] with polarisation
space $V$ and orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable
Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Declare the following **two-bin comparison**:

1. an orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of $V$, read as the pair of orthogonal
   **fringe bin directions** of a declared two-bin detector, with projections
   $Q_{\pm}x:=\langle x,u_{\pm}\rangle u_{\pm}$;
2. a **declared amplitude datum** $a\in V\setminus\{0\}$ whose complex
   coordinates are dimensionless ratios relative to one fixed reference
   amplitude $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$; $a$ need not have unit norm;
3. the **declared classical field model**, whose state datum is the
   amplitude coordinate $a$ relative to $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$, whose dimensionless relative bin intensities are
   $I_{\pm}(a):=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}$, and whose
   normalised two-bin law is $I_{\pm}(a)/(I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a))$;
4. the **quantised model reading** of the same datum: the pure preparation of
   the ray $[a]$ of the polarisation space, measured by the declared ideal
   sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ declared directly in the sense of
   [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
   clause (a), with the Born law of P2. This arbitrary-bin sharp measurement
   need not belong to the real-angle analyser family of the original frame.

Then:

(a) $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$ and the normalised stated laws of the two declared models
coincide for every datum $a\ne0$:
$$\frac{I_{\pm}(a)}{I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a)}=p_{\pm}([a])=\frac{\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}}=\frac{|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}}{\|a\|^{2}};$$

(b) writing $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$ for any declared decomposition of the datum into
two **path components**, both declared laws contain the interference
cross-term
$$\frac{2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle\,\overline{\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle}\bigr)}{\|a\|^{2}},$$
so the presence of a fringe pattern of this two-bin form does not distinguish
the two declared models;

(c) the two declared models are nevertheless different physical models: in the
classical model the datum is a field amplitude with a deterministic intensity,
while in the quantised model it is a state ray with a Born law; a discriminator
requires a prediction on which two fully specified models differ, together
with a declared detector response, preparation and sampling model in the
sense of P7. Count statistics on a declared number-state preparation are a
candidate for a further comparison only after a classical field-and-detector
count law and the corresponding preparations in both models are declared.
The deterministic classical intensities do not supply that count law, so no
count-statistics discriminator follows from the present declarations;

(d) this item constructs no such discriminating comparison and reports no
data; it asserts no measurement, no count, no frequency and no empirical
conclusion, and it does not claim that the classical model agrees with the
quantised model beyond the declared two-bin law.
items.physical_scope: A conditional two-model comparison on a declared two-dimensional transverse amplitude space: the normalised two-bin laws assigned by a declared classical field model with dimensionless amplitude coordinates and relative intensity equal to squared amplitude norm, and by the quantised fixed-mode model with the Born law for the same declared bin projections. The result is that the normalised laws coincide for every declared amplitude, so such a pattern does not discriminate the two declared models; the thought experiment records the cross-term (interference) structure common to both and asserts no experiment, no counts, no detector response and no empirical conclusion.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.3.6 printed pages 14-15 (PDF pages 22-23): agreement of the quantum transmitted fraction with the classical description, and the distinct quantum and classical readings of complex amplitudes

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 3 'Linear algebra: vector spaces and operators', Section 5 'Orthonormal basis and orthogonal projectors': finite-dimensional orthogonal projection formulas, ranges and eigenspaces

items.title: Scope of the photons and radiation modes examples page
items.statement:
**What the three items establish.**
[[ex-nrqm-photons-malus-and-jones-analyzer-ratios]] shows that the Born
probability $\cos^{2}\theta$ of the declared ideal analyser on the preparation
along $e_{1}$ and the transmitted intensity fraction $\cos^{2}\theta$ of the
declared elementary classical transverse-amplitude model coincide for every
declared angle, so that this ratio alone does not establish field
quantisation. [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]]
computes the count laws and their means and variances for three declared
preparations of one mode -- sharp $n$, Poisson for dimensionless coherent-state
label $z$ with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$, and the geometric law of a declared
effective-energy preparation
with $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ joules and $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$, whose mean is
$1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)$ -- and shows different fluctuations for
the coherent and geometric preparations at equal positive mean. A number
state joins that equal-mean comparison when the common mean is a positive
integer and $n$ is chosen equal to it.
[[texp-nrqm-photons-classical-field-and-quantized-detection-comparison]]
proves that the declared classical and quantised models assign the same
normalised two-bin law, with the same interference cross-term, for every
declared amplitude datum, and concludes that a two-bin fringe law of that form
is not a discriminator between the two declared models.

**What they rest on.** All three items are conditional on the state and
composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the
adopted radiation extension and the declared fixed-mode or radiation-sector
vocabulary of the main page; the counting results use only the declared ideal
total-number detector of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. The
classical models appearing in the first and third items are explicit
elementary declared models -- dimensionless amplitude coordinates relative to
a fixed reference amplitude, with relative intensity equal to squared
amplitude norm -- and are not Maxwell's theory; the effective
mode energy $\varepsilon_{0}$ of the second item is a declared parameter, not a
sharp energy of a normalisable mode.

**Different objects.** A one-photon preparation is a unit ray of the
transverse one-particle space read in the one-photon sector; a mode-coherent
preparation is a unit ray of the radiation Fock space with no sharp number when $z\ne0$, while $z=0$ is the vacuum with sharp number zero;
and the declared classical intensity datum is a complex transverse amplitude
with its declared intensity. The three are distinct mathematical objects of
the declared models, and no identification of one with another is made.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no experiment, no apparatus, no
calibration, no measured count, no frequency, no efficiency and no uncertainty
budget, and none is invented. It does not claim that any laboratory polariser,
counter or interferometer realizes the declared ideal models; that claim is a
tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). It does not assert
thermal equilibrium or a temperature for the geometric preparation, and it
does not assert that the coincidence of the classical and quantum ratios is
evidence for field quantisation. Single-photon polarisation and counting
experiments remain research candidates for a separate reported-experiment
item; a finite sample of detections is a random object under any declared
sampling model, visible fringes can fail to appear with nonzero probability
under a correct coherent model, and a $p$-value or confidence level is not the
probability that a model is false. Comparing any of these conditional
predictions with data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions,
not prove the model or the framework.

**Mathematical hypotheses.** The conditional deductions summarized here retain the choice hypotheses of their mathematical suppliers; in particular, the transverse free-field Fock supplier assumes Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice. [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]] record these assumptions.

items.title: The first-order emitted-photon energy law: factorised kernel, normalisation, concentration at the transition energy and positivity on positive-measure windows
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb
C^{3})$ be the transverse space with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
let $\Lambda>0$, let $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) satisfy
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
let $\eta_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and let $c_{1},\dots,c_{J}\in\mathbb C$ with
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}g_{j}\in\mathfrak h .$$
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb R$ and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2}\ \ (t>0),$$
and the vector-valued function
$$A_{b}(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k)\int_{0}^{t} e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Clause (a) includes $M=0$ and every real $\eta_0$, including zero. Clauses (b)-(e) concern the normalized law when $M\ne0$; no nonzero assumption on $\eta_0$ is required. Then:

(a) (factorisation) for every $t>0$ and almost every $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$|A_{b}(k,t)|^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\,K_{t}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2},$$
and consequently
$\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}
K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$;

(b) (normalisation) if $M\ne0$, then for every $t>0$ the denominator
$\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$ is finite and strictly positive,
so
$$P_{t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)}$$
defines a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$P_{t}(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$;

(c) (concentration) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in
L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on
$\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, if $J_{b}$ is continuous at some $\Delta$ with
$0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, and if $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ is
continuous and bounded, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}f\,dP_{t}=f(\Delta);$$

(d) (positivity) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\ge0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere and $J_{b}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ of positive Lebesgue measure, then
$P_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$;

(e) (tail concentration) under the hypotheses of (c), for every $\delta>0$,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}P_{t}\bigl(\{E:|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}\bigr)=0$.

No dynamics, transition probability, rate, decay or physical identification is
asserted; the lemma computes an explicit kernel, its normalised push-forward
law and that law's limit.

items.title: The declared finite-level matter model and its cutoff dipole coupling to the transverse radiation sector
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], in the state
and outcome readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], in the radiation
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and in the units and dimensions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited Fock space
mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Finite-level matter factor.** Take the declared charged pair, the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate
multipliers $Q_{j}$ and the dipole operator components $D_{j}=-q\,Q_{j}$ of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii), with the Coulomb energy operator $H_{\kappa}$ of clause (iv) of that
postulate. Fix, as model data, a declared finite-dimensional subspace
$$W\subseteq D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap D(Q_{3}),\qquad \dim W=d<\infty,$$
with a declared orthonormal basis $(w_{1},\dots,w_{d})$ of $W$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and read $W$ as $\mathbb C^{d}$ in that basis. The model's **compressed matter
energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$
read in joules, where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); the model's **compressed dipole
matrices** are the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
read in $\mathrm{C\,m}$; and the model's **levels** are the pairs $(E,v)$ with
$E\in\mathbb R$ (joules) an eigenvalue of $H_{a}$ and $v\in\mathbb C^{d}$ a
nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair
$(a,b)$ of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},v_{b}$ of $H_{a}$; its **transition
energy** is $E_{a}-E_{b}$. The subspace, its basis and its dimension are model
data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this
pair.

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h$, the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, the
vacuum $\Omega$, the sector projections $\Pi_{n}$ and the free-field energy
observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]
clauses (b),(d), with the domains and self-adjointness of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in
joules. Fix, as further model data, a **cutoff** $\Lambda>0$ (joules), an
integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
For each radiation channel $j=1,\ldots,J$, declare real dimensionless weights $e_{j,i}$ ($i=1,2,3$) and define the Hermitian **channel dipole matrix**
$$D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}:=\sum_{i=1}^3 e_{j,i}D_i^W.$$
These are compressions of the actual real Cartesian dipole combination $\sum_i e_{j,i}D_i$ on $W$, so they have dipole units. This explicitly defines every channel even when $J>3$; the Cartesian case $J=3$, $e_{j,i}=\delta_{ji}$ is included. The weights are declared model data, with no assumed normalization or measured direction. Fix also a real **coupling number** $\eta_0$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
data; no laboratory mode content, no Maxwell field, no mode density and no
value of $\eta_{0}$ is asserted.

**(d) The coupled model.** Write $\phi(g):=A_{-}(g)+A_{+}(g)$ for the maximal
creation-annihilation sum of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] on
$F(\mathfrak h)$. The **declared finite-level cutoff dipole model** is the pair
of the Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and the operator
$$H_{\mathrm{LM}}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}+\eta_{0}\sum_{j=1}^{J}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_j), \qquad D(H_{\mathrm{LM}}):=\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f}).$$
For $d\ge1$, by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clause (c),
read with the Hermitian matrices $H_{a}$, $D_1^{\mathrm{ch}},\dots,D_J^{\mathrm{ch}}$ and the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ (its $d$ is the present $d$), the operator
$H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain and bounded below
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). If $d=0$, both the tensor-product Hilbert space and the displayed domain are $\{0\}$; $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is the unique operator on that space. Its adjoint is the same operator, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{LM}}0,0\rangle=0$, so it is self-adjoint and bounded below without invoking the positive-dimensional supplier. This degenerate case has no levels, level pairs or normalized preparations. For $d\ge1$, the model declares $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ its
**energy observable**, in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], with energies,
mode energies and the coupling read in joules.

**(e) The model's evolution and states.** The model's evolution is the
autonomous unitary family $U(t):=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}$, $t\in\mathbb R$,
in the reading of clause (ii) of P4 and of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; for $d\ge1$, a preparation $\rho$ of
the model is a state of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], with
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$, and the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_{A})$ is the reading of P2
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). No
measurement, no detector, no environment, no external field, no rate and no
record is part of this definition.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are adopted model data and readings. They assert
nothing about a laboratory atom, sample, mode content, cutoff or coupling; no
Maxwell equation, source model, back-reaction or propagation is assumed; the
truncation, the cutoff and the mode vectors are not derived; and no
identification of $\eta_{0}$ or of the $g_{j}$ with laboratory quantities is
made. The identification of a physical preparation with a state of this model
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The model contains no
photon detector, no sampling model, no environment beyond the declared
transverse modes, and no rate, decay or linewidth statement.
items.physical_scope: The declared finite-level cutoff dipole model: the compressed dipole matrices and compressed Coulomb energy of a declared finite-dimensional subspace of the two-body Coulomb relative-coordinate model, the bosonic transverse radiation sector of the adopted extension, the cutoff mode vectors g_j with 0 < epsilon <= Lambda and the bounded-relative coupling eta_0 sum_j D_j tensor phi(g_j) declared to be read in joules, together with the model's self-adjointness, its autonomous evolution and its state and outcome readings. The definition asserts no laboratory atom, field, mode cutoff or coupling value, no Maxwell equation, no derivation of the truncation, the cutoff or the coupling, no detector, no environment, no rate and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.3.2 printed pages 215-218 (PDF pages 223-226): the classical electromagnetic wave as a perturbation of the atomic Hamiltonian, the long-wavelength electric-dipole approximation and the transition rate proportional to the squared dipole matrix element

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50: the single electromagnetic field mode with field amplitudes q and p, the oscillator Hamiltonian and the identification of a classical field with an expectation value

S. Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 9 Section 9.2 printed pages 135-138 (mode expansion of the field operator) and Chapter 14 Section 14.3 printed page 221 (coupling to a classical current that is unaffected by the emission)

items.title: The declared prescribed dipole-drive model and its long-wavelength regime
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the static finite-level
dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(iv), in the state and outcome readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and in the units
of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Read the finite-level matter data of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (b): the
subspace $W\simeq\mathbb C^{d}$, the compressed matter energy $H_{a}$ (joules)
and the compressed dipole matrices $D^{W}_{1},D^{W}_{2},D^{W}_{3}$
($\mathrm{C\,m}$).

**(b) Prescribed field and its regime.** Fix a nonempty compact interval
$I=[t_{0},t_{1}]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds) and a
**prescribed electric field family** $t\mapsto\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)
=(E_{\mathrm{ext},1}(t),E_{\mathrm{ext},2}(t),E_{\mathrm{ext},3}(t))$, a
continuous map $I\to\mathbb R^{3}$ whose components are read in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. The field is prescribed: no Maxwell equation, source
model, propagation, back-reaction or feedback of the matter on the source is
assumed, and no claim is made that a laboratory arrangement realizes it.

**(c) The drive Hamiltonian.** The **declared dipole-drive model** is the
finite-dimensional family
$$H_{\mathrm d}(t):=H_{a}-\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)\,D^{W}_{j}, \qquad t\in I,$$
read as the model's energy in joules, on the matter factor $W\simeq\mathbb
C^{d}$; its **control** is the bounded self-adjoint family
$V(t):=-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)D^{W}_{j}$ with
$$\|V(t)\|\le\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}|E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2} \Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\|D^{W}_{j}\|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2}<\infty,$$
so $t\mapsto H_{\mathrm d}(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$
([[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). The model therefore
declares the driven model of
[[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (b)(i) in its
**bounded norm-continuous class**, with propagator $U(t,s)$ the unique
norm-continuous solution of the integral equation
$$U(t,s)=I-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^t H_{\mathrm d}(r)U(r,s)\,dr,\qquad U(s,s)=I,$$
constructed by the Dyson series of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]]. If $t_0<t_1$,
it satisfies $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H_{\mathrm d}(t)U(t,s)$ in operator
norm, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. If $t_0=t_1$, the
evolution declaration is only $U(t_0,t_0)=I$ and asserts no time derivative; state and
outcome readings are those of clauses (d)-(e) of the driven model, with level
populations read through the eigenbasis of $H_{a}$.

**(d) Long-wavelength regime.** Declare a **characteristic matter length** $L>0$ (metres), a reference point $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ (metres), a **wavevector** $k\in\mathbb R^3$ (inverse metres), and a dimensionless tolerance $0<\delta<1$ as model data. A prescribed spatial phase template for the field of clause (b) is the continuous map
$$\mathbf E^{\mathrm{sp}}:\mathbb R^3\times I\to\mathbb R^3,\qquad \mathbf E^{\mathrm{sp}}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)e^{ik\cdot(x-x_0)}\bigr),$$
with components in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, so $\mathbf E^{\mathrm{sp}}(x_0,t)=\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)$. This template specifies a spatial phase without assuming Maxwell dynamics or a dispersion relation. The **long-wavelength (electric-dipole) regime at tolerance $\delta$** means $|k|L\le\delta$: for $|x-x_0|\le L$, the phase obeys $|k\cdot(x-x_0)|\le\delta$. The model adopts the neglect of this spatial phase and uses the reference-point field in the interaction $-\sum_j E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)D_j^W$ of clause (c). The case $k=0$ is the spatially uniform template. The length $L$ is a declared scale, not a compact-support assertion for the matter wavefunctions. The notation $|k|L\ll1$ denotes choosing a small declared tolerance; no universal tolerance or error estimate for the induced quantum dynamics is asserted. This regime is an adopted model assumption, and identifications of $L$, $k$ and the field with laboratory data are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7.

**(e) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(d) are adopted model data and readings of a
declared finite-dimensional matter model with a prescribed classical field. The
model yields stimulated transition calculations through clause (c) and the
mathematics of the driven model; it contains **no quantized field, no photon
number, no vacuum state and no detector**, and a prescribed field of this kind
does not by itself supply spontaneous emission: the prescribed source is
unaffected by the matter's transitions, in contrast to the quantized
light-matter model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], where the
field's vacuum and the matter's change of level are one coupled model. No rate,
lifetime, linewidth, decay or empirical result is asserted.
items.physical_scope: The declared prescribed dipole-drive model of the finite-level Coulomb pair: a continuous prescribed electric field family E_ext on a compact time interval read in V m^-1, the bounded norm-continuous Hamiltonian H(t) = H_a - sum_j E_ext,j(t) D_j on the declared finite-dimensional matter factor, its norm-continuous bounded propagator, and the declared long-wavelength regime in which the phase variation of the field across the matter is neglected. The field is prescribed and unaffected by the matter; the definition asserts no Maxwell equation, no back-reaction, no propagation, no quantized field, no photon number, no detector, no spontaneous emission and no rate.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.3.2 printed pages 215-217 (PDF pages 223-225): the perturbation of an atom by a classical electromagnetic wave, the long-wavelength expansion of the phase factor and the electric-dipole interaction of the field with the atomic dipole
