canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]], and for $l\in\mathbb N$ and $0\le m\le l$ define the
function $w_{lm}:(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ by

$$w_{lm}(t):=(-1)^m(1-t^2)^{m/2}\,\frac{d^m}{dt^m}P_l(t),$$

where $(1-t^2)^{1/2}>0$ denotes the nonnegative square root. Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ and let the angle coordinates be $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$
([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]). The image of $\Phi$ is
$S^2\setminus C$, where $C:=\{(x,0,z)\in S^2:x\ge0\}$; $C$ is closed and $\sigma(C)=0$ by applying the integral identity of
[[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] to its indicator. For $l\ge m\ge0$, define the representative
$\widetilde Y_{lm}:S^2\to\mathbb C$ on $S^2\setminus C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)\frac{e^{im\varphi}}{\sqrt{2\pi}},$$
and on the cut $C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)/\sqrt{2\pi}\qquad(0\le\theta\le\pi).$$
The limits at $\varphi=0$ and $2\pi$ agree because $m$ is an integer, and the endpoint values of $w_{lm}$ from (a) give the limits at the poles; hence $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ is continuous. For $1\le m\le l$ set
$\widetilde Y_{l,-m}:=(-1)^m\overline{\widetilde Y_{lm}}$, and write $Y_{lm}$ for the class of $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) each $w_{lm}$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]$, with $w_{lm}(\pm1)=0$ when $m\ge1$, and on $(-1,1)$
it satisfies the associated Legendre equation
$$-\bigl((1-t^2)w_{lm}'\bigr)'+\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}w_{lm}=l(l+1)w_{lm}\qquad(-1<t<1),$$
equivalently $(1-t^2)w_{lm}''-2tw_{lm}'+\Bigl[l(l+1)-\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}\Bigr]w_{lm}=0$;

(b) for fixed $m\ge0$ the functions $w_{lm}$, $l\ge m$, are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2((-1,1),dt)$:
$\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}w_{km}\,dt=0$ for $k\ne l$; moreover $0<\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt<+\infty$;

(c) with $b_{lm}:=\bigl(\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt\bigr)^{-1/2}>0$ and the representatives just defined, one has
$|Y_{l,-m}|=|Y_{lm}|$ and
$\overline{Y_{lm}}=(-1)^mY_{l,-m}$ for all $l$ and all $m$ with $|m|\le l$;

(d) the family $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l\}$ is orthonormal in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]): for all $(l,m)\ne(l',m')$
with $|m|\le l$, $|m'|\le l'$, the integral $\int_{S^2}Y_{lm}\overline{Y_{l'm'}}\,d\sigma$ equals $0$, and it
equals $1$ when $(l,m)=(l',m')$;

(e) $w_{l0}=P_l$, and $w_{ll}(t)=(-1)^l\frac{(2l)!}{2^l l!}(1-t^2)^{l/2}$.

The functions $Y_{lm}$ are complex-valued $L^2$-functions on the sphere; no physical interpretation as angular
momentum eigenfunctions or spherical harmonics of an atom is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]] and $w_{lm}$ the associated functions of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]], and let $L^2=L^2((-1,1),dt;\mathbb C)$ with
inner product linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Then, for each fixed $m\in\mathbb N$:

(a) for every $l\ge m$ the polynomial $P_l^{(m)}$ has degree $l-m$ and nonzero leading coefficient, and for
every $d\in\mathbb N$ the polynomials $P_m^{(m)},P_{m+1}^{(m)},\dots,P_{m+d}^{(m)}$ form a basis of the space of
polynomial functions of degree at most $d$ on $[-1,1]$;

(b) the family $(w_{lm})_{l\ge m}$ has dense linear span in $L^2$: if $f\in L^2$ satisfies
$\int_{-1}^1f(t)w_{lm}(t)\,dt=0$ for every $l\ge m$, then $f=0$ almost everywhere; consequently the orthogonal
family $(w_{lm})_{l\ge m}$ is complete in $L^2$ and its normalization $(w_{lm}/\|w_{lm}\|_2)_{l\ge m}$ is a
Hilbert basis of $L^2$, so every $f\in L^2$ has
$f=\sum_{l\ge m}\bigl(\int_{-1}^1f\,w_{lm}\,dt\bigr)\|w_{lm}\|_2^{-2}w_{lm}$ with the finite-subset-net
convergence of [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]];

(c) for every fixed $m$ the orthogonal projection of $L^2$ onto the one-dimensional span of $w_{mm}$ is
$f\mapsto\|w_{mm}\|_2^{-2}\bigl(\int_{-1}^1f\,w_{mm}\,dt\bigr)w_{mm}$, and $w_{mm}(t)=(-1)^m\frac{(2m)!}{2^mm!}(1-t^2)^{m/2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]) and let $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l}$ be the
functions of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] ([[def-complex-exponential]]).
Then $(Y_{lm})$ is a complete orthonormal family of the complex Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]):
the family is orthonormal, and if $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ satisfies
$\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma=0$ for all $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, then $F=0$ almost everywhere.
Consequently every $F$ has the expansion
$$F=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},\qquad \|F\|^2=\sum_{l,m}|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2,$$
with $\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma$ and finite-subset-net convergence
([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real parameter $\hbar>0$. Let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ constructed in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and let
$H:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{lm}:-l\le m\le l,\ l\in\mathbb N\}$ be its algebraic (finite) span. Define operators
$A$ and $L_z$ on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ by the diagonal lemma
[[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]:

$$D(A):=\Bigl\{F:\sum_{l,m}l^2(l+1)^2\,|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad AF:=\sum_{l,m}l(l+1)\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},$$
$$D(L_z):=\Bigl\{F:\sum_{l,m}m^2\,|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad L_zF:=\sum_{l,m}\hbar m\,\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},$$

the sums being in the Hilbert-space norm ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Finally, for $F$ in the finite span
$H$, use the canonical continuous representatives $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ from
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]: set
$\widetilde F:=\sum_{l,m}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle\widetilde Y_{lm}$, a finite sum uniquely determined by the orthonormal coefficients. The same convention applies to $AF,L_zF\in H$. On the chart
$\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ with
$(\theta,\varphi)\in(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)$, write $F(\theta,\varphi):=\widetilde F(\Phi(\theta,\varphi))$ and put

$$(\mathcal S F)(\theta,\varphi):=-\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta\bigl(\sin\theta\,\partial_\theta F\bigr)(\theta,\varphi) -\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\varphi^2F(\theta,\varphi),\qquad (\mathcal D F)(\theta,\varphi):=-i\hbar\,\partial_\varphi F(\theta,\varphi),$$

where the partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then:

(a) $A$ and $L_z$ are self-adjoint operators on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with the displayed domains; on $Y_{lm}$ they
act by $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$ and $L_zY_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]); $A$ is nonnegative, $\langle AF,F\rangle\ge0$, and
$A\mathbf 1=0$;

(b) $H$ is a core of $A$ and of $L_z$: the finite truncations
$F_N:=\sum_{l\le N}\sum_{m}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$ of an element $F$ of $D(A)$ satisfy $F_N\to F$ and
$AF_N\to AF$ in $L^2$, and analogously with $L_z$;

(c) for every $F\in H$ and every chart point with $\sin\theta\ne0$,
$$\mathcal S F(\theta,\varphi)=(AF)(\theta,\varphi),\qquad \mathcal D F(\theta,\varphi)=(L_zF)(\theta,\varphi);$$

(d) for every $l$ the orthogonal projection $P_l$ of $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ onto the $(2l+1)$-dimensional span of
$Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}$, defined by $P_lF:=\sum_{m=-l}^l\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$ (the unique vector in that span with orthogonal residual), reduces both $A$ and $L_z$, i.e. $P_lA\subseteq AP_l$
and $P_lL_z\subseteq L_zP_l$; consequently $A$ and $L_z$ commute on the finite span $H$, and for every $F\in D(A)$ with
$\sum_{l,m}\bigl(l(l+1)\hbar m\bigr)^2|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2<\infty$ one has
$AL_zF=L_zAF=\sum_{l,m}l(l+1)\hbar m\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$. Writing $c_{lm}=\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle$ and $\lambda_l=l(l+1)$, the maximal product domains are $D(AL_z)=\{F\in L^2:\sum_{l,m}(\lambda_l\hbar m)^2|c_{lm}|^2<\infty\}$ and $D(L_zA)=D(A)\cap D(AL_z)$. Thus this is exactly the common domain $D(AL_z)\cap D(L_zA)=D(L_zA)$, while the two maximal product domains need not coincide. The product-weight condition alone does not imply $F\in D(A)$: the vector with coefficients $c_{l0}=1/l$ for $l\ge1$ and all other coefficients zero belongs to $L^2$, has zero product weight, but does not belong to $D(A)$. The product-weight condition is not automatic for all $F\in D(A)\cap D(L_z)$.

The differential expression $\mathcal S$ is evaluated only away from the poles, where the coordinate formulas are
defined; no claim is made about a maximal differential operator on all of $S^2$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, let
$\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), a finite Borel
measure with $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]]), and let
$L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ be the complex Hilbert space of equivalence classes of square-integrable functions with inner
product linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], [[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]). Let $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], put $V_l:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$ and let
$H$ be the algebraic span of all $Y_{lm}$. For $l\ge0$ let
$$H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}:=\{\,p:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C:\ p\ \text{is a homogeneous polynomial of degree } l \text{ with }\Delta p=0\,\}$$
be the complex vector space of harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$
([[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]],
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), let $\mathrm{res}_l:H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}\to L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ send $p$ to
the class of the restriction $p|_{S^2}$, and let $R\in SO(3)$ range over the special orthogonal group, a
subgroup of the general linear group with $R^{-1}=R^{\mathsf T}$ and unit operator norm, the set $M_3(\mathbb R)$
being identified with $\mathbb R^9$ and given the Euclidean metric ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]],
[[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]). For $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ define $U(R)F$ to be the class of the function
$\Omega\mapsto\tilde F(R^{-1}\Omega)$, where $\tilde F$ is any representative of $F$. Then:

(a) $U(R)$ is a well-defined $\mathbb C$-linear isometry of $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ onto itself with inverse
$U(R^{-1})$, hence a unitary operator ([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]);
$U(I_3)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ for all $R,S\in SO(3)$, so $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a group homomorphism
from $SO(3)$ into the group of unitary operators on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$;

(b) for every $R\in SO(3)$ and $p\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ one has $p\circ R^{-1}\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$; the map
$\rho(R):p\mapsto p\circ R^{-1}$ is a $\mathbb C$-linear automorphism of $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ with inverse
$\rho(R^{-1})$, and $\mathrm{res}_l(\rho(R)p)=U(R)\,\mathrm{res}_l(p)$; consequently $U(R)V_l=V_l$ for every
$l\ge0$, and $U(R)H=H$;

(c) (strong continuity) for every $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ and every $R_0\in SO(3)$, for every $\varepsilon>0$
there is $\delta>0$ such that $\|R-R_0\|_F<\delta$ for the Euclidean (Frobenius) norm on $M_3(\mathbb R)$
implies $\|U(R)F-U(R_0)F\|_2<\varepsilon$; thus every orbit map $R\mapsto U(R)F$ is continuous
([[def-metric-continuity]]). More precisely, if $P_NF:=\sum_{l\le N}\sum_{m}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm}$
denotes the orthogonal truncation of $F$ to $\bigoplus_{l\le N}V_l$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
then for all $R$
$$\|U(R)F-F\|_2\le 2\,\|F-P_NF\|_2+\|U(R)P_NF-P_NF\|_2 .$$

All assertions are mathematical statements about the action of $SO(3)$ on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical
interpretation of the rotation action is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-strongly-continuous-rotation-action]]: $S^2$, the polar measure $\sigma$ with
$\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, the Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$, the complete orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$, the blocks
$V_l$, the finite span $H$, the spaces $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree
$l$, the restriction maps $\mathrm{res}_l$, and the unitary action $U(R)F=\text{class of }\tilde F(R^{-1}\cdot)$
of $SO(3)$. Fix $\hbar>0$ and for $i=1,2,3$ define the rotation matrices
$$R_1(t):=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\cos t&-\sin t\\0&\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_2(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&0&\sin t\\0&1&0\\-\sin t&0&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_3(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t&0\\ \sin t&\cos t&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},$$
put $U_i(t):=U(R_i(t))$. Let $L_z$ denote the diagonal operator of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]], set $S:=R_2(-\pi/2)$, $W:=R_1(\pi/2)$,
and define
$$L_3:=L_z,\qquad L_1:=U(S)^{-1}L_zU(S),\qquad L_2:=U(W)^{-1}L_zU(W),$$
with domains $D(L_1)=U(S)^{-1}D(L_z)$, $D(L_2)=U(W)^{-1}D(L_z)$ and $D(L_3)=D(L_z)$.
Here $e^{-itL_z/\hbar}$ is the explicit diagonal unitary sending $Y_{lm}$ to $e^{-itm}Y_{lm}$;
$e^{-itL_1/\hbar}$ and $e^{-itL_2/\hbar}$ mean its conjugates by $U(S)$ and $U(W)$, respectively.
The proof identifies these operators with the complete strong derivative generators, so this construction
has the same generator meaning without an appeal to an unrestricted spectral or Stone theorem. For a polynomial $p$ put
$$D_ip:=(x\times\nabla p)_i=\sum_{j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\,x_j\,\partial_kp,$$
where $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(1,2,3)\mapsto(i,j,k)$ and is $0$ when two indices
coincide. Then:

(a) each $L_i$ is a self-adjoint operator on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with $U(R_i(t))=e^{-itL_i/\hbar}$ for all real
$t$; the finite span $H$ is contained in $D(L_i)$ and is a core of $L_i$
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);
and for $F\in V_l$ with polynomial representative $p_F\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ one has
$$L_iF=\mathrm{res}_l(-i\hbar\,D_ip_F),$$
that is, $(L_iF)(\Omega)=-i\hbar\,D_ip_F(\Omega)$ for $\sigma$-almost every $\Omega\in S^2$; in particular
$L_iY_{lm}\in V_l$ for all $l,m$ and $L_iH\subseteq H$;

(b) on $H$ the operators satisfy the commutation relations
$$L_iL_j-L_jL_i=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}L_k;$$

(c) $L_3=L_z$ as self-adjoint operators (equal domains and equal action); in particular $L_3Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$, so that
$L_3$ is diagonal in the basis $(Y_{lm})$, and for every $F\in H$ and chart point $(\theta,\varphi)$ one has $(L_3F)(\theta,\varphi)=-i\hbar\,\partial_\varphi F(\theta,\varphi)$;

(d) rotational conjugation identifies the domains: with the two quarter-turn rotations
$S:=R_2(-\pi/2)$ and $W:=R_1(\pi/2)$ one has
$$U(S)L_1U(S)^{-1}=L_3,\qquad U(W)L_2U(W)^{-1}=L_3,$$
as self-adjoint operators, and consequently $U(S)D(L_1)=D(L_3)$ and $U(W)D(L_2)=D(L_3)$: the three domains
are unitarily identified.

All assertions are mathematical statements about operators on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation of
the generators as angular momentum is asserted, and no measurement postulate is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]]: $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ with polar measure
$\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), the Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument, the complete orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]],
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks $V_l=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$ and
the finite span $H$, the spaces $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$,
and the polynomial representatives $h_{lm}\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of the $Y_{lm}$, characterized by
$\mathrm{res}_l(h_{lm})=Y_{lm}$ where $\mathrm{res}_l(p)$ is the class of $p|_{S^2}$
([[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]],
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Put $H_{-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}:=\{0\}$, fix $l\ge0$ and $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$,
write $\mathcal H:=h_{lm}$, and define the three polynomial multipliers
$$Q_0:=x_3,\qquad Q_\pm:=\frac{x_1\pm ix_2}{\sqrt2},$$
so that $Q_q=\sum_{i=1}^3c_{q,i}x_i$ with $c_{0,i}=\delta_{i3}$ and $c_{\pm,i}=(\delta_{i1}\pm
i\,\delta_{i2})/\sqrt2$. Let $D_i$ and $L_z,L_3$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]], where $L_3=L_z$ and $L_zY_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]). Then, for each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$:

(a) (harmonic decomposition) the polynomial $G_q:=\dfrac{\sum_ic_{q,i}\,\partial_i\mathcal H}{2l+1}$ lies in
$H_{l-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ and
$$Q_q\,\mathcal H=R_q+r^2G_q,\qquad R_q:=Q_q\mathcal H-r^2G_q\in H_{l+1}^{\mathrm{pol}},$$
where $r^2(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2$; for $l=0$ one has $G_q=0$ and $R_q=Q_q\mathcal H$;

(b) (degree selection) the function $Q_q|_{S^2}\cdot Y_{lm}$ lies in $V_{l+1}\oplus V_{l-1}$ (with
$V_{-1}:=\{0\}$); consequently, for all $l'\ge0$ and $m'\in\{-l',\dots,l'\}$,
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } l'\notin\{l-1,\,l+1\};$$

(c) (weight selection) as elements of $H\subset L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ one has
$$L_z\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr)=\hbar(m+q)\,\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr),$$
because $\partial_\varphi Q_q=iq\,Q_q$ on $S^2$ ([[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]],
[[def-complex-exponential]]); hence in addition
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } m'\ne m+q;$$

(d) (selection rules) combining (b) and (c): the angular matrix element
$\langle Y_{l'm'},\,Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\rangle$ can be nonzero only if
$$l'=l+1\ \text{and } m'=m+q,\qquad\text{or}\qquad l\ge1,\ l'=l-1\ \text{and } m'=m+q;$$
in particular only $\Delta l=\pm1$ and $\Delta m\in\{0,\pm1\}$ occur with the component-dependent shift
$\Delta m=q$ for the multiplier $Q_q$. These are necessary conditions on the angular integrals only: no
assertion is made that an allowed pair has a nonzero integral, and no absorption, emission or transition
probability is asserted or computed.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix complex
scalars. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, bounded or
unbounded, and write $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of
Lebesgue (equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with the inner
product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_Iu\overline v$ linear in the first argument
([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

**First-order space.** Define
$H^1(I):=\{u\in L^2(I;\mathbb C):\ \text{the weak derivative }Du\text{ of the class }u\text{ exists and }Du\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)\},$
where $Du$ is the weak derivative of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]: a class
$Du\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(I;\mathbb C)$ with
$\int_Iu\,\varphi'=(-1)\int_I(Du)\varphi\qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(I),$
an identity that is choice-free
([[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]]). Equip
$H^1(I)$ with the sesquilinear form
$\langle u,v\rangle_{H^1}:=\int_Iu\overline v+\int_I(Du)\overline{Dv},$
whose associated norm is $\|u\|_{H^1}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$;
the symbol $u'$ denotes the same weak derivative $Du$ throughout the page.

**Second-order space.** Define
$H^2(I):=\{u\in H^1(I):Du\in H^1(I)\},$
and for $u\in H^2(I)$ write $D^2u:=D(Du)\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)$; the norm is
$\|u\|_{H^2}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2+\|D^2u\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$.
Thus $H^2(I)$ consists exactly of the classes in $L^2(I)$ whose first and
second weak derivatives exist and lie in $L^2(I)$, and $H^2(I)\subseteq
H^1(I)$.

**Endpoint-vanishing first-order space and the Dirichlet form.** For the
bounded interval $(0,L)$, $L>0$, define
$H^1_0(0,L):=\overline{C_c^\infty(0,L)}^{\,\|\cdot\|_{H^1}},$
the closure of the test functions in $H^1(0,L)$, and define the **Dirichlet
form** on it by $q_D[u]:=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2=\int_0^L|Du|^2$.

**Elementary consequences, recorded for reuse.** Weak derivatives are unique
as locally integrable classes under Countable Choice, are additive and
$\mathbb C$-homogeneous, and classical derivatives of continuously
differentiable functions are weak derivatives. The cited published items
supply these facts, so $H^1(I)$ and $H^2(I)$ are well-defined linear
subspaces of $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$. No claim is made here that $H^1_0(0,L)$
equals the set of classes with vanishing endpoint values; that identification
is proved on this page from the trace estimates.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $-\infty<a<b<\infty$
and let $u\in H^1(a,b)$ have weak derivative $u'=Du$
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]). Then:

(a) there is exactly one representative $u^*$ of the class $u$ that is
continuous on $[a,b]$, is absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$, and satisfies
$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xu'(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in[a,b],$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side means $-\int_x^yu'$;

(b) for all $x,y\in[a,b]$,
$|u^*(x)-u^*(y)|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\;\|u'\|_{L^2(a,b)},$
so $u^*$ is uniformly continuous, and the assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear;

(c) if additionally $u\in H^2(a,b)$, then $(u^*)'$ is absolutely continuous
on $[a,b]$ and $(u^*)'(x)-(u^*)'(y)=\int_y^xD^2u$ for all $x,y\in[a,b]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $u^*$ denote the continuous absolutely
continuous representative of a class in $H^1$ supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]], and write
$\|u\|=\|u\|_{L^2}$ and $\|u'\|=\|u'\|_{L^2}$ for the norms of
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] on the interval under
consideration.

(a) *Bounded-interval trace bound.* Let $L>0$ and $u\in H^1(0,L)$. Then
$|u^*(x)|\le L^{-1/2}\|u\|_{L^2(0,L)}+L^{1/2}\|u'\|_{L^2(0,L)}
\qquad\text{for every }x\in[0,L].$
More generally, for $0\le c<d\le L$ and $x\in[c,d]$,
$|u^*(x)|\le(d-c)^{-1/2}\|u\|_{L^2(c,d)}+(d-c)^{1/2}\|u'\|_{L^2(c,d)} .$

(b) *Half-line.* Let $u\in H^1(0,\infty)$, with representative $u^*$ defined
on $[0,\infty)$ by gluing the representatives on $(0,n)$. Then
$|u^*(x)|\le\|u\|_{L^2(x,x+1)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(x,x+1)}\quad(x\ge0),\qquad
\sup_{x\ge0}|u^*(x)|\le\|u\|_{L^2(0,\infty)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(0,\infty)},$
and $u^*(x)\to0$ as $x\to\infty$.

(c) *Real line and vanishing boundary products.* Let $u,v\in H^1(\mathbb R)$
with continuous representatives $u^*,v^*$. Then $u^*,v^*$ are bounded and
uniformly continuous with
$|u^*(x)-u^*(y)|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\,\|u'\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)},\qquad
\sup_{\mathbb R}|u^*|\le\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)}+\|u'\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)},$
$u^*(x)\to0$ and $v^*(x)\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and consequently
$\lim_{|x|\to\infty}u^*(x)\overline{v^*(x)}=0$.

Assume the Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).
Use the spaces of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and the
absolutely continuous representatives supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].

(a) *Bounded intervals.* Let $0<L<\infty$ and $u,v\in H^1(0,L)$. Then
$\int_0^Lu\,\overline{v'}=u^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}
-\int_0^Lu'\,\overline v .$

(b) *Endpoint-vanishing space.* $H^1_0(0,L)=\{u\in H^1(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$,
with the traces $u^*(0),u^*(L)$ of the continuous representative.

(c) *Second-order identity.* For $u,v\in H^2(0,L)$,
$\int_0^L\bigl(u''\overline v-u\,\overline{v''}\bigr)
=\bigl[u'^*\overline{v^*}-u^*\overline{v'^*}\bigr]_0^L,$
where the bracket denotes
$u'^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(L)\overline{v'^*(L)}
-u'^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}+u^*(0)\overline{v'^*(0)}$.

(d) *Half-line and line.* If $u,v\in H^1(0,\infty)$, then
$\int_0^\infty u\overline{v'}=-u^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}-\int_0^\infty u'\overline v$, both integrals
being absolutely convergent. For $u,v\in H^1(\mathbb R)$ one instead has
$\int_{\mathbb R}u\overline{v'}=-\int_{\mathbb R}u'\overline v$,
with both integrals absolutely convergent.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$ be as in [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]].
Define, for $n\ge1$,
$e_n(x):=\sqrt{\frac2L}\,\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad x\in[0,L].$
Then $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ is an orthonormal family and a complete orthonormal
family (Hilbert basis) of $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]):
$\langle e_n,e_m\rangle=\delta_{nm},\qquad
\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:n\ge1\}=L^2(0,L;\mathbb C).$

Assume the Axioms of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $z\in\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$ and let
$k\in\mathbb C$ be the unique complex number with $k^2=-z$ and $\operatorname{Re}k>0$.
Put
$G_z(t):=\frac{1}{2k}e^{-k|t|}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$
and let $A_0$ be the free one-dimensional operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=1$, $c=4\pi^2$ and $b=0$: $D(A_0)=H^2(\mathbb R)$ and
$A_0u=-D^2u$ for every $u\in H^2(\mathbb R)$, where $D^2$ is the second weak
derivative of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Write
$\sigma:=\operatorname{Re}k>0$. Then:

(a) $G_z\in H^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^2(\mathbb R)$, its weak
derivative is the class of $t\mapsto-\tfrac12\operatorname{sgn}(t)e^{-k|t|}$,
and
$\|G_z\|_{L^1}=\frac{1}{|k|\sigma},\qquad
\|G_z\|_{L^2}=\frac{1}{2|k|\sqrt{\sigma}},\qquad
\|DG_z\|_{L^1}=\frac{1}{\sigma};$

(b) for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R)$ the convolution
$u:=G_z*f$, $u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(x-y)f(y)dy$, lies in $H^2(\mathbb R)$
with
$\|u\|_{L^2}\le\|G_z\|_{L^1}\|f\|_{L^2},\qquad
\|u\|_{L^\infty}\le\frac{1}{2|k|\sqrt\sigma}\|f\|_{L^2},$
and $A_0u-zu=f$;

(c) the linear map $R_0(z):L^2(\mathbb R)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$, $f\mapsto G_z*f$
is bounded with range exactly $H^2(\mathbb R)$, and
$(A_0-z)R_0(z)=I_{L^2},\qquad R_0(z)(A_0-z)=I_{H^2};$
in particular $R_0(z)=(A_0-z)^{-1}$ and $A_0-z$ is a bijection from $H^2(\mathbb R)$
onto $L^2(\mathbb R)$;

(d) $(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}-z)G_z=\delta_0$ in the sense of distributions: for
every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,
$\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(x)\bigl(-\varphi''(x)-z\varphi(x)\bigr)dx=\varphi(0).$

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let
$e_n(x)=\sqrt{\tfrac2L}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad
\lambda_n:=\Bigl(\frac{n\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2\quad(n\ge1),$
let $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]], and let $A_D$ be the diagonal
operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]
associated with $(e_n)$ and $(\lambda_n)$: $A_Dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n
\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n$ with domain
$D(A_D)=\Bigl\{x\in L^2(0,L;\mathbb C):\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$
Let $B$ be the Dirichlet Laplacian
$Bu:=-D^2u,\qquad D(B)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\},$
with $H^2$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D(A_D)=D(B)$ and $A_D=B$; in particular $D(A_D)$ is a linear subspace of
$H^2(0,L)$ whose members have vanishing endpoint traces;

(b) $A_D$ is self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]),
positive, and its spectrum is $\sigma(A_D)=\{\lambda_n:n\ge1\}$; each
$\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue with eigenvector $e_n$; the eigenvalues are
simple in the sense that $\ker(A_D-\lambda_n)$ contains no nonzero vector orthogonal
to $e_n$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_D)$, $\langle A_Du,u\rangle=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2$;
consequently $A_D\ge\lambda_1=(\pi/L)^2$ in the quadratic-form sense on its
domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on an
infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-dimension]]), let $c\in\mathbb R$ lie in the
resolvent set of $A$, and assume that the resolvent
$R_c:=(A-c)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then:

(a) $H$ has a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
eigenvectors of $A$; writing $\mu_n$ for the eigenvalue of $e_n$, one has
$|\mu_n|\to\infty$ (each eigenvalue repeated according to its finite
multiplicity), and every eigenspace of $A$ is finite dimensional;

(b) $\sigma(A)$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues $\mu_n$ of $A$ and has no
other points, and the essential spectrum is empty:
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]]); thus
every spectral point of $A$ is an isolated eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity;

(c) for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$ the resolvent $(A-z)^{-1}$ is
compact.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$. Put
$D_\theta:=\{u\in H^1(0,L):u^*(L)=e^{i\theta}u^*(0)\},\qquad
P_\theta u:=-i\,Du,$
with $H^1$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D_\theta$ is dense in $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, $P_\theta$ is symmetric and
self-adjoint;

(b) the functions
$\varphi_n(x):=\frac{1}{\sqrt L}e^{i(2\pi n+\theta)x/L}\qquad(n\in\mathbb Z)$
form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, each
$\varphi_n\in D_\theta$, and $P_\theta\varphi_n=\kappa_n\varphi_n$ with
$\kappa_n:=\frac{2\pi n+\theta}{L};$
the eigenvalues $\kappa_n$ are simple and
$\sigma(P_\theta)=\{\kappa_n:n\in\mathbb Z\}$;

(c) $P_\theta$ is the unique self-adjoint extension of the symmetric operator
$P_\theta$ restricted to the finite linear span of the $\varphi_n$, and its
domain is exactly
$D_\theta=\Bigl\{\sum_nc_n\varphi_n:\sum_n\kappa_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $A_D$ be the Dirichlet
Laplacian of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]] with
$D(A_D)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$ and $A_Du=-D^2u$, and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ with $\|V\|_\infty=\max_{[0,L]}|V|$. Let
$A:=A_D+M_V$ with domain $D(A):=D(A_D)$, where $(M_Vu)=Vu$ is multiplication
by $V$. Then:

(a) $M_V$ is bounded self-adjoint with $\|M_V\|=\|V\|_\infty$, $A$ is
self-adjoint on $D(A_D)$, and $Au=-D^2u+Vu$ for $u\in D(A_D)$;

(b) $A$ has compact resolvent: $(A-z)^{-1}$ is compact for every
$z\in\rho(A)$; consequently $A$ has a complete orthonormal family of
eigenvectors, all eigenspaces are finite dimensional, the eigenvalues
$E_1\le E_2\le\cdots$ (listed with multiplicity) satisfy $E_n\to\infty$ and
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(c) with $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$ and $E_n(A_D)=\lambda_n$, the min-max
eigenvalues satisfy
$\bigl|E_n-\lambda_n\bigr|\le\|V\|_\infty\qquad(n\ge1).$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb C)$ with $M:=\|V\|_{C^0}=\max_{[0,L]}|V|$. For
$z\in\mathbb C$, $x_0\in[0,L]$ and $c_0,c_1\in\mathbb C$ consider the
initial value problem
$\text{(IVP)}\qquad -u''+Vu=zu,\qquad u(x_0)=c_0,\quad u'(x_0)=c_1,$
for $u\in C^2([0,L];\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) (IVP) has exactly one solution $u(\cdot\,;z,x_0,c_0,c_1)$; it is the
unique continuous solution of the Volterra equation
$u(x)=c_0+c_1(x-x_0)+\int_{x_0}^x(x-t)\bigl(V(t)-z\bigr)u(t)\,dt
\qquad(x\in[0,L]),$
the integral over $[x_0,x]$ for $x<x_0$ carrying the negative orientation, and
$\sup_{[0,L]}|u|\le\bigl(|c_0|+|c_1|L\bigr)e^{(M+|z|)L^2};$

(b) for fixed $x_0,c_0,c_1$, put $p(x):=c_0+c_1(x-x_0)$ and, for
$f\in C([0,L];\mathbb C)$, define
$\mathcal K_zf(x):=\int_{x_0}^x(x-t)(V(t)-z)f(t)\,dt$. Then
$$u(x;z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(\mathcal K_z^np)(x)$$
and the termwise $x$-derivative series converge uniformly on
$[0,L]\times\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le R\}$ for every $R>0$. In particular,
$(x,z)\mapsto(u(x;z),u'(x;z))$ is continuous, and for each fixed $x$ both
$u(x;\cdot)$ and $u'(x;\cdot)$ are entire functions of $z$. The derivative
$w:=\partial_zu(\cdot\,;z)$ is the unique $C^2$ solution on $[0,L]$ of
$-w''+Vw-zw=u(\cdot\,;z),\qquad w(x_0)=0,\quad w'(x_0)=0 .$
It satisfies the associated Volterra equation
$w(x)=\int_{x_0}^x(x-t)\bigl[(V(t)-z)w(t)-u(t)\bigr]dt$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$. For $E\in\mathbb R$ let $u(\cdot,E)$ be the unique
$C^2$ solution of
$-u''+Vu=Eu,\qquad u(0,E)=0,\quad u'(0,E)=1,$
supplied by [[thm-nrqm-intervals-regular-ivp-parameter-series]] (with
$x_0=0$, $c_0=0$, $c_1=1$). Put
$r(x,E):=\bigl(u(x,E)^2+u'(x,E)^2\bigr)^{1/2}>0,\qquad
\theta(x,E):=\int_0^x\frac{u'(t,E)^2-u(t,E)u''(t,E)}{u(t,E)^2+u'(t,E)^2}\,dt .$
Then:

(a) $u=r\sin\theta$ and $u'=r\cos\theta$ on $[0,L]\times\mathbb R$, $\theta$ is
$C^1$ in $x$ with $\theta(0,E)=0$ and
$\partial_x\theta(x,E)=\cos^2\theta(x,E)+\bigl(E-V(x)\bigr)\sin^2\theta(x,E);$

(b) for every $x\in(0,L]$ the map $E\mapsto\theta(x,E)$ is differentiable on
$\mathbb R$ with
$\partial_E\theta(x,E)=\frac{\int_0^x u(t,E)^2\,dt}{u(x,E)^2+u'(x,E)^2}>0;$
in particular $E\mapsto\theta(L,E)$ is continuous and strictly increasing on
$\mathbb R$, and $E\mapsto\theta(x,E)$ is continuous on $[0,L]\times\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E$, $\theta(x,E)>0$ for $0<x\le L$; whenever
$\theta(x_0,E)=k\pi$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$ and $x_0\in(0,L]$, one has
$\partial_x\theta(x_0,E)=1$ and $\theta(x,E)>k\pi$ for all $x\in(x_0,L]$; if
additionally $0<k\pi<\theta(L,E)$, then the level $k\pi$ is attained at exactly
one point of $(0,L)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, with $V_{\min}:=\min_{[0,L]}V$ and
$V_{\max}:=\max_{[0,L]}V$. For $E\in\mathbb R$ let $u(\cdot,E)$ be the
solution of $-u''+Vu=Eu$, $u(0)=0$, $u'(0)=1$, and let $\theta(\cdot,E)$ be
its Prufer angle, as in [[thm-nrqm-intervals-prufer-energy-monotonicity]].
Call $E$ a **Dirichlet eigenvalue** when there is a nonzero
$w\in H^2(0,L)$ ([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with
$w^*(0)=w^*(L)=0$ satisfying $-w''+Vw=Ew$, $w^*$ the continuous
representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].
Then:

(a) $E$ is a Dirichlet eigenvalue if and only if $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ for some
integer $k\ge1$;

(b) for every $k\ge1$ the equation $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ has exactly one
solution $E_k$; the sequence $(E_k)_{k\ge1}$ is strictly increasing,
$E_k\to\infty$, and it is exactly the sequence of Dirichlet eigenvalues, each
with one-dimensional eigenspace:
$\ker(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}+V-E_k)=\mathbb Cu(\cdot,E_k)$;

(c) bounds: for every $k\ge1$,
$\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\min}\le E_k\le
\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\max};$

(d) nodal count: for every $E$, the number of zeros of $u(\cdot,E)$ in
$(0,L]$ equals $\lfloor\theta(L,E)/\pi\rfloor$; consequently the $k$-th
eigenfunction $u(\cdot,E_k)$ has exactly $k-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$, and the same
holds for every nonzero eigenfunction with eigenvalue $E_k$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. Let $D(A_\alpha)$ be
the set of classes $u\in H^1(\mathbb R)$ whose restrictions to $(0,\infty)$
and $(-\infty,0)$ have representatives of class $H^2$ on each half-line
([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) and which satisfy the
**interface condition**
$u'^*(0+)-u'^*(0-)=\alpha\,u^*(0),$
where $u^*$ is the continuous representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]
and $u'^*(0\pm)$ are the one-sided traces of the representative of the weak
derivative, which exist by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-endpoint-trace-and-half-line-decay]]. For
$u\in D(A_\alpha)$ define $A_\alpha u$ to be the class equal to $-D^2u$ on
each half-line. Then:

(a) $D(A_\alpha)$ is a dense linear subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$
and $A_\alpha:D(A_\alpha)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$ is a well-defined linear
operator;

(b) $A_\alpha$ is symmetric;

(c) $A_\alpha$ is self-adjoint; explicitly, for $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$
the operator $A_\alpha-z$ is a bijection $D(A_\alpha)\to L^2(\mathbb R)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and let $A_\alpha$ be the
self-adjoint delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]]; write $A_0$ for the
operator with $\alpha=0$, so that $D(A_0)=H^2(\mathbb R)$ and
$A_0u=-D^2u$. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$ let $k$ with $k^2=-z$,
$\operatorname{Re}k>0$, let $G_z(t)=(2k)^{-1}e^{-k|t|}$, and define the
bounded linear functional
$\ell_z(f):=\int_{\mathbb R}G_z(y)f(y)\,dy\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb R)).$
Then for every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$:

(a) $1+\alpha G_z(0)=1+\alpha/(2k)\ne0$, and
$(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}f=(A_0-z)^{-1}f-\frac{\alpha\,\ell_z(f)}{1+\alpha G_z(0)}\,G_z
\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb R));$

(b) the difference
$K_z:=(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}-(A_0-z)^{-1}$ is a bounded operator of rank at most one (rank one if $\alpha\ne0$, and zero if $\alpha=0$),
$K_zf=-\dfrac{\alpha}{1+\alpha G_z(0)}\,\ell_z(f)\,G_z$, its range is
contained in $\mathbb C G_z$, and
$\|K_z\|\le\frac{|\alpha|\,\|G_z\|_{L^2}^2}{|1+\alpha G_z(0)|}
=\frac{|\alpha|}{4|k|^2\operatorname{Re}k\,\bigl|1+\alpha/(2k)\bigr|}\,;$
consequently
$\bigl\|(A_\alpha-z)^{-1}\bigr\|\le
\bigl\|(A_0-z)^{-1}\bigr\|+\|K_z\| .$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and let $A_\alpha$ be the
self-adjoint delta interface operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-interface-operator]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) $A_\alpha$ has no negative eigenvalue when $\alpha\ge0$; and $E=0$ is
not an eigenvalue of $A_\alpha$ for any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$;

(b) if $\alpha<0$, then $E_\alpha:=-\alpha^2/4<0$ is an eigenvalue of
$A_\alpha$ with one-dimensional eigenspace
$\ker(A_\alpha-E_\alpha)=\mathbb C\,\psi_\alpha,\qquad
\psi_\alpha(x):=\sqrt{-\tfrac\alpha2}\,e^{\alpha|x|/2};$
the vector $\psi_\alpha$ satisfies $\|\psi_\alpha\|=1$, and $E_\alpha$ is the unique
negative eigenvalue, that is, if $E<0$ and $A_\alpha u=Eu$ for some
$0\ne u\in D(A_\alpha)$, then $E=E_\alpha$ and $u\in\mathbb C\psi_\alpha$;

(c) scaling: for any $\hbar,m>0$, the operator
$H_\alpha:=(\hbar^2/2m)A_\alpha$ on the same domain is self-adjoint,
and if $\alpha<0$, then
$H_\alpha\psi_\alpha=E_H\psi_\alpha$ with
$E_H=-\hbar^2\alpha^2/(8m)$; writing $g:=\hbar^2\alpha/(2m)$ gives
$E_H=-mg^2/(2\hbar^2)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
let $V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and put
$D(A):=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au:=-D^2u+Vu,$
with $H^2$, weak derivatives and traces as in
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]. Then:

(a) $D(A)$ is dense in $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, $A$ is well defined and
symmetric, and $A$ is self-adjoint;

(b) for every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$ there are unique $C^2$
solutions $u_a(\cdot,z)$ of $-u''+Vu=zu$ with
$u_a(0)=1$, $u_a'(0)=\alpha$, and $u_b(\cdot,z)$ with
$u_b(L)=1$, $u_b'(L)=\beta$; the Wronskian
$W(z):=u_a(x,z)u_b'(x,z)-u_a'(x,z)u_b(x,z)$
is independent of $x$ and $W(z)\ne0$;

(c) for $f\in L^2(0,L)$ the function
$u(x):=\int_0^LG_z(x,y)f(y)\,dy,\qquad
G_z(x,y):=-\frac{u_a(\min\{x,y\},z)\,u_b(\max\{x,y\},z)}{W(z)},$
lies in $H^2(0,L)$, satisfies the two Robin boundary conditions, and
$(A-z)u=f$. Consequently $(A-z)^{-1}f=u$, the resolvent is an integral
operator with continuous kernel $G_z$ on $[0,L]^2$, and $(A-z)^{-1}$ is a
compact operator for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and let $A$ be the Robin realisation of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green-resolvent]]:
$D(A)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au=-D^2u+Vu .$
Then:

(a) $A$ has compact resolvent; there is a complete orthonormal family
$(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$ of eigenvectors of $A$, every eigenspace of $A$ is
one-dimensional, and the spectrum of $A$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues
$\lambda_n$ of $A$, listed with multiplicity, which satisfy
$\lambda_n\to\infty$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(b) in particular the eigenvalues can be listed strictly increasingly as
$\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\cdots$ (each simple), and if $A\psi=\lambda\psi$ with
$\psi\ne0$, then $\psi$ is a nonzero multiple of the solution $u_a(\cdot,\lambda)$
of $-u''+Vu=\lambda u$, $u(0)=1$, $u'(0)=\alpha$, and the eigenvalue
condition is $\beta=\tfrac{u_a'(L,\lambda)}{u_a(L,\lambda)}$ when
$u_a(L,\lambda)\ne0$, while $u_a(L,\lambda)=0$ occurs for no eigenvalue.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, let
$U>E>0$ and $m,\hbar>0$, and put
$k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar}>0,\qquad
\kappa:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(U-E)}}{\hbar}>0 .$
Consider bounded functions $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ that are $C^1$ on
$\mathbb R$, twice continuously differentiable on each of $(-\infty,0)$,
$(0,a)$, $(a,\infty)$, and satisfy
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi,\qquad
V(x)=\begin{cases}U,&0<x<a,\\0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$
on each of the three intervals. Then:

(a) exactly one such $\psi$ has the *transmission asymptotics*: its
restriction to $(-\infty,0)$ equals $e^{ikx}+re^{-ikx}$ and its restriction
to $(a,\infty)$ equals $te^{ikx}$, for uniquely determined $r,t\in\mathbb C$;

(b) with $D:=2\cosh(\kappa a)+i\bigl(\tfrac{\kappa}{k}-\tfrac{k}{\kappa}\bigr)\sinh(\kappa a)$,
$t=\frac{2e^{-ika}}{D},\qquad
T:=|t|^2=\Bigl[1+\frac{U^2\sinh^2(\kappa a)}{4E(U-E)}\Bigr]^{-1},\qquad
R:=|r|^2=1-T ;$

(c) with $q:=e^{-2\kappa a}$, $C:=U^2/\bigl(4E(U-E)\bigr)$ and
$\delta:=\bigl(\tfrac4C-2\bigr)q+q^2$,
$T=\frac{(4/C)\,q}{1+\delta}$. Put
$\eta:=|\tfrac4C-2|q+q^2$. Whenever $\eta<1$,
$$\Bigl|T-\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\Bigr| \le\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\,\frac{\eta}{1-\eta}.$$
In addition, whenever $|\delta|\le\tfrac12$,
$$\Bigl|T-\frac{16E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\Bigr| \le\frac{32E(U-E)}{U^2}\,q\,|\delta|.$$

No $L^2$ normalisation is asserted: $\psi$ is a bounded generalised solution,
not an element of $L^2(\mathbb R)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $U>0$, $m,\hbar>0$ and put
$K:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar>0$. Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $V(x)=-U$ for
$|x|\le a$ and $V(x)=0$ for $|x|>a$, and let
$H\psi:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi,\qquad D(H):=H^2(\mathbb R),$
with $H^2$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb R)$;

(b) *root conditions.* $E\in\mathbb R$ with $-U<E<0$ is an eigenvalue of $H$
if and only if, writing $E=-\varepsilon$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m\varepsilon}/\hbar$
and $k:=\sqrt{2m(U-\varepsilon)}/\hbar$ (so that $k,\kappa>0$ and
$k^2+\kappa^2=K^2$), the pair $(k,\kappa)$ satisfies
$k\tan(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(even case)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad
-k\cot(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(odd case)} .$
Every such eigenvalue is simple, and its eigenfunction is, up to a nonzero
scalar, $x\mapsto\cos(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by $ce^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside
in the even case and $x\mapsto\sin(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by
$c\,\operatorname{sgn}(x)e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the odd case;

(c) *range of energies.* There are no eigenvalues $E\le-U$ and no eigenvalues
$E\ge0$; hence all eigenvalues of $H$ lie in $(-U,0)$ and are given by (b);

(d) *bound count.* The number of negative eigenvalues of $H$ equals
$\Bigl\lceil\frac{2aK}{\pi}\Bigr\rceil,$
and more precisely the equations of (b) have exactly one solution $k$ in each
interval $\bigl(\frac{n\pi}{2a},\frac{(n+1)\pi}{2a}\bigr)$, $n\ge0$, whose
left endpoint satisfies $\frac{n\pi}{2a}<K$, and no solution in $(0,K)$
elsewhere; the solutions are alternatively of even type ($n$ even) and odd
type ($n$ odd).

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of Lebesgue
(equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and write $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
for the same construction over the product with Lebesgue measure; identify
Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^6$ with the completion of the product of
Lebesgue measures on the two $\mathbb R^3$ factors.

**Kernel data and sections.** Let $k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, an almost-everywhere equivalence class, and choose a finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable representative $k_0:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C$. When $f\in L^2$ is used, choose likewise a finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable representative $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C$. For almost every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, the section $k_x(y):=k_0(x,y)$ is measurable, by applying the completed-product Fubini theorem to the positive and negative parts of the real and imaginary components of $k_0$ ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]).

**Domain and action.** For $f\in L^2$ say that the integral defining $T_kf$
*exists at* $x\in\mathbb R^3$ if the section product
$y\mapsto k_0(x,y)f_0(y)$ is measurable and lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, and at such points put
$$(T_kf)(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}k_0(x,y)f_0(y)\,dy .$$
Define
$$D(T_k):=\Bigl\{f\in L^2:\ x\mapsto(T_kf)(x)\ \text{exists for almost every }x\text{ and agrees a.e. with a class in }L^2\Bigr\},$$
and for $f\in D(T_k)$ let $T_kf$ denote that class. The assignment
$f\mapsto T_kf$ is called the *$L^2$-kernel operator with kernel $k$*.

This definition is independent of both representative choices. If $k_1$ is
another representative of $k$, its disagreement set with $k_0$ is null for the
completed product Lebesgue measure. Fubini applied to the indicator of that
set gives $k_0(x,\cdot)=k_1(x,\cdot)$ almost everywhere for almost every
$x$. For each such $x$ and any representative of $f$, the two section products
therefore have the same $L^1$ status and, when integrable, the same integral.
Replacing $f_0$ by another representative changes the section product only on
a null set of $y$, so it too preserves integrability and the integral.
Consequently the almost-everywhere sections, the subset $D(T_k)\subseteq L^2$,
and the resulting output class are unchanged by either representative choice.

**Hilbert-Schmidt operators.** A linear operator $T$ on $L^2$ is called a
*Hilbert-Schmidt operator* if there is
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with $D(T)=D(T_k)$ and
$T=T_k$; such a $k$ is called an *$L^2$ kernel* of $T$.

This definition asserts nothing about whether $D(T_k)$ is all of $L^2$,
whether $T_k$ is bounded, or whether $T_k$ is compact; those properties are
proved in [[lem-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators-bounded-and-compact]]. A
finite product kernel $\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ with
$f_i,g_i\in L^2$ is also a class in $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$,
as the same lemma records, so $T_k$ is defined for it whenever that membership
is used.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and let
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with $T_k$ the
$L^2$-kernel operator of [[def-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators]]. Then:

(a) $D(T_k)=L^2$; $T_k$ is linear and bounded with
$\|T_kf\|_2\le\|k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\|f\|_2$ for every
$f\in L^2$, so $\|T_k\|\le\|k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}$;

(b) if $n\ge1$, $f_1,\dots,f_n,g_1,\dots,g_n\in L^2$ and
$k(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ a.e., then $k$ is a class in
$L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, the range of $T_k$ is contained
in $\operatorname{span}\{f_1,\dots,f_n\}$, and $T_k$ is compact;

(c) $T_k$ is compact; and

(d) for every sequence $(k_m)$ in
$L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with
$\|k_m-k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\to0$ one has
$T_{k_m}-T_k=T_{k_m-k}$ and
$\|T_{k_m}-T_k\|\le\|k_m-k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\to0$; in
particular $T_k$ is the operator-norm limit of finite-rank kernel operators.

No statement is made about the spectrum of $T_k$, about its singular values,
or about $L^2$ kernels of a given compact operator.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V)$ and $(H,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_H)$ be
complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $i:V\to H$ be a linear map with dense
image.

**Symmetric forms.** A *sesquilinear form on $V$* is a map
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb C$ that is linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second; it is *symmetric* if
$a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$ for all $u,v\in V$, in which case $a(u,u)\in\mathbb R$
and $\operatorname{Re}a(u,v)=\operatorname{Re}\overline{a(v,u)}$.

**Bounded and semibounded.** Such a form is *bounded* if there is $C>0$ with
$|a(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ for all $u,v\in V$, and *semibounded below with
bound $M\ge0$* if $a(u,u)\ge-M\|i(u)\|_H^2$ for every $u\in V$.

**Form seminorm and closedness.** Let $M\ge0$ be a bound as above and define the
*form seminorm*
$$\|u\|_{a,M}:=\Bigl(\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+(M+1)\|i(u)\|_H^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\qquad(u\in V).$$
It is a seminorm because $a(u,v)+(M+1)\langle i(u),i(v)\rangle_H$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form; its Cauchy–Schwarz inequality follows by expanding its value on $u+tv$ and minimizing over the scalar $t$, and gives the triangle inequality. It need not separate points for a general dense-image map $i$. The form $a$ is *closed* if there are such an $M$ and constants $c,C>0$ with
$c\|u\|_V\le\|u\|_{a,M}\le C\|u\|_V$ for every $u\in V$; then
the form seminorm is a norm, and $(V,\|\cdot\|_{a,M})$ is complete because $V$ is. If $i$ is injective, it is already a norm before closedness, since its square is at least $\|i(u)\|_H^2$.

**Associated operator.** With $a$ and $i$ as above, define
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{u\in V:\ \text{there is }f\in H\text{ with }a(u,v)=\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H\text{ for every }v\in V\Bigr\},\qquad Au:=f .$$
The element $f$ is unique when it exists, because two candidates differ by an
element of $H$ orthogonal to the dense subspace $i(V)$, hence coincide;
$A$ is called the *operator associated with $a$*. This definition asserts
neither that $A$ is densely defined, nor that $A$ is symmetric, nor that $A$ is
self-adjoint or bounded below; the specific closed semibounded form of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] establishes those
properties for its own associated operator by a direct computation. When $V$
is a subspace of $H$ and $i$ is the inclusion, $\|i(u)\|_H$ is written
$\|u\|_H$ and the pairing $\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H$ is written
$\langle f,v\rangle$.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] with the weak gradient $\nabla u$ of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], write
$r(x):=|x|$, and write $\|u\|_2^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(x)|^2\,dx$ for the
$L^2$ norm of [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Then:

(a) for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\};\mathbb C)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{|u(x)|^2}{|x|^2}\,dx\le 4\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla u(x)|^2\,dx;$$

(b) the same inequality holds for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$;

(c) for every $u\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ the a.e.-defined function $x\mapsto u(x)/|x|$ lies in $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and satisfies $\|u/|\cdot|\|_2\le 2\|\nabla u\|_2$.

No constant smaller than $4$ is claimed, and no statement is made about
$\|u/|\cdot|\|_2$ for $u$ outside $W^{1,2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and let
$H_0:=-\Delta$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
with domain $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]): $H_0=\mathcal F_2^*M_{4\pi^2|\xi|^2}\mathcal F_2$
and $H_0u=-\Delta u$ for $u\in D(H_0)$, where $\Delta u$ is the distributional
Laplacian. Write $M$ for the multiplication operator
$$M u:=\frac{u}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(M):=\Bigl\{u\in H:\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\in H\Bigr\},$$
and write $\|u\|_2=\|u\|_H$. Then:

(a) for every $u\in D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ one has $u/|\cdot|\in L^2$ and

$$\Bigl\|\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\Bigr\|_2\le 2\sqrt{\|u\|_2\,\|\Delta u\|_2}\,,\qquad \Bigl\|\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\Bigr\|_2\le \eta\|\Delta u\|_2+\frac1\eta\|u\|_2\quad(\eta>0);$$

(b) $M$ is a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with $D(H_0)\subseteq D(M)$, symmetric on $D(H_0)$, with $H_0$-bound zero in the sense that for every $\eta>0$ the pair $(\eta,\eta^{-1})$ is admissible for $M$ relative to $H_0$;

(c) for every $\gamma>0$ the operator
$$C:=H_0-\gamma M,\qquad D(C):=D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),$$
is self-adjoint on $H$, bounded below, and acts by $Cu=-\Delta u-\gamma u/|\cdot|$ for every $u\in D(C)$; for every $\eta\in(0,1/\gamma)$ one has $C\ge-\gamma\eta^{-1}/(1-\gamma\eta)$ in the quadratic-form sense.

No sharp lower bound of $C$ is claimed here, and no physical interpretation of
$C$, $H_0$, $\gamma$ or $\Delta$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H_0=-\Delta$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
let $M u=u/|\cdot|$ be the multiplier of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with $D(M)\supseteq D(H_0)$,
and let $V:=-\gamma M$, so that $Vf=-\gamma f/|\cdot|$. For $z\notin\mathbb R$
write $R_0(z):=(H_0-z)^{-1}$
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[thm-self-adjoint-resolvent-estimate]]). Then:

(a) for every $z\notin\mathbb R$ there holds $R_0(z)=\mathcal F_2^*M_{m_z}\mathcal F_2$ with $m_z(\xi):=(4\pi^2|\xi|^2-z)^{-1}\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and $\|R_0(z)f\|_\infty\le\|m_z\|_2\|f\|_2$ for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(b) for every $z\notin\mathbb R$ there is $g_z\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with $R_0(z)f=g_z*f$ for every $f\in L^2$;

(c) for every bounded measurable $\chi$ with compact support the operator $M_\chi R_0(z)$ is Hilbert–Schmidt, hence compact;

(d) $V$ is $H_0$-compact ([[def-relative-compactness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]): $V$ is graph-norm bounded with respect to $H_0$ and $VR_0(z)$ is a compact operator for one, equivalently every, $z\notin\mathbb R$; explicitly $VR_0(z)=-\gamma M R_0(z)$ is compact.

No statement is made about compactness of $M$ itself, about point spectrum or
about any other spectral property of $H_0+V$; no physical interpretation is
asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H_0=-\Delta$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
let $M$ be the multiplier $Mu=u/|\cdot|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]], and let
$$C:=H_0-\gamma M,\qquad D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),$$
be the self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c).
Write $\sigma_{\mathrm d}$, $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}$, $E$ for the discrete
spectrum, essential spectrum and spectral projection valued measure of
[[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]] and
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. Then:

(a) $C$ is bounded below and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,+\infty)$;

(b) every point of $\sigma(C)\cap(-\infty,0)$ lies in $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(C)$: it is an eigenvalue of $C$ of finite multiplicity isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of such eigenvalues is at most countable;

(c) the negative spectral subspace $E((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ is the closed linear span of the eigenspaces of $C$ for its negative eigenvalues.

No claim is made about the multiplicity or the number of the negative
eigenvalues, about the nonnegative part of the spectrum beyond
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,\infty)$, or about any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), and let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
$L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]. Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with Lebesgue measure and inner product linear
in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$K:=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C\bigr)$$
be the Hilbert direct sum over $l\ge0$, $-l\le m\le l$. For $\psi\in L^2$ and
each $(l,m)$ define the coefficient function and the reduced function
$$c_{lm}(r):=\int_{S^2}\psi(r\Omega)\overline{Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\quad(r>0,\ \text{a.e.}),\qquad u_{lm}(r):=r\,c_{lm}(r).$$
Then:

(a) for every $\psi\in L^2$ and every $(l,m)$ the function $u_{lm}$ is a well-defined element of $L^2((0,\infty),dr)$ depending only on the class of $\psi$, and $U\psi:=(u_{lm})_{l,m}$ is a linear isometry of $L^2$ into (indeed onto) $K$ with
$$\|U\psi\|_K^2=\sum_{l\ge0}\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\int_0^\infty|u_{lm}(r)|^2\,dr=\|\psi\|_{L^2}^2;$$

(b) $U$ is unitary, and for every $(u_{lm})\in K$ the finite-subset sums $\sum_{l\le N,\,|m|\le l}u_{lm}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ converge in $L^2$ to a function $\psi$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$;

(c) on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ every $f\in C^2$ satisfies, in the notation $\partial_r f$, $\Delta_{S^2}f$ of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]],
$$\Delta f=\partial_r^2f+\frac2r\partial_rf+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2}f;$$

(d) for every $l\ge0$, $m$, and $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, the function $\psi:=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\subseteq H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, its image under $U$ is the finite-support vector with $(l,m)$-entry $u$, and
$$-\Delta\psi=\frac1r\Bigl(-u''(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\Bigr)Y_{lm}(\Omega),\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla\psi|^2\,dx=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr .$$

All statements are purely mathematical assertions about $L^2$ spaces, the
surface measure and the Laplacian; no physical interpretation and no statement
about operators with unbounded potentials is included.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, let
$C:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c) when $\gamma>0$, and the free Fourier multiplier when $\gamma=0$,
and let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$
onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr\bigr)$, with coefficients
$u_{lm}=r\,c_{lm}$. For $l\ge0$ let $V_l$ be the closure of
$C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$ in $L^2(0,\infty;\mathbb C)$ for the norm
$$\|u\|_{V_l}^2:=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2+|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr,$$
realized as the space of $u\in L^2$ with $u'-\frac ur\in L^2$ and
$\int|u|^2/r^2<\infty$ in the distributional sense
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and define
$$a_l(u,v):=\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\overline{\Bigl(v'(r)-\frac{v(r)}{r}\Bigr)}\Bigl(u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\overline{v(r)}-\frac{\gamma}{r}u(r)\overline{v(r)}\Bigr]dr .$$
Then:

(a) $V_l$ is a dense linear subspace of $L^2(0,\infty)$ that is a Hilbert space for $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$, the inclusion $V_l\hookrightarrow L^2(0,\infty)$ is continuous, and $a_l$ is a bounded symmetric sesquilinear form on $V_l$ that is closed and semibounded below;

(b) the operator $A_l$ defined by
$$D(A_l):=\Bigl\{u\in V_l:\exists\,f\in L^2(0,\infty)\ \text{with}\ a_l(u,v)=\langle f,v\rangle\ \forall v\in V_l\Bigr\},\qquad A_lu:=f,$$
is well defined, self-adjoint and bounded below; $D(A_l)$ is dense in $V_l$ in the norm $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$ and $a_l(u,u)=\langle A_lu,u\rangle$ for $u\in D(A_l)$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_l)$ the distributional identity $-u''+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)u=A_lu$ holds on $(0,\infty)$; consequently $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty)$, $u$ is of class $C^1$ with $u'$ locally absolutely continuous, and the identity holds pointwise almost everywhere on $(0,\infty)$; if moreover $A_lu=Eu$ for some constant $E\in\mathbb C$ (in particular if $u$ is an eigenfunction of $A_l$), then $u$ is of class $C^2$ on $(0,\infty)$ and the differential equation holds pointwise there;

(d) *block identity.* For $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$ one has $\psi\in D(C)$ if and only if $u_{lm}\in D(A_l)$ for every $(l,m)$ and $\sum_{l,m}\bigl(\|u_{lm}\|^2+\|A_lu_{lm}\|^2\bigr)<\infty$; then $U(C\psi)=(A_lu_{lm})_{l,m}$. Equivalently $UCU^*=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_l$ on $K$;

(e) *eigenfunction transport.* If $u\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu=Eu$ for some $E\in\mathbb R$, then the function $\psi(x):=u(r)Y_{l0}(\Omega)/r$ (with $x=r\Omega$) lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, satisfies $C\psi=E\psi$, and $r\mapsto u(r)/r$ is bounded on $(0,1]$; moreover $\psi$ is bounded and continuous on $\mathbb R^3$.

No endpoint boundary condition is imposed by hand: the domain $D(A_l)$ is the
form-domain realization transported from $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and no
physical interpretation of $A_l$, $C$, $U$ or $\gamma$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$,
$k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write
$$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$
and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let
$$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$
be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then:

(a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$;

(b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and
$$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$
is a $C^\infty$ solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ with $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$; it is, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, the only solution with $u(r)/r^{l+1}$ bounded as $r\downarrow0$; every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $c_1u_{\mathrm{reg}}+c_2u_2$ with $u_2$ defined near zero by $u_2(r):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)\int_{r_*}^r u_{\mathrm{reg}}(s)^{-2}ds$, where $0<r_*<\delta$ and $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has no zero in $(0,\delta)$, and extended uniquely to $(0,\infty)$ by the regular initial-value equation, and every solution that is not a multiple of $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has $|u(r)|/r$ unbounded as $r\downarrow0$;

(d) *termination.* $v$ is a polynomial if and only if $j\in\mathbb N_0$; in that case $v$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $L_j^{(2l+1)}$, and
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_j^{(2l+1)}(2kr)\quad(c\ne0)$$
lies in $L^2(0,\infty;dr)$;

(e) *eigenfunction.* If $j\in\mathbb N_0$ then $u_{\mathrm{reg}}\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu_{\mathrm{reg}}=-k^2u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; equivalently, for every $m$ the transported function $\psi(r\Omega):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap D(C)$ and satisfies $C\psi=-k^2\psi$.

The assertions are statements about the ordinary differential equation and
the operators $A_l,C$; no physical interpretation of $\gamma,k$ or of any
spectral level is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, and for
every $l\ge0$ let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]]; let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c),
with essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$
([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-essential-spectrum]]), and let $U$ be the polar unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] (d). Then:

(a) if $k>0$ and $j:=\gamma/(2k)-l-1\notin\mathbb N_0$, then the regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] is not square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$, and $-k^2$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$;

(b) the negative eigenvalues of $A_l$ are exactly the numbers
$$-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2},\qquad n\ge l+1,$$
each with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the corresponding regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; in particular every negative eigenvalue of $A_l$ is simple;

(c) the negative eigenvalues of $C$ are exactly the numbers $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ with $n\ge1$;

(d) every eigenfunction of $C$ with negative eigenvalue lies in the closed span of the transported regular solutions: if $C\psi=E\psi$ with $E<0$ and $U\psi=(u_{lm})$, then $E=-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ for some $n\ge1$, and each nonzero $u_{lm}$ is a scalar multiple of the regular solution of $A_l$ at that energy.

This exhausts the negative spectrum of $A_l$ and of $C$ by the terminating
Laguerre solutions; no claim is made here about completeness of these
eigenfunctions in the negative spectral subspace, about the multiplicity of
the levels of $C$, or about any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$ and let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$. For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$ and
$-l\le m\le l$ let $u_{nl}$ be the regular solution of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] at $k=\gamma/(2n)$
(the polynomial-exponential solution, unique up to a nonzero scalar), and put
$$\psi_{nlm}(x):=\frac{u_{nl}(r)}{r}Y_{lm}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega).$$
Then:

(a) each $\psi_{nlm}$ lies in $D(C)$ and $C\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\psi_{nlm}$; the vectors $\psi_{nlm}$ with distinct labels are pairwise orthogonal, and for fixed $n$ the eigenspace of $C$ at $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ is exactly their span; it has dimension $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^2$;

(b) after normalization, the family $(\psi_{nlm}/\|u_{nl}\|_2)_{n\ge1,0\le l\le n-1,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace $E_C((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(c) the family is not complete in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$: the nonnegative spectral subspace $E_C([0,\infty))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is nonzero (indeed infinite dimensional), so the bound states alone do not span $L^2$.

All claims concern the mathematical spectral decomposition of $C$; no physical
interpretation is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above,
and put $a_0:=2/\gamma>0$. Define
$$\psi_{100}(x):=\Bigl(\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}\Bigr)^{1/2}e^{-r/a_0}\quad(x=r\Omega,\ r=|x|).$$
Then:

(a) $\psi_{100}\in D(C)$, $\|\psi_{100}\|_{L^2}=1$, and $C\psi_{100}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4}\psi_{100}$;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, writing $dx$ for Lebesgue measure,
$$\int_B|\psi_{100}(x)|^2dx=\int_0^\infty\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}r^2e^{-2r/a_0}\Bigl(\int_{S^2}\mathbf1_B(r\Omega)d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr,$$
so the radial probability density $p(r):=\frac{\gamma^3}{2}r^2e^{-2r/a_0}=4r^2a_0^{-3}e^{-2r/a_0}$ is a probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p\ge0$ and $\int_0^\infty p(r)dr=1$;

(c) the mean of $p$ is $\int_0^\infty r\,p(r)dr=3a_0/2$, and the unique maximum (mode) of $p$ is at $r=a_0$;

(d) the spatial density $|\psi_{100}(x)|^2=\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}e^{-2r/a_0}$ is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at $x=0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a remainder $R_\varepsilon$ such that
$$
\int_{|x|<\varepsilon}|\psi_{100}(x)|^2\,dx=\frac16\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_0}\Bigr)^3+R_\varepsilon, \qquad |R_\varepsilon|\le\frac18\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_0}\Bigr)^4.
$$
Thus this probability is positive and tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and the spatial probability measure has no point atoms, including at the density maximum $x=0$;

(e) *parametrisation and dimensions.* If $\hbar,m,\kappa>0$ and $\gamma:=2m\kappa/\hbar^2$, then $a_0=\hbar^2/(m\kappa)$ and the operator
$$
C_{\hbar,m,\kappa}:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta-\frac{\kappa}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(C_{\hbar,m,\kappa})=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),
$$
has eigenvalues $-\frac{m\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2n^2}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Bigl(-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\Bigr)$ ($n\ge1$); under the dimensional conventions $[\hbar]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[m]=\mathrm{kg}$, $[\kappa]=\mathrm{J\,m}$, the constants $a_0^2$ and $m\kappa^2/(2\hbar^2)$ have the dimensions of $\mathrm m^2$ and $\mathrm J$ respectively.

Clauses (a)–(d) are mathematical statements about the normalised ground vector
and its distribution; clause (e) is a dimensional-consistency statement about
the parametrisation and is not a physical claim, measurement or identification
of any quantity with nature.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator with spectral projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel
$\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $c>0$. Write $cA$ for the operator
with $D(cA):=D(A)$ and $(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$, and for $m_{c}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
$m_{c}(\lambda):=c\lambda$, define
$$F(B):=E\bigl(m_{c}^{-1}(B)\bigr)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
Then:

(a) $F$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$;

(b) for every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the bounded integrals
satisfy $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f\circ m_{c})$, and the operator
$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)$ of the spectral theorem equals $cA$ with
domain $D(A)$;

(c) consequently $F$ is the spectral projection valued measure $E_{cA}$ of
$cA$: for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{cA}(B)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr);$$in particular the negative spectral subspaces agree,$$E_{cA}\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H=E\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H .$$

The assertion transfers the spectral measure along positive scaling of the
operator. It asserts no spectral type of a particular operator, no multiplicity
statement and no physical interpretation; $c<0$ is not covered, and no
statement is made about unbounded Borel functions of $cA$ beyond the identity
functional calculus stated in (b).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m_1,m_2>0$, put
$M:=m_1+m_2$, $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$, let $\kappa>0$, $\hbar>0$, and define the
linear coordinate map
$$\Phi:\mathbb R^6\to\mathbb R^6,\qquad \Phi(x_1,x_2):=\Bigl(R,r\Bigr),\qquad R:=\frac{m_1x_1+m_2x_2}{M},\quad r:=x_1-x_2,$$
with inverse $x_1=R+\frac{m_2}{M}r$, $x_2=R-\frac{m_1}{M}r$. Write $L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ and for $f\in L^2$ put $(U_\Phi f)(R,r):=f(x_1,x_2)$ with $x_i$ expressed through $(R,r)$. Then:

(a) $\Phi$ is a linear isomorphism with $|\det\Phi|=1$, and $U_\Phi$ is a unitary operator on $L^2$;

(b) for every Schwartz function $f$, $U_\Phi(-(\hbar^2/2m_1)\Delta_{x_1}-(\hbar^2/2m_2)\Delta_{x_2})U_\Phi^{-1}f=(-(\hbar^2/2M)\Delta_R-(\hbar^2/2\mu)\Delta_r)f$; moreover both sides define the same self-adjoint operator on the common domain $H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$;

(c) the operator $H_2:=-(\hbar^2/2m_1)\Delta_{x_1}-(\hbar^2/2m_2)\Delta_{x_2}-\kappa/|x_1-x_2|$ with $D(H_2):=H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ is self-adjoint, and $U_\Phi H_2U_\Phi^{-1}=T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu$ under the identification $L^2(\mathbb R^6)\cong L^2(\mathbb R^3_R)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3_r)$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], where $T_R:=-(\hbar^2/2M)\Delta_R$ and $C_\mu:=-(\hbar^2/2\mu)\Delta_r-\kappa/|\cdot|$;

(d) $\sigma(H_2)=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2},\infty)$, and $H_2$ has no eigenvalues at all: the negative part of its spectrum is the interval $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2},0)$, consisting entirely of continuous spectrum, and each relative bound-state energy $-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2n^2}$ of $C_\mu$ is a threshold of the continuous spectrum of $H_2$ rather than an eigenvalue; in particular a relative bound state tensored with any centre-of-mass state is not an eigenvector of $H_2$;

(e) On $L^2(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C)$ define the centre-of-mass momentum component
$$
P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}:=\frac{\hbar}{i}\partial_{R_j},\qquad D(P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}):=\{g\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}g\in L^2\text{ as a weak derivative}\}.
$$
On the full two-body space define its lift
$$
\widetilde P_{R,j}:=U_\Phi^{-1}(P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}\otimes I)U_\Phi,\qquad D(\widetilde P_{R,j}):=U_\Phi^{-1}\{F\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R\times\mathbb R^3_r;\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}F\in L^2\text{ as a weak derivative}\}.
$$
Each $\widetilde P_{R,j}$ is self-adjoint and has no nonzero eigenvectors in $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$; hence there is no normalisable state of definite total momentum (a simultaneous eigenvector of the three lifted components).

All statements are mathematical statements about the operators on $L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ and the coordinate map; no physical interpretation, no identification of $m_1,m_2,\kappa,\hbar$ with measured constants, and no claim about nature is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above, let
$(\psi_{nlm})$ be the bound eigenfunctions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]], and for
$i=1,2,3$ define the coordinate multiplication operator
$$Q_i\psi:=(\xi\mapsto\xi_i\,\psi(\xi)),\qquad D(Q_i):=\{\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C):\xi_i\psi\in L^2\}.$$
Write also $Q_0:=x_3$ and $Q_\pm:=(x_1\pm ix_2)/\sqrt2$. Then:

(a) each $Q_i$ is self-adjoint on $D(Q_i)$, the domain is a proper dense subspace of $L^2$, and every bound state satisfies $\psi_{nlm}\in D(Q_i)$, with $\|Q_i\psi_{nlm}\|_2^2=\int_0^\infty r^2|u_{nl}(r)|^2dr\cdot\int_{S^2}|\Omega_iY_{lm}(\Omega)|^2d\sigma(\Omega)<\infty$;

(b) for all labels and each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the matrix element $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ is absolutely convergent and factors as
$$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle=\Bigl(\int_0^\infty r\,u_{n'l'}(r)\overline{u_{nl}(r)}\,dr\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_{S^2}Y_{l'm'}(\Omega)\overline{Q_q(\Omega)\,Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr),$$
where $Q_q(\Omega)$ denotes the restriction of the polynomial $Q_q$ to $S^2$;

(c) the angular factor vanishes unless $l'=l+1,\ m'=m+q$ or $l\ge1,\ l'=l-1,\ m'=m+q$; these are necessary conditions only: no assertion is made that an allowed pair has nonzero radial integral, and no transition probability is asserted or computed;

(d) for the oscillator: with $\omega>0$, $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, the complete orthonormal family $(\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}})$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] and the position operator $X$ (multiplication by $\ell y$ in the scaled variable) one has
$$X\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}^{\mathrm{osc}}+\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}^{\mathrm{osc}}\bigr),$$
