Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared isolated system of the massive-matter sector ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a)), and let
$$U(t)=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda),\qquad \psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0),\qquad \rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$$
be the flow and the state evolutions of clauses (b) and (c) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], with $\hbar>0$ and the energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) **Unitary flow.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$; every orbit has constant norm, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$, so for $\psi(0)\ne0$ the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation of the model for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

(b) **Domain invariance.** $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $t$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$: the flow preserves the energy domain and commutes with the energy there.

(c) **Schroedinger equation on the domain.** For $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ is norm-differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, it stays in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0);$$
for $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve is norm-differentiable at no $t\in\mathbb R$, so the equation is not asserted there, although the evolution $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ remains continuous.

(d) **Density-operator evolution.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every $t$ the operator $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is again a preparation: self-adjoint, positive, trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover for every bounded operator $B$ the identity $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$ holds.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They assert no evolution for a prescribed time-dependent Hamiltonian, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement, apparatus or detector model, no claim that any laboratory system is isolated, and no empirical result.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ as in [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable: $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ is self-adjoint everywhere defined ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then:

(a) **The Heisenberg representative is an assigned sharp observable.** For every $t$, $A_H(t)$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|A_H(t)\|=\|A\|$ and spectrum $\sigma(A_H(t))=\sigma(A)$, and its spectral projection-valued measure is
$$E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$
with the declared unit $u_A$ it is again a bounded assigned sharp observable of the framework, and $A_H(0)=A$.

(b) **The two pictures assign the same laws.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_H(t)}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
where $\mu^{\cdot}_{\cdot}$ is the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$; for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ this reads $\|E_A(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_{A_H(t)}(B)\psi\|^{2}$. In particular the expectation value of the bounded observable agrees, $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)A_H(t)\bigr)$.

(c) **Heisenberg equation.** If $A\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, then for every $x\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto A_H(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=\bigl[A_H(t),H_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr]x=\bigl(A_H(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}-H_{\mathrm{op}}A_H(t)\bigr)x .$$

(d) **Energy-compatible observables are frozen.** If $A$ is compatible with the energy, that is $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel $B,C$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)), then $A_H(t)=A$ for every $t$, and by (b) the outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is the same in $\rho(t)$ as in $\rho(0)$ for every preparation.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They introduce no new physical assumption, no measurement or apparatus model, no collapse, no driven or open dynamics; they make no claim about which laboratory quantity realizes $(A,u_A)$ and record no empirical result.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and write $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. Then:

(a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\ne0$ and $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and second moment of the energy law of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent. For any nonzero representative $\psi(0)$ their time-zero values are
$$\frac{\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}},$$
respectively. The displayed conservation of moments makes no assertion that these moments are finite for preparations outside this domain hypothesis.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(c) **Stationary states are exactly the eigenrays.** Let $\psi\in H$, $\psi\ne0$. The pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, if and only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $\psi\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. In that case $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi(0)$ for every $t$, and every assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law in this preparation: $\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\mu^{A}_{[\psi(0)]}(B)$ for every $(A,u_A)$, every Borel $B$ and every $t$.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** No equilibration, relaxation, decay or convergence of the law of an arbitrary preparation is asserted; no moment beyond those finite at time zero is claimed; the converse of (b) — constancy of the law of a bounded observable in every preparation implying strong spectral compatibility with the energy — is not asserted for a general (possibly unbounded) $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; and the item is conditional on the isolated-system idealization of P4, asserting no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

**What the page adopts.** The single physical assumption materialized here is the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), read in the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for an isolated system of the framework with state space of the type fixed by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. In particular the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$, its energy unit and the reduced Planck constant entering the phase are model specifications in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; no numerical value of any of them is produced by this page.

**What is proved.** [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] draws, from P4 and the local mathematics [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]], the unitary flow, the invariance of the energy domain, the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation and the evolution of density-operator preparations. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]], using [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]], identifies the Heisenberg representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable and proves that the two pictures assign the same outcome laws, together with the domain-qualified Heisenberg equation and the freezing of energy-compatible bounded observables. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] reads the conservation of the energy law and its finite moments, the conservation of any bounded energy-compatible observable, and the equivalence of stationary pure preparations with the eigenrays of the energy; the mathematical core of that equivalence is [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-ray-characterization]]. All statements are conditional consequences of the adopted postulates and the cited mathematics; none of them is an empirical claim.

**What is not claimed.** (i) The page treats only the autonomous case: a prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ and the propagator problems it raises are not covered by P4(ii) and are deferred to the driven-dynamics development, and an open or reduced non-unitary evolution is an extension requiring an environment model, in the sense of clauses (iv) and (v) of P4. (ii) No measurement, collapse, conditioning or apparatus model is introduced; the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] is used only to read statistics of a preparation, and the state after an outcome is not treated. (iii) No relaxation, equilibration or convergence of the law of a general preparation is asserted. (iv) The converse of the conservation criterion — that a bounded observable whose law is constant in every preparation must be strongly spectrally compatible with the energy — is not proved for a general possibly unbounded $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and is therefore not claimed. (v) The equation of motion is asserted exactly on the operator domain; for vectors outside the domain only the unitary flow, not the differential equation, is available.

**Empirical status.** Whether a concrete laboratory system realizes P4's isolated-system idealization, and whether a concrete apparatus realizes a preparation of the type used here, are tested identifications with uncertainty, in the sense of the framework's preparation and apparatus assumptions; they are not consequences of P4. This pair records no measurement, apparatus, calibration or data, and the worked companion page contains finite model computations only.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited definitions of the adjoint. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, let
$H_{1},\dots,H_{r}$ be complex Hilbert spaces with inner products linear in the
first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$H:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H_{l},\qquad \bigl\langle (x_{l}),(y_{l})\bigr\rangle:=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle x_{l},y_{l}\rangle_{H_{l}},$$
be their orthogonal sum. For each $l$ let $A_{l}:D(A_{l})\subset H_{l}\to H_{l}$
be a densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and put
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{(x_{l})\in H:\ x_{l}\in D(A_{l})\ \text{for all }l,\ \sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad A(x_{l}):=(A_{l}x_{l}).$$
Then:

(a) $H$ is a complex Hilbert space, $D(A)$ is a dense linear subspace of $H$,
and $A:D(A)\to H$ is a linear operator;

(b) $A$ is symmetric and self-adjoint, and
$\|Ax\|^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}$ for every $x\in D(A)$;

(c) if $B_{l}\in\mathcal B(H_{l})$ for every $l$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), then $B:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}$, defined
by $B(x_{l}):=(B_{l}x_{l})$ for all $(x_{l})\in H$, is bounded with
$$\|B\|=\max_{1\le l\le r}\|B_{l}\|$$
([[def-operator-norm]]), its adjoint is
$B^{*}=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and $B$
is unitary if every $B_{l}$ is unitary.

No assertion is made about infinite orthogonal sums: only the finite case is
proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers
$d\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $H:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with the Euclidean
integral pairing ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]), let
$$H^{(r)}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr),\qquad \langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}(x)\overline{g_{l}(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $\mathbb C^{r}$ carry the standard inner product with orthonormal basis
$e_{1},\dots,e_{r}$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
Write $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ for the completed tensor product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] with inclusion $\kappa$.
Then:

(a) the map
$$\Psi_{0}\Bigl((f_{l})\Bigr):=\bigl(x\mapsto(f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{r}(x))\bigr)$$
is a well-defined unitary isomorphism $\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H\to H^{(r)}$, and
$$\|\Psi_{0}(f)\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|f_{l}\|_{H}^{2},\qquad \langle\Psi_{0}(f),\Psi_{0}(g)\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle f_{l},g_{l}\rangle_{H};$$

(b) the assignment on elementary tensors
$\Theta_{0}(\kappa(u\otimes e_{l})):=\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)$ is
the $r$-tuple with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere, extends uniquely to a
surjective linear isometry $\Theta:H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}\to H^{(r)}$
(so $\Theta$ is unitary), and
$\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=\sum_{l=1}^{r}z_{l}\,\iota_{l}(u)$ for all
$u\in H$, $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$;

(c) for every $a\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d})$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^{d}$ one
has the intertwining identities
$$\Theta^{-1}\bigl(a\cdot\Theta(w)\bigr)=(M_{a}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w,\qquad \Theta^{-1}\bigl(T_{v}^{(r)}\Theta(w)\bigr)=(T_{v}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w\qquad(w\in H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}),$$
where $M_{a}$ is multiplication by $a$, $T_{v}$ is the Euclidean translation
$T_{v}h:=h(\cdot-v)$ of [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]
clause (c), $T_{v}^{(r)}$ is its componentwise action on $H^{(r)}$, and the
bounded amplifications are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with
the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let
$\mathcal S^{(r)}:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise
Schwartz class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and let $\Psi_{0}$
and $\Theta$ be the unitaries of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]. For
$S=(S_{lm})\in M_{r}(\mathbb C)$ write
$$S_{\times}f:=\Bigl(\sum_{m=1}^{r}S_{lm}f_{m}\Bigr)_{l}\qquad(f\in H^{(r)}).$$
Then:

(a) $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all $j,k$,
$Q_{j}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$P_{k}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$, and on $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the
canonical commutation relations hold:
$$(Q_{j}P_{k}-P_{k}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,\delta_{jk}f\qquad(f\in\mathcal S^{(r)});$$

(b) $S_{\times}$ is bounded with $\|S_{\times}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$
([[def-operator-norm]]), and
$$S_{\times}D(Q_{j})\subseteq D(Q_{j}),\quad Q_{j}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}Q_{j}f\ (f\in D(Q_{j})),\qquad S_{\times}D(P_{k})\subseteq D(P_{k}),\quad P_{k}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}P_{k}f\ (f\in D(P_{k}));$$

(c) the spectral projection-valued measures of $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}},\qquad E_{P_{k}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)*}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}\in B\}}}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)} \qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
where $M_{g}$ is multiplication by $g$; consequently
$S_{\times}E_{Q_{j}}(B)=E_{Q_{j}}(B)S_{\times}$ and
$S_{\times}E_{P_{k}}(B)=E_{P_{k}}(B)S_{\times}$ for every Borel $B$, and for
unitary $V\in U(r)$ and every $f\in H^{(r)}$
$$\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)f\bigr\|,\qquad \bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)f\bigr\|;$$

(d) under the tensor identification $\Theta$ the operator $S_{\times}$
corresponds to the bounded amplification $I\otimes S$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], that is
$\Theta^{-1}S_{\times}\Theta=I\otimes S$; in particular the internal-factor
operators commute with the spatial ones in the sense of (b).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. For translations by $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and boosts with parameter $u\in\mathbb R^3$, choose the componentwise representative convention
$$(T_a\psi)(x)=\psi(x-a),\qquad (B_u(t)\psi)(x)=\exp\!\left(\frac{i}{\hbar}\left(mu\cdot x-\tfrac12m|u|^2t\right)\right)\psi(x-ut).$$
Here $a$ is length-valued, $u$ velocity-valued and $t$ time-valued, so the phase is dimensionless. These formulas specify classes almost everywhere and are chosen model conventions. The covariance theorems of this page derive operator and outcome-law identities conditional on these choices; they do not derive the choice of representative convention itself. No Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert

([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]

model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none

[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics

the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter

([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],

[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of

transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its

the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;

zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value

$$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k};$$

$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j}),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B):$$
translating the preparation by $a$ translates the position law by $a$ and
leaves every momentum law unchanged;

(c) **Dynamics covariance.** With $H_{V}$ and $H_{V_{a}}$ the energy operators
of the potentials $V$ and $V_{a}$,
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},\qquad T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
in particular, if $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ (equivalently

([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, let
$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and flow
$U_{0}(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, and for real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ let $H_{V}$ and $U_{V}$ be the operator and flow of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]], with
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and
$V_{u}(x,t):=V(x-ut)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$ define the
**boost operator** $B_{u}(t)$ componentwise by
$$\bigl(B_{u}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\Bigl(\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl(m\,u\cdot x -\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}t\Bigr)\Bigr)\psi(x-ut).$$
Then:

(a) for every $u,t$ the operator $B_{u}(t)$ is unitary,
$B_{u}(t)^{-1}=B_{u}(t)^{*}$, and it maps $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ onto themselves;

(b) $B_{u}(t)D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ and $B_{u}(t)D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$; for
$f\in D(Q_{j})$ and $g\in D(P_{k})$, respectively,
$$Q_{j}B_{u}(t)f=B_{u}(t)(Q_{j}+u_{j}tI)f,\qquad P_{k}B_{u}(t)g=B_{u}(t)(P_{k}+mu_{k}I)g.$$
For a Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and
$a\in\mathbb R$, write $B-a:=\{b-a:b\in B\}$. Consequently, for every
unit $\psi$ and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-u_{j}t),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B-mu_{k});$$

(c) **free covariance.** $B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t-s)=U_{0}(t-s)B_{u}(s)$ for all
$s,t\in\mathbb R$; in particular the freely evolved boosted preparation equals
the boost at time $t$ of the initial boosted preparation,
$$B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t)\psi=U_{0}(t)B_{u}(0)\psi\qquad(\psi\in H_{s});$$
and the conjugated free Hamiltonian identity
$$B_{u}(t)^{-1}H_{0}B_{u}(t)=H_{0}+u\cdot P+\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}I$$
holds on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ (in the chart velocity
$v=-u$ of clause (e) it reads $H_{0}-v\cdot P+\frac{m|v|^{2}}{2}I$), the
operator form of the frame change on the free generator;

(d) **moving-frame bounded-potential model.** For every real bounded
measurable $V$ and every $u$, the two-parameter family
$$W_{u}(t,s):=B_{u}(t)\,U_{V}(t-s)\,B_{u}(s)^{-1}$$
consists of unitaries preserving $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi_{0}\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
the curve $t\mapsto W_{u}(t,s)\psi_{0}$ takes values in $W^{2,2}$, is
differentiable as an $L^{2}$-valued curve and satisfies
$$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V_{u}(\cdot,t)}\Bigr)\psi(t),\qquad \psi(s)=\psi_{0};$$
it is unique among maps $w:\mathbb R\to W^{2,2}$ that are differentiable
into $L^{2}$ and satisfy this equation in $L^{2}$ for every $t$ with
$w(s)=\psi_{0}$;

(e) **Frame reading and scope.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+ut$ of P5 (the new chart moves with velocity $-u$ relative to the
old one) on state representatives by $\psi'(x',t)=(B_{u}(t)\psi(\cdot,t))(x')$;
clauses (b)-(d) are the covariance consequences of that reading for the laws
of the free model and for the bounded-potential dynamics in the moving frame.
The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics,
concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded measurable
potentials only, and asserts no Lorentz covariance, no photon limit, no
covariance for singular or unbounded potentials and no worldline of an
unmeasured particle; no apparatus or empirical result is recorded.

## What the pair establishes

The items of this pair are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics. [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
founds the spin-$s$ model on the state space $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] proves that these
operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains and provides the Fourier
representation and the translation identities;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] proves the
canonical commutation relations on the Schwartz core, identifies the spectral
measures and proves that the internal factor commutes with the spatial
measures; [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] constructs the
momentum representation;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] derives the position and momentum
outcome laws of the spin-$s$ model, including the Born density
$\|\psi(x)\|^{2}_{\mathbb C^{2s+1}}$ and the momentum density
$\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}$;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-boost-covariance]] establish the covariance of these
laws and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the Galilean translations and
boosts of the model's frame class. All of this is conditional on P1, P2, P4,
P5 and P6 and on the cited mathematical suppliers; none of it is a statement
that any physical system is exactly described by the model.

## Empirical status of the parameters

The mass parameter $m>0$ and the spin label $s$ are model parameters: within
the framework they are declared values, and the identical-particle and spin
postulate assigns to a species its mass, spin, statistics and couplings as
empirical model parameters with uncertainty. This pair derives no value of
$m$ or $s$, records no measurement and asserts no species identification; the
units in which $m$, $\hbar$, $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are read are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the exact defining constants
of the current SI recorded there are unit conventions, not measurements of
this framework.

## What is not claimed

The outcome laws are sharp-law statements: an exact position or momentum value
has probability zero in every preparation, finite-resolution outcomes are
Borel bins, and no detector, efficiency, resolution or sampling model is
introduced. The covariance theorems hold for the free model and for real
bounded measurable potentials; they assert nothing for singular or unbounded
potentials, confined or boundary realizations, massless particles, radiation
or relativistic matter. The internal factor is bookkeeping: it is not
identified with a spatial rotation, a classical angular momentum or a
relativistic spinor, and no empirical consequence of the spin assignment alone
is derived. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ with concrete
laboratory procedures remains a tested identification under the preparation
and apparatus postulate, external to this pair.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited Hilbert-space and measure suppliers. Let
$(D,\mathcal A,dx)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space ([[def-measure]]), let
$r\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$$L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r}):=\Bigl\{f:D\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality $dx$-almost everywhere
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), with
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{D}\langle f(x),g(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad \|f\|^{2}:=\langle f,f\rangle=\int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).
For $a,b\in L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r})$ and measurable $B\subseteq D$ write
$$\langle a,b\rangle_{B}:=\int_{B}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad N:=\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2},\qquad c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{D}.$$
Then:

(a) *Pointwise and integrated cross term.* For $dx$-almost every $x\in D$,
$$\|a(x)+b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}=\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}},$$
and for every measurable $B\subseteq D$, the three functions $\|a\|^{2}$,
$\|b\|^{2}$, $\langle a,b\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ being $dx$-integrable on $B$,
$$\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx=\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx+\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{B}.$$

(b) *Coherent bin law.* If $\|a+b\|>0$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B):=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a+b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
([[def-probability-measure]]), and for every $B\in\mathcal A$ the expansion of
(a) holds with $\|a+b\|^{2}=N+2c$ in the denominator.

(c) *Incoherent bin law.* If $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and $w\in[0,1]$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.

(d) *Recorded weights, sub-probability and conditioning.* Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$ and let $W:D\to[0,1]$ be measurable.
Then $B\mapsto\nu(B):=\int_{B}W\,d\mu$ is a finite measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
with $0\le\nu(D)\le1$; if $\nu(D)>0$, then
$\bar\nu(B):=\nu(B)/\nu(D)$ defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.
More generally, for finitely many measurable weights $W_{1},\dots,W_{m}:D\to[0,1]$
with $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}\le1$ pointwise, the numbers
$\nu_{a}:=\int_{D}W_{a}\,d\mu$ satisfy $\nu_{a}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}\le1$; if $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}=1$ pointwise, then
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}=1$.

(e) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and $\|a+b\|>0$, and put
$w_{*}:=\|a\|^{2}/N$, so that $p_{\mathrm{mix}}$ with weight $w_{*}$ is
$p_{*}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}\bigl(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2}\bigr)dx$. Then
$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{*}(B)$ for every $B\in\mathcal A$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for }dx\text{-almost every }x\in D .$$
In particular, if $\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost every
$x$, then the two laws coincide; and if $c=0$, then they coincide if and only
if $\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost
every $x$.

The assertions concern the specified classes and weights only; no probability
law of an apparatus, no sample of trials and no empirical claim is asserted.

**(a) Framework data and state convention.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
one-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle and spin postulate P6,
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $r:=2s+1$, and fix a mass parameter
$m>0$. P5 assigns the one-particle state space
$$H_s:=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$$
with almost-everywhere equivalence classes and pairing
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{l=1}^r f_l(x)\overline{g_l(x)}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). P1 identifies a pure
preparation with the ray $[\psi]:=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a
unit vector $\psi$ and a general preparation with a density operator, meaning a
bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Write
$$D(H_s):=\{\rho:\rho\text{ is a bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator on }H_s\text{ and }\operatorname{tr}\rho=1\}$$
for the set of general preparations.

For a unit vector $u$, define $P_uf:=\langle f,u\rangle u$. By Cauchy--Schwarz
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]),
$\|P_uf\|=|\langle f,u\rangle|\le\|f\|$, so $P_u$ is bounded. Then
$P_u^2=P_u$ and $P_u$ is self-adjoint because for $f,g\in H_s$,
$\langle P_uf,g\rangle=\langle f,u\rangle\langle u,g\rangle
=\langle f,P_ug\rangle$. Moreover
$\langle P_uf,f\rangle=|\langle f,u\rangle|^2\ge0$ by the inner-product
identities and $\langle u,u\rangle=1$. Its range is $\mathbb C u$, so it has
finite rank and is trace class by [[def-trace-class-operator]]. The one-term
nuclear representation $P_uf=\langle f,u\rangle u$ gives
$\operatorname{tr}P_u=\langle u,u\rangle=1$ by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Thus $P_u$ is a
density operator. For $\psi\ne0$ define
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=P_{\psi/\|\psi\|},\qquad \widehat\rho(\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{\|\psi\|^2}.$$
For every nonzero scalar $z$, conjugate-linearity in the second argument and
$\|z\psi\|^2=|z|^2\|\psi\|^2$ give
$$\widehat\rho(z\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,z\psi\rangle z\psi}{\|z\psi\|^2}=\frac{|z|^2\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{|z|^2\|\psi\|^2}=\widehat\rho(\psi)f,$$
so the pure density operator depends only on the ray.

**Position PVM and Born-density calculation.** P5 assigns the componentwise
position operators $Q_jf=x_jf$ on
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in H_s:x_jf\in H_s\},\qquad j=1,2,3.$$
Each $Q_j$ is self-adjoint on this domain. To see density, for $f\in H_s$ put
$f_n=\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}f$; then $f_n\in D(Q_j)$ and $f_n\to f$ in
$H_s$ by dominated convergence. If $f,g\in D(Q_j)$, then
$\langle Q_jf,g\rangle=\langle f,Q_jg\rangle$ because $x_j$ is real-valued
and both products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz. If $g\in D(Q_j^*)$ with
$Q_j^*g=h$, let $E_n=\{x:|x_j|\le n\}$. For every $q\in H_s$ supported in
$E_n$, one has $q\in D(Q_j)$ and
$\langle q,(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}\rangle=0$ by the defining adjoint
identity. The vector $(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}$ lies in $H_s$ because $x_j$
is bounded on $E_n$; taking it for $q$ shows $x_jg=h$ almost everywhere on
$E_n$. Since $E_n\uparrow\mathbb R^3$, $x_jg=h\in H_s$ almost everywhere,
so $g\in D(Q_j)$ and $Q_j^*g=Q_jg$. Symmetry gives the reverse domain
inclusion; hence $Q_j=Q_j^*$ by
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]].

For a Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, define the indicator multiplication
operator $M_{\mathbf 1_S}:H_s\to H_s$ by
$(M_{\mathbf 1_S}f)(x):=\mathbf 1_S(x)f(x)$ almost everywhere. This is
independent of the representative of the $L^2$ class and is bounded, since
$$\|M_{\mathbf 1_S}f\|^2=\int_S\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|f\|^2.$$
It is linear and a bounded operator with bound one
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). It is an orthogonal projection:
$\mathbf 1_S^2=\mathbf 1_S$ and the real indicator multiplier is
self-adjoint for the declared pairing.

For Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, define
$$E_j(C):=M_{\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}}.$$
Each value is a bounded orthogonal projection since
$\|\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}f\|\le\|f\|$, and
$E_j(\varnothing)=0$,
$E_j(\mathbb R)=I$, and $E_j(C\cap D)=E_j(C)E_j(D)$. For a disjoint sequence
$(C_n)$ with union $C$, the squared norm of
$E_j(C)f-\sum_{n\le N}E_j(C_n)f$ equals
$$\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\setminus\cup_{n\le N}C_n\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
which tends to zero by dominated convergence; hence $E_j$ is strongly
countably additive. Its scalar measures are finite Borel measures
$$\langle E_j(C)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
and are regular on $\mathbb R$ by
[[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]]. The
push-forward integral identity
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g(\lambda)d\langle E_j(\lambda)f,f\rangle =\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(x_j)\|f(x)\|^2dx$$
holds first for indicators and nonnegative simple functions and then for
nonnegative measurable $g$ by monotone convergence. In particular the domain
of $\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)$ is exactly $D(Q_j)$ by the same identity
with $g(\lambda)=\lambda^2$. For bounded Borel $g$, the bounded PVM calculus
equals multiplication by $g(x_j)$: this holds for indicators by the
definition of $E_j$, for finite simple functions by linearity, and for bounded
Borel functions by uniform simple approximation and the norm bound of the
bounded calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Therefore the
truncations of the unbounded integral are multiplication by
$x_j\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}$. For $f\in D(Q_j)$ these converge in $H_s$
to $x_jf$, since the squared tail norm is
$\int_{\{|x_j|>n\}}x_j^2\|f(x)\|^2dx\to0$ by dominated convergence. Thus
$\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)=Q_j$ on exactly $D(Q_j)$, and the regular spectral
theorem identifies $E_j$ as the spectral PVM of $Q_j$
([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

Define the joint position PVM by
$$G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_B}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$
For each $f$, $\|G(B)f\|\le\|f\|$, so its values are bounded; indicator
multiplication gives its projection, identity, and intersection laws. Strong
countable additivity follows from dominated convergence applied to $\|f\|^2$.
Its scalar measures are $B\mapsto\int_B\|f(x)\|^2dx$, finite
regular Borel measures on $\mathbb R^3$. On coordinate rectangles,
$$G(C_1\times C_2\times C_3)=E_1(C_1)E_2(C_2)E_3(C_3).$$
The rectangles generate $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^3)$; the published Borel-product
and finite-measure uniqueness theorems show that these rectangle values
uniquely determine the joint PVM ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]],
[[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]],
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]): for any two candidate PVMs,
their finite scalar measures agree on the generating rectangles and on the
whole space, so they agree on every Borel set; the polarization identity in
the last lemma then gives equality of the operator values. This constructs the
mathematical joint position PVM; a physical joint detector reading is supplied
only for the finite effect families declared below. For a density operator
$\rho$ define
$\mu^G_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$ for each Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Since $G$ is a PVM, this set function is a probability
measure by the general density/PVM calculation used in clause (ii) of P2. For a
finite Borel partition $(B_a)_{a=1}^m$,
the operators $G(B_a)$ are orthogonal projections and sum to $I$. For each
$f\in H_s$,
$\langle G(B_a)f,f\rangle=\|G(B_a)f\|^2\in[0,\|f\|^2]$, so they are
bounded effects with $0\le G(B_a)\le I$ in quadratic-form order. Clause (iv)
of P2 therefore assigns the channel probabilities
$p_a(\rho)=\mu^G_\rho(B_a)$; the two-channel partition
$(B,\mathbb R^3\setminus B)$ assigns $\mu^G_\rho(B)$ to bin $B$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Thus $G$ is the
mathematical joint position PVM, while the detector reading used here is the
declared finite-effect model of P2(iv); this does not assert that every three
sharp coordinate measurement is jointly realized by a laboratory apparatus.
For a unit vector $u$, the trace formula for the rank-one operator $P_u$ gives
$$\mu^G_{P_u}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(P_uG(B))=\|G(B)u\|^2=\int_B\|u(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx,$$
and P7(iii) leaves identification of this ideal detector with a concrete
apparatus as a tested physical claim with uncertainty.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as required by
the cited trace and spectral suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared two-path assignment.** A **declared two-path preparation model**
of the apparatus is the assignment of two nonzero classes
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, called the **path components** of the model with
respect to the declared pair of alternative path conditions of the apparatus,
together with a declared **relative phase** $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and a declared
**weight** $w\in[0,1]$. The assignment of $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$, $\varphi$ and
$w$ is part of the preparation model in the sense of clause (i) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): it is declared, not
computed from the framework, and no item of this page asserts that a particle
described by the model "took" one of the two paths.

**(c) Coherent preparation.** The declared two-path model is **admissible at
phase $\varphi$** when $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$ in $H_{s}$. When it
is admissible, the **coherent preparation** of relative phase $\varphi$ is the
pure preparation
$$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\bigr),$$
the normalized rank-one density operator defined in clause (a). The relative
phase $\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). Multiplying both path
components by one common nonzero scalar leaves their associated pure density
operator unchanged, while the declared relative phase remains part of the
preparation assignment.

**(d) Incoherent preparation.** For a declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ the
**incoherent preparation**, or **which-path preparation**, of the model is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w):=w\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{2}).$$
It is a density operator: both summands are positive trace-class operators of
trace one; trace-class operators form a vector space, nonnegative real
combinations preserve positivity and self-adjointness, and the trace is linear,
so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)=w+(1-w)=1$
([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). The weight $w$
is a declared preparation weight, not an outcome probability.

**(e) Ideal detection bins.** A **declared ideal detector** of the model is a
finite family $\mathcal B=(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$ of pairwise disjoint Borel subsets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $\bigcup_{a}B_{a}=\mathbb R^{3}$; the **ideal bin
probabilities** of a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ are the numbers
$$p_{a}(\rho):=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_{a})\bigr)\qquad(a=1,\dots,m),$$
the reading of the finite-effect clause (iv) of P2 for the declared detector
and its mathematical joint position PVM
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). By clause (iv) of P2 these numbers are
nonnegative, are at most one, and satisfy
$\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho)=1$. A single **declared bin** $B$ is the two-element ideal
detector $(B,\mathbb R^{3}\setminus B)$; its probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)$.

For the **ideal support**, choose a Lebesgue-measurable representative $f$ of
the unit $L^2$ class and form $S_f:=\{x:\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}>0\}$. The
ideal support is the class of $S_f$ under equality up to a Lebesgue-null
symmetric difference. This class is independent of the representative, and
it is not asserted to be a Borel detector bin.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data of the pair:
the framework reading, the declared path components and preparations, and the
ideal bin reading of the position observable. They adopt no assumption beyond
P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; the declaration of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ and of the bins is an apparatus-model input, and
the claim that a concrete two-slit apparatus realizes a particular such
declaration is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7(iii). The
declared bins are subsets of $\mathbb R^{3}$; the model does not claim that a
physical screen of lower dimension is literally a spatial region, and a
marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state to a screen coordinate
or surface is a separate detection model, not supplied here. No dynamics, no
recorded-event response, no sampling model and no empirical result is
asserted; the recorded-event and sampling models are declared separately on
this page.

Adopt the declared two-path preparation model of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], the
unsharp finite-outcome clause (iv) of the observable and probability postulate
P2, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The following vocabulary is used
by this page.

**(a) Declared recorded detector.** A **declared recorded detector** of the
arrangement is a finite set $A$ of **recorded outcome labels** with
$0\notin A$, together with measurable **recorded weights**
$w_{a}:\mathbb R^{3}\to[0,1]$ for $a\in A$ such that
$\sum_{a\in A}w_{a}(x)\le1$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}$. The
**effect** of the label $a$ is the multiplication operator
$$F_{a}:=M_{w_{a}},\qquad (M_{w}\psi)(x):=w(x)\psi(x)\quad\text{a.e.},$$
on $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and the **no-record effect** is
$$F_{0}:=I-\sum_{a\in A}F_{a}.$$
The multiplier is a well-defined linear map on almost-everywhere classes,
since changing a representative on a null set changes its product only on
that null set.
Each $F_a$ is bounded: for $\psi\in H_s$,
$$\|M_{w_a}\psi\|^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)^2\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2,$$
so the boundedness inequality holds with bound $C=1$ by monotonicity of the
nonnegative integral ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).
Thus $F_a$ is a bounded linear operator ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Because $w_a$
is real, the componentwise pairing gives
$\langle M_{w_a}\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,M_{w_a}\phi\rangle$ for all
$\psi,\phi\in H_s$; hence $F_a$ is self-adjoint by
[[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]. At almost every $x$, the finite-dimensional
operator $w_a(x)I_{\mathbb C^r}$ is nonnegative in the sense of
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], and therefore
$$0\le\langle F_a\psi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2.$$
Here $0\le F_a\le I$ means these quadratic-form inequalities for every
$\psi\in H_s$.

Define $w_0(x):=\max\{0,1-\sum_{a\in A}w_a(x)\}$. This is measurable,
$0\le w_0\le1$, and it equals $1-\sum_aw_a$ almost everywhere by the
admissibility condition. Thus $F_0=M_{w_0}=I-\sum_aF_a$ on $H_s$, and the
same argument gives $0\le F_0\le I$ and self-adjointness. Consequently
$\sum_{a\in A}F_a+F_0=I$, so the completed family is a finite family of
bounded effects of clause (iv) of P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

**(b) Recorded probabilities.** For a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ the
**recorded probability** of a label $a\in A$ and the **no-record probability**
are
$$\nu(a):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{a}\bigr),\qquad \nu(0):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{0}\bigr)=1-\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a),$$
the outcome reading of clause (iv) of P2 for the declared effects
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (f)
records the reading; the numbers are nonnegative and sum to one). The
**recorded-event mass** is $\nu(A):=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)=1-\nu(0)\in[0,1]$. A
detector is **full-efficiency** when $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, so
that $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every preparation. For a fixed preparation
$\rho$, the model **loses** events when $\nu(0)>0$, and the no-record channel
carries this lost mass. A detector that is not full-efficiency can nevertheless
have $\nu(0)=0$ for a particular preparation. A **declared recorded bin** $B$ is
the special case with one label $a$ and $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B}$; then
$F_{a}=G(B)$ is the position projection of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], with the
position set $B$ read in the metre unit of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the recorded probability is
the ideal bin probability.

**(c) Loss conditioning.** When $\nu(A)>0$, the **conditioned recorded law** is
$$\bar\nu(a):=\frac{\nu(a)}{\nu(A)}\qquad(a\in A).$$
It is a probability measure on the finite set $A$
([[def-probability-measure]]); it is the law of the recorded label under the
declared model conditioned on the occurrence of a record. Conditioning is a
statistical operation on the recorded data; it is not a state update, and no
claim of P3 is made here.

**(d) Sampling model.** A **declared $N$-trial sampling model** for a fixed
preparation $\rho$ is a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$
carrying measurable maps
$O_{1},\dots,O_{N}:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to
(A\cup\{0\},\mathcal P(A\cup\{0\}))$ ($N\ge1$), where $0$ is the no-record
label of clause (b) and is distinct from every recorded label because
$0\notin A$. The maps are **mutually independent** in the sense of
[[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]] and **identically distributed**
with $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a)=\nu(a)$ for every $a\in A$, $\mathbb P(O_{k}=0)=\nu(0)$
and every $k$, where $\nu$ is the recorded law of clause (b); the numbers
$\nu(a)$ and $\nu(0)$ sum to one, so this is a probability law on the finite
set $A\cup\{0\}$. The **empirical frequency** of the label $a$ in the sample is
$$F_{N}(a):=\frac{1}{N}\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}.$$
A **declared fringe criterion** for sample size $N$ is a subset
$C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$; the model **accepts** the sample when
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\in C$ and **fails the criterion** otherwise. The
identification of repetitions of a concrete procedure with the independent
identically distributed model is an additional statistical assumption in the
sense of clause (ii) of P7; it is not a consequence of P1-P6, and correlated
trials, drifting preparation, dead time and selection must be modeled or
recorded as limitations if present ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the recorded-detector and sampling
vocabulary of the pair and read clause (iv) of P2 and clauses (i)-(iii) of P7.
The recorded weights, the label set, the conditioning convention and the
sampling model are declared apparatus and procedure inputs. The claim "this
apparatus realizes the effect family $F_{a}$" and the claim "its repetitions
are independent and identically distributed draws of $\nu$" are physical
identifications with uncertainty under P7(iii) and P7(ii), can fail, and are
not derived here. No calibration, efficiency, background or resolution value
is asserted, no counts are recorded, and no statistical-inference conclusion
is drawn by this definition.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor postulate P6, as read by
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7, and adopt the declared two-path
preparation model of that definition with path components
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, relative phase
$\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and weight $w\in[0,1]$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ be the joint position
PVM constructed in clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and read
its outcome law by P2 as $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Put
$$N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2},\qquad Z(B):=\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx,\qquad Z:=Z(\mathbb R^{3}),\qquad c(B):=\operatorname{Re}Z(B),\qquad c:=c(\mathbb R^{3}).$$
Then:

(a) *Coherent law.* If the declared model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator expands as
$$\int_{B}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr),$$
with denominator $N+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}Z)$; in particular
$\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}>0$.

(b) *Which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$, so that
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$.
If the declared model is admissible at phase $0$, then
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(0)}(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$
for every Borel set $B$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for almost every }x .$$
In particular, if $\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$, then the coherent law of phase $0$ and the which-path law of
weight $w_{*}$ agree on every bin; and if $c=0$, then, under phase-$0$
admissibility, they agree if and only if
$\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the
declared model, and identify the laws of exactly two declared preparations.
They assert no path ontology, use no entangled marker state and no reduced
state, assert no detector response, no loss, no sampling model, no dynamics and
no empirical result.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in its unsharp finite-outcome
reading, the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$, relative phase $\varphi$ and weight $w$, and
the declared recorded detector
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$ satisfying $0\notin A$, recorded weights $w_{a}$ and effects
$F_{a}=M_{w_{a}}$, no-record
effect $F_{0}=I-\sum_{a}F_{a}$, recorded probabilities $\nu(a)$ and recorded-event
mass $\nu(A)=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited trace-class,
rank-one and square-root suppliers. Let
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ be the declared
coherent and which-path preparations and put $N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$,
$c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle$ and
$w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$. Then:

(a) *Recorded coherent law.* If the model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every label $a\in A$
$$\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(\varphi)}(a)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}(x)\,\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator equals
$$\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr).$$

(b) *Recorded which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every
$a\in A$,
$$\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w)}(a)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Loss.* The no-record probability is
$\nu(0)=1-\nu(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{0})\ge0$, so $\nu(A)\le1$. If
$\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, then $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every
preparation; if $F_{0}\ne0$, then there is a declared pure preparation with
$\nu(0)>0$. When $\nu(A)>0$, the conditioned recorded law
$\bar\nu(a)=\nu(a)/\nu(A)$ is a probability measure on $A$.

(d) *Ideal bins and coincidence.* If $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B_{a}}$ for a declared
ideal detector $(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$, then
$\nu(a)=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})$ is the ideal bin probability of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Moreover, if
the declared model is admissible at phase $0$ and if
the almost-everywhere relation
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)$$
of clause (c) of that theorem holds, then the recorded coherent law of phase
$0$ and the recorded which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ agree, $\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(0)}(a)=\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w_{*})}(a)$,
for every label $a$ of every declared recorded detector.

(e) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional on P2, the declared preparation
and detector models and the cited mathematics; they assert no calibration, no
resolution, background or efficiency value, no state update, no counts and no
empirical result, and the claim that a concrete apparatus realizes the declared
effects is a tested identification with uncertainty.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 with its internal-factor postulate P6,
read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Assume Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be the
real bounded measurable P5 potential and choose a bounded real measurable
representative $V:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$; on $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$
use its restriction. Fix the P5 constants $\hbar>0$ and $m>0$, a spin label
$s$ with $r=2s+1$, a nonempty
open spatial region $\Omega$, and a nonempty open time interval
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Let $\psi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb C^r$ have
components $\psi_l$, $\partial_t\psi_l$, $\partial_j\psi_l$ and
$\partial_k\partial_j\psi_l$ continuous on $\Omega\times I$ for all
$j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, and suppose the **model equation** holds for Lebesgue
almost every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$:
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi_l(x,t)=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi_l(x,t)+V(x)\psi_l(x,t)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r).$$
The displayed equation is the local differential expression assigned by
P5/P4; it is a hypothesis here, and $\psi$ is not required to be a global P4
domain vector. P5 assigns $H_{\mathrm{op}}=-\hbar^2\Delta/(2m)+V(Q)$ on the
componentwise $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$ domain, and P4 asserts the
norm-differentiable equation for vectors in that domain. Existence of a smooth
representative for such a global solution is a separate regularity hypothesis
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv), [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] clause (iii)).

Define the **squared-amplitude density** and its associated **current** by
$$n(x,t):=\sum_{l=1}^r|\psi_l(x,t)|^2=\|\psi(x,t)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2,\qquad j(x,t):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\sum_{l=1}^r\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l(x,t)}\,\nabla\psi_l(x,t))=-\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\langle\psi(x,t),\nabla\psi(x,t)\rangle_{\mathbb C^r}.$$
For $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, when $\psi(\cdot,t)$ is a unit vector of $H_s$,
$n(\cdot,t)$ is the model's position probability density. Under the local
hypotheses stated here, no global normalization or $H_s$ membership is assumed;
$n$ is the squared-amplitude density and the same balance equations apply.
Accordingly, $j$ is the probability current for a normalized state and the
corresponding squared-amplitude current otherwise.
The minus sign in the pairing expression follows from the convention that the
$L^2$ pairing is linear in its first argument. For each component put
$j_l=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l}\nabla\psi_l)$.
Then:

(a) *Pointwise continuity.* For every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_{t}n(x,t)+\operatorname{div}j(x,t)=0 .$$

(b) *Integrated balance.* If $D\subseteq\Omega$ is a bounded open set with
$C^{1}$ boundary and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$
([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]), then
$t\mapsto\int_Dn(x,t)dx$ is differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{D}n(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\partial D}j(x,t)\cdot\nu(x)\,dS ,$$
$\nu$ the outward unit normal.

(c) *Global conservation under domination.* If $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$, if for
each $l$ there is a nonnegative measurable $g_l\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ with
$|\psi_{l}(x,t)|^{2}\le g_{l}(x)$ for almost every $x$ and every $t\in I$, and
if
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{t\in I}\int_{\{|x|=R\}}|j_l(x,t)|\,dS=0$$
for each $l$, then $t\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^3}n(x,t)dx$ is finite and
constant on $I$. In particular, if this integral is $1$ at one time, it is
$1$ throughout $I$ and $n(\cdot,t)$ is a position probability density at every
time.

(d) *Flow conservation.* For the model's assigned unitary flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ on the model's state space and every
$\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$, one has $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$; consequently the model's position probability of a unit
preparation integrates to one at every time, without the regularity hypotheses
of (a)-(c), because P4 assigns a unitary group
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

(e) *Units, reading and scope.* In the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the position wave function has
unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, the density $n$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the current $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$;
the display of (a) is the local balance of the model's squared-amplitude density
in its smooth regime, and (b) reads the rate of change of its integral over a
region as minus the outward current flux across its boundary. When $\psi$ is a
normalized full-space state, these are the position probability density and
probability flux, respectively. The
statement does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial vector
has a representative obeying the regularity hypotheses of (a)-(c), does not
identify a recorded screen rate or any detection law with the surface flux (the
detection model of this page is the declared effect and bin model), and records
no empirical result.

Adopt the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] and the
declared recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$ satisfying $0\notin A$, recorded law $\nu$ (a probability law
on $A\cup\{0\}$, with $0$ the distinct no-record label), and the declared
$N$-trial sampling model of clause (d)
of that definition; the identification of repetitions with that model is the
additional statistical assumption of clause (ii) of the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).
Fix a preparation $\rho$, which may be a coherent preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ or a which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ of the declared model, so that its recorded law is the
law $\nu$ of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]]. Let
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})$ be the outcome sequence,
$S_{N}(a):=\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}$ and $F_{N}(a):=S_{N}(a)/N$ the empirical frequency
of $a\in A\cup\{0\}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Concentration.* For every label $a$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb E\bigl[F_{N}(a)\bigr]=\nu(a),\qquad \operatorname{Var}\bigl(F_{N}(a)\bigr)=\frac{\nu(a)\bigl(1-\nu(a)\bigr)}{N},\qquad \mathbb P\bigl(|F_{N}(a)-\nu(a)|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{\nu(a)(1-\nu(a))}{N\varepsilon^{2}} .$$

(b) *Positive failure probability.* Let $C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$ be a
declared fringe criterion, and suppose there is a sequence
$(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})$ with $(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})\notin C$ and $\nu(a_{k})>0$ for
every $k$. Then the failure probability of the criterion is
$$\mathbb P\bigl((O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\notin C\bigr)\ge\prod_{k=1}^{N}\nu(a_{k})>0 .$$
In particular, if $\nu(a)>0$ for some label $a$, then every criterion that
rejects the constant sequence $(a,\dots,a)$ has failure probability at least
$\nu(a)^{N}>0$.

(c) *No discrimination between coincident laws.* If the model is admissible
at phase $0$ and the recorded coherent law of phase $0$ and the recorded
which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ coincide in the sense of clause (d) of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]], then no
criterion whatsoever has different probability of acceptance under the two
declared preparations; in particular no finite sample distinguishes them with
certainty.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on the declared preparation,
detector and sampling models and the cited mathematics. The independence and
identical distribution of the trials are declared model assumptions, not
consequences of P1-P6; no failure probability, error rate, p-value, confidence
level, power, sample size or measured count is computed or asserted, and no
conclusion is drawn about any real apparatus. In particular the statements do
not assert that a coherent preparation must show a visible fringe pattern in a
finite sample, and do not assert that a sample without a visible pattern
falsifies the coherent model.

## Scope of the page

**What is established.** The page declares the two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with its
path components, coherent and which-path preparations and ideal detection bins,
and the recorded detector and sampling model
