canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint
operator on $H$ with domain $D(A)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and let $B$ be a
bounded self-adjoint operator on $H$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with
$$B\,e^{isA}=e^{isA}B\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
where $e^{isA}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{is\lambda}\,dE_A(\lambda)$ is the unitary
group of $A$ in the spectral calculus
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put $A+B$ on its natural domain
$D(A+B):=D(A)\cap D(B)=D(A)$. Then:

(a) $A+B$ is self-adjoint;

(b) $e^{isB}e^{itA}=e^{itA}e^{isB}$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$; the flows of
$A$ and of the bounded $B$ commute;

(c) the family $s\mapsto P(s):=e^{isA}e^{isB}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group
([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]), and its
infinitesimal generator $G$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G=i(A+B)$: the
quotient $\frac1s\bigl(P(s)x-x\bigr)$ converges as $s\to0$ exactly for
$x\in D(A)$, with limit $i(A+B)x$. Consequently $P(s)=e^{is(A+B)}$ for every
$s\in\mathbb R$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put
$r:=2s+1$, and let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the
special orthogonal group ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]), let
$U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be the componentwise spatial rotation action
$$(U(R)f)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r)$$
of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], and let
$\rho_0:SU(2)\to SO(3)$ be the quaternion conjugation cover of
[[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]], using the matrix identification
$$a+bi+cj+dk\longmapsto\begin{pmatrix}a+bi&c+di\\-c+di&a-bi\end{pmatrix}$$
and the imaginary basis $(i,j,k)$ of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].
For the physical coordinate axes used by the Pauli matrices fix
$$C:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&-1\\0&-1&0\\-1&0&0\end{pmatrix}\in SO(3),\qquad \rho(W):=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C.$$
Thus $\rho$ is the same two-sheeted cover transported to the axes
$(Ce_1,Ce_2,Ce_3)=(-e_3,-e_2,-e_1)$; it is not the literal matrix $\rho_0$ in the imaginary basis. It is smooth by
[[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]]. Let
$F_{s}:\mathcal S_{2s}\to V_{s}=\mathbb C^{r}$ be the unitary identification
$v_{k}\mapsto e_{s-k}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] clause
(d) (for $s=0$, $\mathcal S_{0}=\mathbb C v_{0}$ and $F_{0}v_{0}:=1$),
define $D_{s}:SU(2)\to U(V_{s})$ by
$D_{s}(W):=F_{s}U_{2s}(W)F_{s}^{-1}$ for $s>0$ and
$D_{0}(W):=I_{\mathbb C}$, and let $S_{i}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the self-adjoint
spin endomorphisms of $V_{s}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (a). By clauses
(b),(d),(f) of the theorem the maps $D_{s}$ are strongly continuous unitary
representations of $SU(2)$.
For $W\in SU(2)$ define the matrix action $M_{s}(W)\in\mathcal B(H_{s})$ and
the lifted operator $U_{s}(W)$ by
$$(M_{s}(W)f)(x):=D_{s}(W)\bigl(f(x)\bigr),\qquad U_{s}(W):=U(\rho(W))\,M_{s}(W)\qquad(f\in H_{s},\ x\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
where the matrix $D_{s}(W)$ acts on the column vector $f(x)\in\mathbb C^{r}$.
For any $T\in\operatorname{End}(V_s)$ write $M_Tf(x):=Tf(x)$ almost
everywhere, and define the spin operators on $H_s$ by
$$S_i:=M_{S_i^{\mathrm{fin}}},\qquad D(S_i):=H_s.$$
These bounded self-adjoint operators, rather than the endomorphisms
$S_i^{\mathrm{fin}}$ on $V_s$, occur in all sums, spectral commutation
claims and conjugations on $H_s$ below.
Finally let $R_{i}(t)$, $i=1,2,3$, be the coordinate rotation matrices and
$L_{i}$ the self-adjoint coordinate-rotation generators on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] (so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$), and put
$A_{i}(t):=\cos(t/2)I_{2}-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_{i}\in SU(2)$ with the Pauli
matrices $\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e). Then:

(a) for every $W\in SU(2)$ the operator $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary, with
$U_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})$ for
all $W_{1},W_{2}\in SU(2)$, and $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]);

(b) $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and every $i$, and
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(c) the operators $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ strongly commute (their spectral
projection-valued measures commute;
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), the sum $J_{i}:=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with
domain $D(J_{i}):=D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint, and
$$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
moreover for $W\in SU(2)$ one has the conjugation identities including
domains
$$U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l},\qquad U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l},$$
where $Q_{j},P_{k}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a) and
$\rho(W)_{lj}$ are the matrix entries of the transported cover in the standard basis; the sums mean the maximal directional realizations $Q(\rho(W)e_j)$ and $P(\rho(W)e_k)$ of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clause (b), with domains $U_s(W)D(Q_j)$ and $U_s(W)D(P_k)$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is a mathematical statement about the
finite-dimensional spin representation and the componentwise rotation action;
it asserts no physical interpretation, no measurement, no dynamics and no
value of $\hbar$, $s$ or $W$. The spatial action enters only through
$U(R)=U(\rho(W))$ and the internal action only through $M_{s}(W)$; no action
on a second spatial or internal factor is introduced.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]: $S^2$ with its
polar measure $\sigma$, the Hilbert space $L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), the complete orthonormal
family $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks
$V_{l}:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$, the finite span $H$,
the self-adjoint operators $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ with $L_{3}=L_{z}$ and
$L_{i}Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$ for all $l,m,i$, and the diagonal sphere Laplacian $A$
with $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Then for every $l\ge0$:

(a) each $L_{i}$ leaves $V_{l}$ invariant, and the restriction
$L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of the finite-dimensional
inner product space $V_{l}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for $-l\le m\le l$;

(b) the triple $\bigl((1/\hbar)L_{1}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{2}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{3}|_{V_{l}}\bigr)$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$l$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; in particular
$$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F\qquad(F\in V_{l});$$

(c) for every $F$ in the finite span $H$ one has
$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}AF$.

The statement is a mathematical statement about the operators on
$L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation as angular momentum of a
particle is asserted.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables. They satisfy $S_+^*=S_-$; for $s>0$ they
are not self-adjoint, since $S_+e_{-s}=\hbar\sqrt{2s}\,e_{-s+1}\ne0$
whereas $S_-e_{-s}=0$, while for $s=0$ both vanish and are self-adjoint.
For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action, using the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ defined in that lemma (rather than the literal quaternion-coordinate cover $\rho_0$),
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.

Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, for the declared massive
spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the
scope stated below, the following **effective magnetic-moment coupling**
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

**(i) Gyromagnetic parameter and magnetic moment.** For the declared spin
label $s$ assign a real **gyromagnetic parameter** $\gamma_{s}$, with unit
$\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, and define the **magnetic moment** of the model as
the internal-factor operator
$$\boldsymbol\mu:=\gamma_{s}\mathbf S=(\gamma_{s}S_{1},\gamma_{s}S_{2},\gamma_{s}S_{3}),$$
with unit $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$. Here $\mathbf S=(S_{1},S_{2},S_{3})$ are the
spin operators of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] read on
the internal factor as in
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c). The
parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is an empirical model parameter of the species: it is
part of the declared model data, with uncertainty, and it is not derived from
$s$, from the mass parameter $m$ or from the charge of the particle; no
relation between $\gamma_{s}$ and any other species parameter is asserted by
this postulate.

**(ii) Prescribed field and Zeeman energy operator.** Let
$\mathbf B:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a real bounded measurable
vector field, the **prescribed magnetic field profile**, with components
$B_{i}$ in tesla, entering the model as externally prescribed data
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]); in the
declared inertial frame the model adopts the **Zeeman energy operator**
$$H_{Z}:=H_{0}+M_{W},\qquad H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad M_{W}f:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\gamma_{s}B_{i}(\cdot)\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)(\cdot),$$
on the componentwise domain
$D(H_{Z}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, the domain of $H_{0}$
(componentwise, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]];
$\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ is the componentwise free operator with that domain by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied to each component). The added term $M_{W}$ is bounded with

$\hbar(m+n)$;

(d) for $s=t=\tfrac12$ one has $V_{1/2}\otimes V_{1/2}=W_{0}\oplus W_{1}$ with
$\dim W_{0}=1$ and $\dim W_{1}=3$; the vector
$$\Psi:=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}-e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\bigr)$$
is a unit vector with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for every $i$, and it is
the unique unit vector in the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ up to a phase;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the internal factors of a declared
composite, the assignments of P1 and P6 and the declared diagonal
two-factor action. It asserts no spatial
two-particle model, no statistics or permutation symmetry, no interaction, no
dynamics, no measurement and no empirical correlation; in particular it does
not by itself imply the singlet correlations of a separated pair, which
belong to the composites page.

## Scope and empirical status

- **Adopted assumptions.** This page adopts P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the
  readings of the framework and the spin assignment P6 of
  [[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)
  ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
  [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The
  effective magnetic-moment coupling with its gyromagnetic parameter
  $\gamma_{s}$ and bounded field profile is the additional model assumption
  [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]]; like the spin
  label, mass and charge, the parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is a species parameter
  with uncertainty and is not derived on this page.

- **What is proved.** The local mathematics
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] supplies the
  bounded-perturbation flow and the lifted SU(2) rotation action with its
  coordinate generators, and
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]] identifies the
  orbital Casimir on the harmonic blocks. On that basis:
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] gives the
  spectra and Born laws of the spin components;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigenstates-and-quantum-numbers]]
  describes the orbital eigenstates with the quantum numbers $l,m$ and the
  Casimir value; [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-total-conservation]] proves the
  conservation of the total angular momentum for a spin-independent
  rotation-invariant bounded-potential dynamics;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] gives the Larmor
  precession of the transverse spin expectations and the conservation of the
  field component in a uniform static field;
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] supplies the
  internal-factor composition with the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition and the
  spin-half singlet; and
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]] transfers
  the conditional smooth-field force identity to the model.

- **What is not claimed.** No result of this page derives any value of
  $\gamma_{s}$, $s$, $m$, $g$-factor or $\hbar$; no spin-orbit, fine or
  hyperfine structure, relativistic spinor, anomaly or radiative correction
  is included; no spin-statistics theorem is asserted; no atomic, molecular
  or solid-state model is constructed; and no statement about the
  compositeness or internal structure of any particle is made. The internal
  factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping device, not a rotating body.

- **Experiments.** This page contains no experiment item: it records no
  apparatus, calibration, sampling, count or uncertainty. The historical
  Stern-Gerlach setup appears only as the name of the conditional model of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]], whose
  clause (b) is a prediction of the model conditional on an explicit
  preparation hypothesis. Identifying the operators and parameters of this
  page with a laboratory preparation and apparatus is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under
  [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the measurement
  statistics of sequential spin filters are treated on the measurement pages
  of the category, and agreement or disagreement with data there constrains
  the combined model and apparatus assumptions without proving them.

- **Consumers.** Composites, Bell and identical-particle pages of the
  category consume the internal-factor results of
  [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-composition]] and the lifted rotation
  action of [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]];
  their empirical qualifications are added on those pages and are not
  inherited as certainty from this one.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a
measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) and let $E$ be a projection valued
measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).
Define, for $B\in\Sigma$,
$$F(B):=E(B)\otimes I_{K}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
the bounded tensor operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]
clause (a). Then:

(a) $F$ is a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on
$H\widehat\otimes K$;

(b) for every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb C$, writing
$\Phi_{F}(f)=\int f\,dF$ and $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ for the integrals of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], one has
$$\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I_{K};$$

(c) if $(S_{n})$ is a sequence of bounded operators on $H$ with
$\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and $S_{n}x\to Sx$ for every $x\in H$, then
$(S_{n}\otimes I_{K})z\to(S\otimes I_{K})z$ for every
$z\in H\widehat\otimes K$;

(d) if $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]),
$\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and $E$
regular in the sense of [[def-projection-valued-measure]], then $F$ is regular.

Clause (d) is what makes $F$ a regular projection valued measure on
$\mathbb R$ in the application to assigned sharp observables, so that the
converse direction of the spectral theorem supplies a self-adjoint operator
having $F$ as its spectral measure. No assertion is made about unbounded
operators in this lemma itself.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be arbitrary nonzero complex Hilbert spaces, with inner products linear in the first argument, and put $L=H\widehat\otimes K$ with the isometric inclusion $\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Write $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Set
$$\mathcal P=\{T_{\kappa(a\otimes b),\kappa(a\otimes b)}:\|a\|=\|b\|=1\},\qquad \mathcal S=\overline{\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P}^{\|\cdot\|_1},$$
with trace class as in [[def-trace-class-operator]], where the convex hull consists of finite convex combinations, and the closure is taken in the trace-class operators on $L$. For each unit $\Psi\in L$, let $P_\Psi=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$. Then
$$P_\Psi\in\mathcal S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)\text{ for some unit }a\in H,\ b\in K.$$

More precisely, let $\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\kappa(v_r\otimes u_r)$ be any finite or countably infinite positive Schmidt expansion from [[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]], and put $\lambda_r=s_r^2$. The number $m=\max_{r\in J}\lambda_r$ exists. Every pair of unit vectors $a,b$ satisfies $|\langle\Psi,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle|^2\le m$, with equality at a Schmidt pair whose weight is $m$. Every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\le m$, whereas $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1$. If $\Psi$ is non-product then $m<1$ and, for every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$,
$$\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge 1-m>0.$$
The factors need not be separable; only the support of the single tensor vector has a countable Schmidt expansion. These are mathematical trace pairings, with no measurement or Born-rule assumption.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Density operators are
the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators of trace one
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]]), and for $u,u'\in H$, $v,v'\in K$ the rank-one
operator $T_{u\otimes v,\,u'\otimes v'}$ is the one of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]].

**(a) Product vectors and pure product states.** A vector $\Psi\in
H\widehat\otimes K$ is a **product vector** when $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
some $u\in H$, $v\in K$. A **pure product state** of the composite is a
density operator of the form
$$T_{\Psi,\Psi},\qquad \Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v),\quad \|u\|=\|v\|=1 .$$
A vector is **non-product** when it is not a product vector.

**(b) Separable states.** Write $\mathcal P$ for the set of all pure product
states, a subset of the set $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of density operators. The
**separable states** are the elements of the trace-norm closed convex hull
$$\mathcal S(H,K):=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\,\mathcal P \ \subseteq\ D(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
where $\operatorname{conv}$ denotes the set of finite convex combinations and
the closure is taken in the trace norm $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ of
[[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. A state
$\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is **entangled** (with respect to the
declared splitting $H,K$) when $\rho\notin\mathcal S(H,K)$.

**(c) Conventions and elementary consequences of the form of the definition.**
The set $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ consists exactly of the finite sums
$\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_{j}T_{\Psi_{j},\Psi_{j}}$ with $n\ge1$, weights $w_{j}\ge0$,
$\sum_{j}w_{j}=1$ and unit product vectors $\Psi_{j}$: such sums are convex
combinations of density operators and hence density operators
([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]] clause (a)),
without any orthogonality requirement on the product vectors.
Every element of $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is a density operator, and
$\mathcal S(H,K)$ is a convex subset of $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$: if $\rho,\sigma$
are limits of convex combinations $\rho_{n}\to\rho$, $\sigma_{n}\to\sigma$ and
$t\in[0,1]$, then $t\rho+(1-t)\sigma$ is the trace-norm limit of the convex
combinations $t\rho_{n}+(1-t)\sigma_{n}$. Separability of a state is a
property of the declared splitting $(H,K)$; no assertion is made here about
its behaviour under a different factorization of a larger space.

**(d) Finite dimension.** When $H$ and $K$ are finite dimensional,
$\mathcal P$ is compact and $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is already closed
in the trace norm (it is a compact, hence closed, convex set in the
finite-dimensional space of endomorphisms of $H\widehat\otimes K$), so
$\mathcal S(H,K)=\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ and no closure convention is
needed. In the general case the closure in clause (b) is declared explicitly
and is part of the definition.

**(e) Pure-state specialization and status.** A pure state $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\|\Psi\|=1$ is separable in the precise trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of clause (b) exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector of clause (a); otherwise it is entangled. This is the proved mathematical specialization of [[lem-nrqm-composites-pure-state-separability-criterion]], whose locally defined $\mathcal P,\mathcal S$ are exactly those above. Clauses (a)-(e) fix mathematical vocabulary and adopt no physical assumption, dynamics, measurement or probability law. Whether a laboratory preparation realizes a separable or entangled state for the declared splitting remains a tested identification with uncertainty, not a consequence about nature of this definition.

Adopt the state and composition postulate (P1), the observable and probability
postulate (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate (P3) of the
framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
The following vocabulary is used by this page for a declared pair of
distinguishable subsystems.

**(a) Declared composite and its state space.** A **declared composite model**
is the assignment of two declared systems $A$ and $B$ of the massive-matter
sector, their assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces $H$ and $K$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i) and (iv),
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and the **composite assigned space**
$$H\widehat\otimes K,$$
the completed Hilbert tensor product of $H$ and $K$ with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], clause (iv) of P1). The
**state space of the declared composite** is $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$, the set of
density operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). A **preparation of the
composite** is an element of this set; the model's assignment of a state to a
preparation is the assignment of clause (iii) of P1, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(b) Product basis convention.** If $(e_{a})_{a\in\mathbf A}$ is a finite or
countable orthonormal basis of $H$ and $(f_{b})_{b\in\mathbf B}$ one of $K$,
then $(\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}))_{(a,b)\in\mathbf A\times\mathbf B}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (d)); every
$\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ has the expansion
$$\Psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}),\qquad c_{ab}\in\mathbb C,$$
converging in norm. A **product vector** is $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
$u\in H$, $v\in K$, and a **product preparation** is a state of the form
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$, $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Pure composite preparations are projectors $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ for unit vectors
$\Psi$ given by norm-convergent superpositions of product vectors as above.
General composite preparations are density operators on the completed product,
including statistical mixtures of pure composite preparations; these need not
factor. Superposition acts on vectors, while mixing acts on density operators
(P1 clauses (ii)-(iv)).

**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

**(d) Local effects.** A **local effect** of subsystem $A$ is a bounded
operator of the form $F\otimes I_{K}$ with $0\le F\le I_{H}$ in the
quadratic-form order; the map $F\mapsto F\otimes I_{K}$ is well defined by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a), and $F\otimes I_{K}$
is an effect on $H\widehat\otimes K$: it is bounded, self-adjoint
$((F\otimes I)^{*}=F^{*}\otimes I=F\otimes I)$, and it factors as
$$F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),\qquad I_{H}\otimes I_{K}-F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),$$
with the positive square roots of the continuous functional calculus
([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and
the product and adjoint rules of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (b), (c); hence
$0\le F\otimes I_{K}\le I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the quadratic-form order
([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).
Local effects of subsystem $B$ are defined in the same way.

**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates, defined only for outcomes with $p_a>0$,
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the reading of clause (iv) of P1 together
with clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) of P2 and clause (v) of P3 for a declared pair
of distinguishable subsystems. They add no physical assumption to those
postulates beyond the readings displayed. In particular: the subsystems are
distinguishable, so no exchange sector, symmetrization or exclusion statement
is introduced (those are separate assumptions of P6); no superselection
restriction or algebraic replacement of the tensor product is adopted; no
interaction, dynamics, disturbance of the other subsystem or correlation is
asserted; and whether a concrete laboratory arrangement realizes a declared
composite, a declared local readout or a declared local instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

Adopt the declared composite model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] with
subsystems $A,B$, assigned spaces $H,K$ and composite space
$H\widehat\otimes K$, the state postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the state space
$D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the framework
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
partial-trace and tensor construction results. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.

**(a) Reduced preparations.** For a preparation $\rho\in
D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the declared composite, the **reduced preparation
of subsystem $A$** is
$$\rho_{A}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),$$
the image of $\rho$ under the partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a), characterized by
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(X\otimes I_{K})\bigr) \qquad\text{for every bounded }X\in\mathcal B(H);$$
the **reduced preparation of subsystem $B$** is
$\rho_{B}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$, characterized by
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes Y))$ for
every bounded $Y\in\mathcal B(K)$. By clause (b) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] the partial trace maps density
operators to density operators and is trace preserving, so $\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho_{B}$ are states of the respective subsystems in the sense of the state
space of the framework.

**(b) Affineness and continuity.** The maps $\rho\mapsto\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho\mapsto\rho_{B}$ are affine and continuous in the trace norm:
$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ is linear and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T\|_{1}\le\|T\|_{1}$
by clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]], with the
trace norm of [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. In
particular the reduction of a statistical mixture
$\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of composite preparations is
the corresponding mixture $\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{A,n}$ of the reduced
preparations.

**(c) Product preparations reduce to their factors.** If
$\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is a
product preparation ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), then
$$T_{u\otimes v,\,u\otimes v}=T_{u,u}\otimes T_{v,v}$$
as bounded operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$, because both sides agree on
every elementary tensor $\kappa(x\otimes y)$ in the sense of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a) and $\kappa[H\odot K]$
is dense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c));
consequently
$$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u},\qquad \rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$$
by clause (c) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]. Thus a
product preparation is exactly a preparation whose reductions reconstruct it,
$\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, and whose reductions are pure.

**(d) Correlated and uncorrelated preparations.** A composite preparation
$\rho$ is called **uncorrelated** when $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ and
**correlated** otherwise; a pure preparation
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is called a product preparation when $\Psi$ is a product
vector and **non-product** otherwise
([[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clauses (a), (b)).
These are descriptive names for the displayed algebraic conditions; the
statistical reading of the distinction, including the failure of
factorization of local outcome laws for non-product pure preparations, is a
theorem of this page and is not assumed here.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix vocabulary: the subsystem states attached
to a composite preparation by the partial trace. The reduction is a
mathematical operation on the model description. It is not a dynamics, not an
interaction, not a measurement and not a physical discarding of subsystem $B$;
no disturbance of either subsystem and no empirical fact is asserted, and the
question whether a laboratory procedure prepares a state whose reduction is a
prescribed state is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The
physical reading of clause (a) — that the reduced preparation reproduces every
local outcome law of subsystem $A$ — is a theorem of this page and is not
assumed here.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The adopted composite
reading also carries the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for its
local spectral readouts; the Schmidt and partial-trace deductions below use
only Countable Choice. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ satisfy
$\|\Psi\|=1$, let
$$\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K),\qquad \rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),\qquad \rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$$
be the pure preparation of the declared composite and its two reduced
preparations. Then:

**(a) Schmidt expansion and reductions.** There are an at most countable index
set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq H$,
$(u_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq K$ and numbers $s_{r}>0$ with
$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\,\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})\quad\text{(norm convergence)},\qquad \sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}=1,$$
and the reduced preparations are given by the trace-norm convergent series
$$\rho_{A}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{v_{r},v_{r}},\qquad \rho_{B}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{u_{r},u_{r}} .$$
Moreover $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{4}$.

**(b) Purity and product criterion.** The following are equivalent:
(i) exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero; (ii) $\rho_{A}$ is pure, that is
$\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$; (iii) $\rho_{B}$ is pure;
(iv) $\Psi$ is a product vector, $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$; (v) $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$; (vi) $\rho$ is separable in the trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). In that case
$s_{r_{0}}=1$ at the unique nonzero index and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$,
$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ for $u=v_{r_{0}}$, $v=u_{r_{0}}$.

**(c) Non-product pure preparations.** If $\Psi$ is not a product vector, then
at least two coefficients $s_{r}$ are nonzero, $\rho_{A}$ and $\rho_{B}$ are
mixed, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$, and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$;
the pure preparation is entangled in the full trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). More precisely, if $m=\max_rs_r^2<1$, every separable $\sigma$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma\rho)\le m$ and $\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\ge1-m>0$.

**(d) Scope.** The statement concerns the declared composite, its pure
preparations and the reduced preparations of the factors. It asserts no
dynamics, no interaction, no measurement, no apparatus realization and no
empirical fact; and it concerns pure composite preparations only, mixed-state
separability being outside its scope.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for a
declared composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned
spaces $H,K$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited suppliers. Let $\rho,\rho'\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be
preparations with reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$,
$\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ and
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$. Then:

**(a) Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of
subsystem $A$ with local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{A}\,E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B),$$
where $E_{A}$ is the spectral projection valued measure of $A$. In particular
the local statistics of subsystem $A$ depend on the composite preparation only
through its reduced preparation, and if $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$ then every local
readout law is the same in $\rho$ and in $\rho'$.

**(b) Determination of the reduced preparation.** Conversely, if
$\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$, then there are a bounded assigned sharp observable
$(P,1)$ of subsystem $A$ and a Borel set $B$ with
$\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)\ne\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)$: the
family of local readout laws of subsystem $A$ determines $\rho_{A}$ among the
preparations of the composite.

**(c) Ideal local measurement.** Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ be a declared
ideal sharp measurement of subsystem $A$
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (a)). Then $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})_{a\in A_{0}}$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement of the declared composite, its outcome probabilities in a
preparation $\rho$ are
$$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a}),$$
and for $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state
$\rho_{a}:=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ of the
composite has the reduced preparation
$$(\rho_{a})_{A}=\frac{P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
which is the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$ by $P_{a}$. The
discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$
has reduced preparations
$$\Phi(\rho)_{A}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a},\qquad \Phi(\rho)_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{B} .$$
The analogous statements hold with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the readings of the cited items and of the cited mathematics. They concern
the declared composite and its declared measurements; they assert no dynamics,
no interaction, no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes
and no empirical fact, and clause (c) is a statement about the declared ideal
Lueders instrument only, not about every laboratory procedure.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited
spectral-law supplier. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$
be a unit vector, $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ the associated pure preparation, and
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ its
reduced preparations. Then:

**(a) Product preparations factorize.** If $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$, then for every bounded effect $F$ on $H$ and every bounded
effect $F'$ on $K$
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(F\otimes F')\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}F)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F').$$
In particular, for a declared finite-outcome measurement of $A$ with effect
family $(F_{i})$ and one of $B$ with $(F'_{j})$, the joint outcome
probabilities factorize, $p(i,j)=p_{A}(i)p_{B}(j)$: in a product preparation
the two subsystems have independent local statistics.

**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=0\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$
so the joint law of the corresponding two-outcome local measurements does not
factorize; the product of the marginal probabilities exceeds the joint
probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$.

**(c) Scope.** The statement is a conditional computation for pure
preparations of the declared composite; it asserts no dynamics, no
interaction, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no
empirical fact, and it does not claim that a joint law failing to factorize
establishes any particular physical mechanism.

Adopt the framework's composition and measurement readings for a declared
composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the local
sharp-readout law used below. Let $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be a preparation of the
declared composite with reduced preparations
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$, and
let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ be a declared finite or
countable instrument of subsystem $B$, normalized:
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{K}$ in the strong sense, with effects
$F_{a}:=\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ and outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$. Then:
 
**(a) The local extension.** The family
$(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ is a declared
finite or countable instrument of the declared composite, with outcome effects
$F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}=I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$, outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}})$, and conditional states
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0).$$

**(b) No-signalling.** The discarded-outcome state
$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a,r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$
is a preparation of the composite, its reduced preparation on $A$ is unchanged,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho=\rho_{A},$$
and consequently every local outcome law of subsystem $A$ is unchanged:
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\Phi(\rho)}=\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}\qquad\text{for every assigned sharp observable }(A,u_{A})\text{ of }A .$$
The same holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(c) Conditional reductions.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state $\rho_{a}$
has reduced preparation $(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho_{a}$ on $A$,
and
$$\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\,(\rho_{a})_{A}=\rho_{A};$$
the conditional reduced preparations $(\rho_{a})_{A}$ may differ from
$\rho_{A}$, and the recorded outcome $a$ is the classical datum needed to
select them.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the stated readings and of the cited mathematics; they concern declared
instruments of the declared composite. They assert no relativistic causality
principle, no claim that a particular apparatus realizes the declared
instrument, no disturbance of the other factor by any concrete device and no
empirical fact.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited position-outcome law. In
the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}),\,\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})}+\tfrac12\,T_{\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}),\,\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.

Adopt the declared marked two-component model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] with unit path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, unit marker states $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
phase family $\rho(\varphi)$, marker-carried which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$, and a declared detection bin $B$. Assume the model is
**overlap-normalized**, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the
cited position and local-readout suppliers. Put
$$\gamma(B):=\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\,\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle,\qquad p_{j}(B):=\langle G(B)\psi_{j},\psi_{j}\rangle\quad(j=1,2),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(p_{1}(B)+p_{2}(B)\bigr).$$
Then:
 
**(a) Unit-norm phase family.** $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every $\varphi$, so
$\rho(\varphi)=T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}$.
 
**(b) Detection law.** For every $\varphi$,
$$p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B)\bigr).$$
 
**(c) Contraction of the cross term.** For every $\varphi$,
$$\bigl|p(\varphi)(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)\bigr|\le|\gamma(B)|\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\sqrt{p_{1}(B)p_{2}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B).$$
In particular, if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$
for every $\varphi$: the marked detection law is exactly the which-path law.
 
**(d) Visibility.** Writing $\gamma(B)=|\gamma(B)|e^{i\theta}$ with
$\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, one has
$$\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|,\qquad \inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|,$$
so that, whenever $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$, the fringe visibility of clause (e)
of the definition is
$$V(B)=\frac{|\gamma(B)|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle| .$$
 
**(e) Extremes.** If the model is trivially marked,
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$, then for every bin with
$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$ one has
$V(B)=\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le1$;
if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $V(B)=0$ for every bin with $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$.
 
**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional computations in the declared
model. They assert no measured pattern, no trial counts, no statistical
analysis, no decoherence mechanism, no irreversibility and no which-path
ontology, and they contain no empirical claim.

- **Adopted readings.** The page adopts the composition clause of P1
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) for a declared pair of
  distinguishable subsystems, together with the observable and probability
  postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 in the
  readings of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]];
  the reduced preparations of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]];
  and, for the marked interference model,
  [[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]], whose path
  components, marker states and detector bin are declared apparatus data under
  P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). The composition
  assignment, the local readout convention and the marked model are adopted,
  not derived from the rest of the framework or from observation.
- **Derived results.** The conditional results of the page are the Schmidt
  reduction, purity criterion and exact pure separability/product equivalence for pure preparations
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]]), the
  identification of local readout laws with the laws of the reduced
  preparation and its converse
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]]), the
  invariance of the untouched factor's reduced preparation under discarded
  local instruments, with the conditional reductions averaging back to it
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]]), and the
  contraction of the marker cross term with the visibility bound
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]]). Each is
  conditional on its stated hypotheses, including the choice hypotheses of the
  cited mathematics.
- **Empirical status.** No item of the page reports an experiment, a count, a
  calibration or a measured correlation, and none is a proof about nature. The
  detection weights and the visibility of the marked model are probabilities
  and contrasts of a declared model; whether a concrete interferometer
  realizes a marked model with particular components, marker states and bin is
  a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii)
  of P7, and a comparison of the model with recorded data would require the
  sampling, efficiency, resolution and background qualifications of the
  apparatus, which this page does not supply.
- **Localized detections and accumulated distributions.** The detection
  weights of the page are probabilities for one trial of the declared model.
  An interference pattern is a property of the accumulated distribution of
  many detections, not of a single event, and a finite sample can fail a
  declared fringe criterion with positive probability under ordinary
  independent sampling even when the model is correct; nothing in the page
  draws a statistical conclusion from the displayed probabilities.
- **No-signalling is a model statement.** The invariance proved in
  [[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] is a statement
  about declared local instruments of the adopted framework and its
  mathematics. It is not a relativistic causality principle, does not assert
  anything about spacelike separation, and does not by itself exclude
  alternative models; the conditional changes of the measured factor's partner
  are the correlations of the model, and every interpretation of the
  alternatives, of the marker and of "which path" is outside the page.
- **Deferred content.** The following are outside this pair and are not
  supplied or assumed here: setting-independent local-response models and the
  classical-versus-quantum Bell comparison, with specified angles and
  finite-data caveats, which belong to the later Bell-models pair; a general
  theory of mixed-state separability, entanglement measures and separability
  criteria beyond the definition given in
  [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]]; the exchange
  sectors and exclusion statements for identical particles; quantum circuits,
  teleportation and computation; and any dynamics, interaction or open-system
  model of decoherence, the marked model of this page being a kinematic
  preparation model.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
This item fixes finite combinatorial vocabulary for outcome laws of a
two-station comparison. No physical interpretation, measurement model,
dynamics or locality assertion is made here; the physical readings are fixed
on the page of this pair. No choice principle is used.

**(a) Binary correlation model.** Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty sets, the
**setting labels** of the two stations, and put
$\Sigma:=\{-1,+1\}$ for the common **outcome labels**. A **binary correlation
model** on $(I,J)$ is a family
$$\mu=(\mu_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J},\qquad \mu_{ij}:\Sigma\times\Sigma\to[0,1],$$
of functions with the normalization
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=1 \qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in I\times J$$
([[def-finite-sum]]). Each $\mu_{ij}$ is the **joint law** of the setting pair
$(i,j)$: it is the outcome-weight function of a finite probability space on
the four outcomes $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ in the sense of
[[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]], and sums over $\Sigma\times\Sigma$
are finite sums.

**(b) Marginals.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$ the **marginal law of the first
station** and the **marginal law of the second station** are
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma .$$

**(c) No-signalling.** The model $\mu$ is **no-signalling** when the marginal
law of the first station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}$ for all $i\in I$ and all $j,j'\in J$, and the
marginal law of the second station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $j\in J$ and all $i,i'\in I$. The word is
used as a name for this pair of identities about the tables; no spatial or
causal claim is attached to it.

**(d) Correlations and the CHSH functional.** Assume $I=J=\{0,1\}$. The
**correlation** of the setting pair $(i,j)$ and the **CHSH functional** of the
model are the real numbers
$$E_{ij}(\mu):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma} \varepsilon\,\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad S(\mu):=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu).$$

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) introduce finite tables, their marginals, the
no-signalling identities and one linear functional of four correlations. They
assert no physical assumption, no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law
for a real apparatus and no statement about nature; the identification of a
laboratory arrangement with a model $\mu$ is a separate physical matter.

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]). No choice principle is used in
this definition.

**(a) Local-response representation.** A **local-response representation** of
$\mu$ is a tuple consisting of a probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},
\mathbb P)$ ([[def-measure-space]], [[def-probability-measure]]) and two
families of **response laws**
$$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I},\qquad (\beta_{j})_{j\in J},$$
where for each $i\in I$ the function
$\alpha_{i}:\Lambda\times\Sigma\to[0,1]$ has the two properties
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=1\quad(\lambda\in\Lambda), \qquad \lambda\mapsto\alpha_{i}(\lambda,+1)\ \text{is measurable}$$
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]), and the family
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ has the same two properties; and the **representation
identity**
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P(\lambda) =\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\right]$$
holds for every $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and every
$(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. The integrand is a product of two
bounded measurable $[0,1]$-valued functions, so the expectation exists as a
finite number ([[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). The functions
$\alpha_{i}(\cdot,-1)=1-\alpha_{i}(\cdot,+1)$ and likewise for $\beta_{j}$ are
measurable as well. The variable $\lambda$ is called the **specification**
of the representation; it is a mathematical index, and no physical
interpretation is asserted.

**(b) Response functions (deterministic form).** Equip the finite outcome set
$\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ with its discrete $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal P(\Sigma)$.
A local-response representation **has response functions** when there are
measurable maps
$a_{i}:(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})\to(\Sigma,\mathcal P(\Sigma))$ $(i\in I)$
and $b_{j}:(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})\to(\Sigma,\mathcal P(\Sigma))$
$(j\in J)$ with
$$\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=\mathbf 1_{\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}}(\lambda), \qquad \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)=\mathbf 1_{\{b_{j}=\delta\}}(\lambda),$$
in which case the representation identity reads
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\mathbb P\bigl(\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}\cap\{b_{j}=\delta\}\bigr).$$
The deterministic form is a special case of clause (a): it is obtained by
setting the response laws to the Dirac laws at $a_{i}(\lambda)$ and
$b_{j}(\lambda)$. In this form one and the same specification space and the
same single-station functions $a_{i}$ and $b_{j}$ serve every setting
pair, and the response of a station depends on the specification and on that
station's own setting only.

**(c) Terminology.** The two mathematical features named by **local response**
are: (i) a single specification space carrying the probability law used for
every setting pair (setting-independence), and (ii) per-station response laws
that do not depend on the distant station's setting. A model that admits such
a representation is also called a **local model** of the tables in the
literature; the representation is an existence statement about the tables and
asserts no determinism, no mechanism, no dynamics and no causal relation. In
particular clause (a) permits probabilistic responses and does not require
the response functions of clause (b).

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix vocabulary. They assert no physical
assumption and no property of any laboratory arrangement; whether a declared
physical model of a comparison admits a representation of this form is a
mathematical question about its tables, and the physical reading of that
question is fixed on the page of this pair.

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})$, $(\beta_{j})$
and probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then:

(a) for every $i\in I$ the marginal law of the first station satisfies
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}\qquad\text{for all }j,j'\in J,$$
and for every $j\in J$ the marginal law of the second station satisfies
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $i,i'\in I$; that is, $\mu$ is
no-signalling;

(b) consequently, if a binary correlation model is not no-signalling, then it
admits no local-response representation.

No physical assumption and no choice principle is used; the proposition is a
statement about the tables and their representation.

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the setting sets $I=J=\{0,1\}$
with outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$, with correlations $E_{ij}(\mu)$ and
CHSH functional $S(\mu)$ as in
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clauses (d), and suppose that
$\mu$ admits a local-response representation with response laws
$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then
$$\bigl|S(\mu)\bigr|\le 2 .$$
The statement is a theorem about the tables and their representation; it
asserts no measurement, no dynamics, no spatial or causal structure, and it
contains no physics. No choice principle is used.

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$,
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Let
$D\in\Sigma_{\Lambda}$ be a **selection event** with $\mathbb P(D)>0$, put
$$\mathbb P_{D}(A):=\frac{\mathbb P(A\cap D)}{\mathbb P(D)}\qquad(A\in\Sigma_{\Lambda})$$
for the **conditional probability measure** on $D$, and define the
**$D$-conditional tables**
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\frac{1}{\mathbb P(D)} \int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}(\lambda)\,\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\,d\mathbb P(\lambda)$$
for $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and $(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. Then:

(a) $\mathbb P_{D}$ is a probability measure on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})$
and $\mu^{D}:=(\mu^{D}_{ij})$ is a binary correlation model on $(I,J)$;

(b) the same response laws represent $\mu^{D}$ over $\mathbb P_{D}$:
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P_{D}(\lambda)\qquad\text{for all }i,j,\varepsilon,\delta ;$$

(c) if $I=J=\{0,1\}$, then $\bigl|S(\mu^{D})\bigr|\le2$.

The selection event $D$ is a subset of the specification space: membership in
$D$ is the same for every setting pair and does not depend on the settings or
on the outcomes. No choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis
of the tensor construction cited below. Let $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the
orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and let
$$\sigma_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{z}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
be the Pauli matrices of clause (e) of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] in the ordered basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; for $a=(a_{x},a_{y},a_{z})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$\sigma_{a}:=a_{x}\sigma_{x}+a_{y}\sigma_{y}+a_{z}\sigma_{z}$, and for
$\varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ put
$$P_{a,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,\sigma_{a}\bigr).$$
Let $V\widehat\otimes V$ be the completed tensor product with inclusion
$\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and let
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr)\in V\widehat\otimes V, \qquad q:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) for every unit $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$ the
operator $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ is an orthogonal projection on $V$,
$P_{a,+}+P_{a,-}=I$ and
$P_{a,\varepsilon}P_{a,\varepsilon'}=\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}P_{a,\varepsilon}$;

(b) $\|\Psi\|=1$ and the four vectors $\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),
\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$ are mutually orthogonal, so
$(\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-}))$ is an
orthonormal basis of $V\widehat\otimes V$;

(c) for all unit $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and all
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b\bigr);$$

(d) the marginals of the four numbers in (c) are
$$\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12 =\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle,$$
and their correlation is
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\delta\, \bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =-a\cdot b .$$

The lemma is a finite-dimensional computation in the tensor product; it
asserts no preparation, measurement or physical interpretation. The Axiom of
Countable Choice enters only through the construction of the completed tensor
product cited from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].

## Definition

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3, the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5 as inherited through the cited
spin-$s$ model and spin-spectrum result (only their internal-factor content
is used here), the
internal-factor assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), together with the
composite, observable and measurement readings of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, read as assigned sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and P6
clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c) the
observable $S_{n}$ has the two eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ with
spectral projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
