consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(e) Declared local-response models of the arrangement.** A **declared
local-response model of the arrangement** is a local-response representation,
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], of the
correlation table $\nu^{\rho}$. It is a model of the same four tables: it
consists of a probability space of **specifications** and of per-station
response laws, subject to the representation identity, and it need not be a
model of the framework's state space. The arrangement **admits a
local-response model** when such a representation exists.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

## Remarks

- **Why the joint measurement is declared and not derived.** The framework's
  measurement vocabulary declares outcome structures; it does not assert that
  arbitrary observables of two factors possess a joint sharp measurement. For
  the arrangement the product family of clause (d) is itself a finite family
  of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, so the joint
  measurement of the two sign measurements is a declared ideal sharp
  measurement of the composite in the framework's own sense. No claim is made
  that an arbitrary pair of laboratory procedures realizes it.
- **Sign labels versus coordinates.** The sign labels $\pm1$ are the outcome
  indices used by the correlation tables; the physical outcome coordinates are
  $\pm\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The correlation and the CHSH
  functional of clause (d) are functionals of the sign labels and are
  dimensionless; no numerical value of an angular momentum coordinate is
  asserted anywhere.

Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: the composite
$V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared spin-half factors with orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, a declared preparation $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, the
setting directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and the four
declared joint sign measurements with outcome laws
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\bigr), \qquad P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\,a\cdot\sigma) .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of
the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and
take the **singlet preparation**
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr), \qquad \rho_{\Psi}:=T_{\Psi,\Psi},$$
where $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is the rank-one operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Then:

(a) for every $(i,j)\in\{0,1\}^{2}$ and all $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\bigl\langle(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a_{i}\cdot b_{j}\bigr);$$

(b) the correlations of the arrangement are
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$ and
$$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}) =-\bigl[a_{0}\cdot b_{0}+a_{0}\cdot b_{1}+a_{1}\cdot b_{0}-a_{1}\cdot b_{1}\bigr] =-\,(a_{0}\cdot(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}\cdot(b_{0}-b_{1}));$$
in particular, for the unit directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ and
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2$;

(c) consequently the correlation table $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$ of the arrangement
at those directions admits no local-response model in the sense of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: there is no local-response
representation of the four tables
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]) with these laws;

(d) the marginal sign laws of the arrangement are
$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac12=
\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},B}_{ij}(\delta)$ for every setting pair and every direction, so
the table is no-signalling in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; and a discarded declared local
instrument on either factor leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor
and every local outcome law of that factor unchanged
([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

The item is a conditional model computation: it asserts no measured
correlation, no apparatus and no empirical fact, and its exclusion is exactly
of the declared local-response class of these four tables. Higher singleton
claims about hidden variables in general are not asserted.

Let $(V\widehat\otimes V,\rho,a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1})$ be a declared spin
correlation arrangement of the two declared spin-half factors in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], with a preparation
$\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, unit directions
$a_{i},b_{j}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, outcome laws
$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and CHSH functional
$S(\nu^{\rho})$ as in clauses (d) of that definition and (d) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers. Then:

(a) $\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho})\bigr|\le2\sqrt2$ for every preparation $\rho$ and all
unit directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$;

(b) the bound is attained: with $\Psi:=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$
and the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$, for the directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$,
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has
$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2$.

The statement is a conditional theorem about the declared arrangement model; it
asserts no measured value and no apparatus realization.

## Remarks

- **What the comparison establishes.** For the declared spin correlation
  arrangement of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], the four sign
  tables are the laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ of clause (d) of
  that definition. If the arrangement's CHSH functional satisfies
  $|S(\nu^{\rho})|>2$, then the four tables admit no local-response model:
  every local-response representation would give $|S|\le2$ by
  [[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]. The singlet at the
  directions of [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] is the
  displayed instance, with $|S|=2\sqrt2$. The statement is a conditional
  no-go for one precisely defined class of models of one precisely defined set
  of four tables.

- **What is not excluded.** The theorem concerns models of the four tables
  that consist of one specification space whose probability law is the same
  for all setting pairs, together with per-station response laws that do not
  depend on the distant setting ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]
  clauses (a), (c)). Models outside that class are not addressed: a model
  whose specification or response is allowed to depend on the distant setting,
  a model that does not reproduce all four tables simultaneously, or a model
  of a different arrangement or of a different measurement structure is not
  excluded. In particular the comparison does not rule out "hidden variables"
  in general, and it does not claim that no completion of quantum mechanics
  exists; it excludes the declared local-response class for these tables.

- **Assumptions used.** The deduction rests on the framework readings P1, P2,
  P3, P5, P6 and P7 fixed by
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], on the declared composite,
  preparation and spin-half assignments, on the ideal sharp character of the
  declared measurements ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
  on the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom
  of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) stated in the arrangement and
  singlet-attainment hypotheses, and on the cited mathematics (the
  finite-dimensional tensor calculus, the CHSH bound for representable models
  and the operator bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). Changing one of these
  readings voids the conditional conclusion for the changed model; it does not
  weaken it, and a replacement conclusion needs its own proof.

- **Measurement-model boundary.** The declared sign measurements have exactly
  two outcomes with sign labels $\pm1$; detection efficiency, finite
  resolution, dark counts, background, drift and loss are outside the
  arrangement and require their own apparatus models. In particular an
  observed violation on a recorded sub-ensemble does not by itself contradict
  the declared model class: the recorded tables are conditional tables, and
  the CHSH bound transfers to them when the selection is determined by a
  positive-probability event of the specification space that is the same for
  every setting pair, as in
  [[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]; that lemma is a
  sufficient condition, not a necessary one, and is not a claim about any
  real detector. A different selection model may also yield representable
  conditional tables; its consequences require their own justification. Finite
  samples add a sampling model and its fluctuations, treated on the examples
  page. Whether a finite record deductively excludes one of two specified
  models depends on their sampling supports: a record with positive
  probability under both is compatible with both, while an observed
  zero-probability record can exclude one specified ideal model conditional on
  its assumptions. No universal claim is made about every model pair or every
  finite sample.

- **No-signalling is not the separator.** Every local-response model is
  no-signalling ([[prop-nrqm-bell-local-representations-are-no-signalling]]),
  and every declared arrangement's marginals are also setting-independent:
  summing its joint law over $\delta$ gives
  $\nu^{\rho,A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_i,\varepsilon}\otimes I))$
  because $\sum_\delta P_{b_j,\delta}=I$, and the symmetric sum is
  $\nu^{\rho,B}_{ij}(\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I\otimes P_{b_j,\delta}))$
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (a), (d)). For the
  singlet both marginals are $1/2$
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (d)); a discarded
  declared local instrument on one factor leaves the other factor unchanged
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).
  The contrast between the two classes therefore lies in the joint tables,
  not in any dependence of one station's marginal law on the distant setting.

- **Attainment and sharpness.** The value $2\sqrt2$ is attained for the
  declared arrangement
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]] clause (b)), so within
  the declared class of binary sharp readouts of self-adjoint involutions no
  smaller uniform bound for the CHSH functional is available. This says
  nothing about other functionals, other numbers of settings, unsharp
  measurements or other systems.

- **Interpretation.** The result is a statement about four probability
  tables. It identifies no mechanism, no influence between the stations and
  no preferred frame; the arrangement carries no spatial or temporal
  structure. Interpretations that attach additional physical content to the
  violation are not part of the deduction and are not asserted here. Whether
  a laboratory arrangement realizes the declared model and what a recorded
  sample shows are separate matters under the preparation and apparatus
  postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Mathematical vocabulary for binary correlation
  models and their local-response representations
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]],
  [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]), the CHSH bound for every
  representable model ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]),
  the preservation of representability and of the bound under a
  setting-independent selection
  ([[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]), the exact joint
  laws of the two-factor singlet ([[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]]), the
  declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]), the singlet computation with
  the failure of local-response representability at violating settings
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]]) and the Tsirelson bound
  with its attainment
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). All are conditional
  model statements; the spin-arrangement and spin-comparison claims carry the
  Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Choice
  ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) stated in their supplier hypotheses.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment item, no reported count,
  no calibration, no detector efficiency, no loss model, no background, no
  trial-level uncertainty analysis, no p-value, no confidence level and no
  measured correlation. None of the computations establishes that the
  framework or any of its postulates describes nature, and none of them
  asserts that any laboratory procedure realizes the declared arrangement.
  The marginals, tables and correlations are model probabilities for the
  declared preparation; the identification of a concrete apparatus with the
  declared measurements is the
  tested identification with uncertainty of clause (iii) of the preparation
  and apparatus postulate P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Treating repetitions
  as independent and identically distributed draws is the additional
  statistical model of clause (ii), to be declared and checked for the
  apparatus and procedure; it is not implied by the state postulate.

- **Deferred experiment destination.** The design of this pair reserves an
  experiment item for a Bell test. Such an item is not built here: it would
  require reading a primary or authoritative full report and recording its
  source-specific preparation and apparatus, calibration, measured outputs,
  trial count where reported, detection efficiency, loss and post-selection,
  background, the reported statistical treatment and systematics, and the
  source's omissions; none of the sources read for this page supplies that
  level of detail. The sources' experimental remarks motivate the model
  comparison only: Binney's section 6.1.4 refers to the 1972
  Freedman-Clauser test and cites a 1998 photonic test, and the MIT chapter
  closes with the statement that experiments have confirmed violations; no
  numerical value from those secondary accounts is reproduced here as an
  observation, and no interval, count or precision is asserted. The
  statistics and primary-report gap named in the design is recorded as an
  open destination.

- **Source qualifications not imported.** The same sources contain general
  conclusions that the comparison rules out hidden variables as such or that
  quantum mechanics cannot be superseded by a theory with a definite spin
  direction. Those conclusions are stronger than the conditional statement
  proved here — which excludes only the declared local-response class of the
  declared tables — and are not imported. Likewise the operator bound used on
  this page is proved by the operator-norm route of the cited mathematics
  (the identity for the square of the CHSH operator and the norm bound,
  invoked in [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]] fact F6 and
  proof step 1.2). That route uses
  $\|[A_0,A_1]\|\le2$ and $\|[B_0,B_1]\|\le2$ for the supplier's
  self-adjoint involutions $A_i,B_j$, where $[A,B]:=AB-BA$ is the
  commutator; no
  reversed variance inequality of the form
  $\langle C^{2}\rangle\le\langle C\rangle^{2}$ is
  used as a premise.

- **What a comparison with data could show.** Under declared preparation,
  detection, settings, selection and sampling models, agreement of recorded
  frequencies with the arrangement's tables supports the combined model and
  apparatus assumptions. The bound $|S(\mu)|\le2$ constrains the correlations
  of a local-response model's probability tables, rather than every finite
  sample estimate $\widehat S$. A finite recorded estimate with
  $|\widehat S|>2$ can have positive probability under that model; finite-sample
  fluctuations are treated in [[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]. Evidence
  against a specified model class requires an explicit statistical test with
  its sampling assumptions, uncertainty and error control, together with the
  apparatus and selection qualifications. A threshold crossing alone does
  not deductively exclude the class, and a p-value is not the probability
  that the class is false. Agreement does not prove the framework, and a null
  or reduced result does not by itself falsify it.

- **Interpretation and scope of the model.** The arrangement assigns no
  spatial positions, separation or temporal order to the two factors, so no
  relativistic locality principle is modelled here; the exclusion is a
  statement about the four tables. The boundaries of the comparison are
  recorded in [[rem-nrqm-bell-boundaries-and-comparison-scope]], and no
  interpretation of the violation beyond those boundaries is asserted.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), let
$H\widehat\otimes H$ be its completed tensor square with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and for $n=2$ let
$(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_2}$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$ be those of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Write
$\tau:=U_{(0\,1)}$ for the **exchange operator**, so that
$\tau\bigl(\kappa(u\otimes v)\bigr)=\kappa(v\otimes u)$ for $u,v\in H$; in the
sequel the inclusion is suppressed and $u\otimes v$ denotes
$\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Then:

(a) $\tau$ is self-adjoint and $\tau^2=I$; consequently $\tau$ is an isometry
with $\tau^{-1}=\tau=\tau^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(b) $P_+^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I+\tau)$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\tfrac12(I-\tau)$, and
$$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=x\},\qquad \operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}=\{x\in H\widehat\otimes H:\tau x=-x\};$$

(c) for all $u,v\in H$,
$$\|u\otimes v+v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}+|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr), \qquad \|u\otimes v-v\otimes u\|^{2}=2\bigl(\|u\|^{2}\|v\|^{2}-|\langle u,v\rangle|^{2}\bigr);$$
in particular, if $u,v$ are orthonormal, then
$s:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)$ and
$a:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)$ are orthonormal, $\tau s=s$ and
$\tau a=-a$, and both $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(2)}$ are nonzero;

(d) whenever $u,v\in H$ are orthonormal,
$\tau\kappa(u\otimes v)\ne\kappa(u\otimes v)$. Consequently, if $H$
contains an orthonormal pair (equivalently, $\dim H\ge2$), both exchange
eigenspaces contain nonzero vectors and $\tau\ne I$. If $H=\{0\}$ or
$\dim H=1$, then $\tau=I$, $P_+^{(2)}=I$ and $P_-^{(2)}=0$; for $H=\{0\}$
the tensor square and both ranges are zero.

**Slot convention.** For $\ell\ge1$, $S_\ell$ acts on $\{0,\dots,\ell-1\}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. On one-based tuple positions use $\widehat{\pi}(k):=1+\pi(k-1)$ for $1\le k\le\ell$. Conjugation by $k\mapsto k-1$ gives $\widehat{\pi\sigma}=\widehat{\pi}\circ\widehat{\sigma}$ and $\widehat{\pi^{-1}}=\widehat{\pi}^{-1}$; thus the supplier's tensor action becomes $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_\ell)=v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\widehat{\pi}^{-1}(\ell)}$. The parameters of $U_\pi$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)$ remain canonical zero-based permutations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Let
$n\ge1$, and let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold completed tensor power with
$H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and let
$P_\pm^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$, be the permutation
projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. For a
multi-index $i=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n$ write
$$e_i:=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\}\ (j=1,\dots,d).$$
For $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ with $|J|=n$, written $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_n\}$, put
$$e_J^\wedge:=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\widehat{\sigma}(n)}},$$
and for $\lambda\in W(n,d):=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ put
$\operatorname{orb}(\lambda):=\{c\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n:|c|=\lambda\}$ and
$m_\lambda:=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$. Then:

(a) *product basis*: $(e_i)_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$H^{\otimes n}$, and $\dim H^{\otimes n}=d^n$;

(b) *Slater basis*: for every $J$ with $|J|=n$ one has
$e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})$ and the
family $(e_J^\wedge)_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\},\ |J|=n}$ is an orthonormal family whose
closed linear span is $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$; it is therefore an
orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$,
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\binom dn$, and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$ when $n>d$. Moreover for every multi-index
$i$ one has $P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=0$ when two entries of $i$ coincide, and
$$P_-^{(n)}(e_i)=\operatorname{sgn}(\rho_i)\,\frac{e_J^\wedge}{\sqrt{n!}}$$
when the entries of $i$ are pairwise distinct with underlying set $J$ and
$\rho_i\in S_n$ is the unique permutation with $i_k=j_{\widehat{\rho_i}(k)}$;

(c) *symmetric basis*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the vector $m_\lambda$ is
nonzero, the family $(m_\lambda)_{\lambda\in W(n,d)}$ is orthogonal,
$U_\pi m_\lambda=m_\lambda$ for every $\pi\in S_n$, and for every multi-index
$i$ there is a real number $\gamma_i>0$ with
$P_+^{(n)}(e_i)=\gamma_i\,m_{|i|}$; consequently
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is the linear span of $(m_\lambda)$, the family
$(m_\lambda)$ is an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and
$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\binom{n+d-1}{n}$;

(d) *occupation operators*: for $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ the map
$$N_j:H^{\otimes n}\to H^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,e_i\rangle\,e_i,$$
is a self-adjoint bounded endomorphism, the $N_j$ commute pairwise,
$\sum_{j=1}^dN_j=nI$, and
$$N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)\,e_J^\wedge,\qquad N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_j\,m_\lambda .$$
Consequently both sectors are invariant under every $N_j$, the joint
eigenspaces of $(N_1,\dots,N_d)$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}$ are the
lines $\mathbb Ce_J^\wedge$ (one for each $n$-element subset $J$, with
eigenvalue vector $\mathbf 1_J$), and the joint eigenspaces inside
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ are the lines $\mathbb Cm_\lambda$ (one for each
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$, with eigenvalue vector $\lambda$).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with orthonormal basis
$(e_1,\dots,e_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H^{\otimes n}$ and
$P_\pm^{(n)}$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (with
$P_\pm^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$), and let $W(n,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$
and $m_\lambda$ be the symmetric vectors of that theorem. Then:

(a) *fermionic configurations*: the map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection
from the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,d\}$ onto the set
$\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$; consequently
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\#\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_j=n\},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{d}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=2^{d};$$

(b) *bosonic configurations*: the assignment $\lambda\mapsto m_\lambda$ induces
a bijection from $W(n,d)$ onto the set of lines spanned by the orthogonal basis
$(m_\lambda)$, so the number of bosonic configurations of total occupation
exactly $n$ is $\binom{n+d-1}{n}=\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}$, and for every $N\ge0$ the
number of bosonic configurations of total occupation at most $N$ is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{N}\dim\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\sum_{n=0}^{N}\binom{n+d-1}{d-1}=\binom{N+d}{d};$$

(c) *exclusion counts*: no fermionic configuration has an entry $\ge2$, so the
antisymmetric Slater index set contains no $\lambda$ with $\lambda_j\ge2$ for
some $j$; for $n>d$ there is no fermionic configuration at all and
$\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(n)}=\{0\}$, while for every $n$ and every $j$ the
bosonic configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ and all other entries $0$ occurs, so
no occupation bound holds in the symmetric sector;

(d) *consistency with the total occupation*: for every $\lambda\in W(n,d)$ one
has $\sum_j\lambda_j=n$, and for every fermionic configuration
$\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d\cap\{\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ likewise; in particular the
total occupation equals the particle number $n$ in both sectors.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,V$ be
nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]),
$\dim H=m$, $\dim V=k$. All tensor products below are the completed tensor
products of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with
elementary tensors $u\otimes v$, and all permutation projections
$P_\pm^{(2)}$ and exchange operators $\tau_W$ are those of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and
[[lem-nrqm-identical-particles-two-particle-exchange-operator]] for the
displayed Hilbert space $W$. Then:

(a) *identification*: the inclusion $\kappa:H\odot V\to H\widehat\otimes V$ of the algebraic tensor product is a surjective linear isometry, so elementary tensors and finite sums of them may be treated as elements of the completed product without ambiguity; the same holds for $(H\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(H\otimes V)$ and $(H\otimes H)\widehat\otimes(V\otimes V)$;

(b) *regrouping unitary*: there is a unique bounded linear operator $\Theta:(H\otimes V)\widehat\otimes(H\otimes V)\to(H\otimes H)\widehat\otimes(V\otimes V)$ with
$$\Theta\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')$$
for all $u,v\in H$, $\chi,\chi'\in V$; $\Theta$ is unitary and its inverse is the unique bounded operator with $\Theta^{-1}\bigl((u\otimes v)\otimes(\chi\otimes\chi')\bigr)=(u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')$;

(c) *exchange intertwining*: $\Theta\,\tau_{H\otimes V}=(\tau_H\otimes\tau_V)\,\Theta$, where $\tau_H\otimes\tau_V$ is the bounded tensor product of the two exchange operators;

(d) *symmetriser identities*: $\Theta P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\bigl(P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\Theta$ and $\Theta P_+^{(H\otimes V)}=\bigl(P_+^{(H)}\otimes P_+^{(V)}+P_-^{(H)}\otimes P_-^{(V)}\bigr)\Theta$; consequently $\Theta$ maps $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}$ onto the orthogonal direct sum $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H\otimes V)}$ onto $\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(V)}\bigr)+\bigl(\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H)}\otimes\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(V)}\bigr)$;

(e) *vector identities*: for all $u,v\in H$ and $\chi,\chi'\in V$,
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_-^{(H\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr)=P_+^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi'),$$
$$\Theta\Bigl(P_+^{(H\otimes V)}\bigl((u\otimes\chi)\otimes(v\otimes\chi')\bigr)\Bigr)=P_+^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_+^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi')+P_-^{(H)}(u\otimes v)\otimes P_-^{(V)}(\chi\otimes\chi');$$

(f) *dimensions*:
$$\dim\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(H\otimes V)}=\binom m2\binom{k+1}2+\binom{m+1}2\binom k2=\binom{mk}2,$$
with the two summands of (d) having dimensions $\binom m2\binom{k+1}2$ and $\binom{m+1}2\binom k2$.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] read on
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary with which the
framework reads the adopted P6 assumptions: they add no assumption to P1 and
P6, and the permutation invariance of sector preparations and of sector
readouts is a conditional consequence proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]]), not a content of
this definition. The definition asserts no spin-statistics theorem, no
dynamics, no measurement instrument and no empirical fact; whether a
laboratory ensemble is described by a declared sector preparation is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7, not a consequence of the declaration.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt a declared species sector in the vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
the observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is inherited
from the general spectral-PVM construction in P2 and clause (b) of the
observable definition used in clause (c) below; the finite joint-eigenspace
decomposition in clause (d) requires no additional choice.

**(b) The declared finite-mode model.** Fix $d\ge1$, a finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $K$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with a
declared orthonormal basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, the **declared modes** of the
model, and an integer $n\ge1$. The **declared finite-mode model** of the
species with these data is the declared species sector of clause (a) whose
one-particle space is $K$, together with its $n$-particle sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq K^{\otimes n}$
and the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
clauses (c)-(d). The declaration is an idealization: it asserts that the model
confines the one-particle content to the $d$ declared modes. No claim is made
that a species has finitely many modes; whether the declared modes describe a
laboratory mode family is a tested identification with uncertainty under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a consequence of this definition.

**(c) The occupation readouts.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ let
$$N_j:K^{\otimes n}\to K^{\otimes n},\qquad N_jx:=\sum_{i\in\{1,\dots,d\}^n}|i|_j\,\langle x,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n}\rangle\,f_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{i_n},\qquad |i|_j:=\#\{k:i_k=j\},$$
be the occupation operator of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (d) for the
basis $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$. By that clause $N_j$ is bounded and self-adjoint, the
$N_j$ commute pairwise, and $N_j$ preserves the sector $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$;
the **sector occupation readout** is the restriction
$$N_j^\sigma:=N_j|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},$$
a bounded self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with spectrum
contained in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$. The model reads $(N_j^\sigma,\text{particle
count})$ as an assigned sharp observable of the declared sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a):
its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\, E_{N_j^\sigma}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
the reading of P2 clause (ii) through the observable definition.

**(d) The joint occupation readout.** The operators $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$
are simultaneously diagonalised by the sector bases of the cited theorem: the
Slater basis in the fermionic case and the family $(m_\lambda)$ in the
bosonic case, with joint eigenvalues $\mathbf 1_J$ and $\lambda$ respectively.
Write $\Lambda_n:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\lambda_j\le n,\
\sum_j\lambda_j=n\}$ and, for $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$, let $P_\lambda$ be the
orthogonal projection of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ onto the joint eigenspace of
$(N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma)$ for the eigenvalue vector $\lambda$; the cited
theorem exhibits a line $\mathbb C m_\lambda$ for every bosonic
$\lambda\in\Lambda_n$. In the fermionic sector there is a line
$\mathbb C f_J^\wedge$ exactly when $\lambda=\mathbf 1_J$ for an
$n$-element subset $J$; if any entry of $\lambda$ is at least $2$, the joint
eigenspace is $\{0\}$ and $P_\lambda=0$. Thus the $P_\lambda$, including
these zero projections, are mutually orthogonal, their finite sum is the
identity of the sector, and $N_j^\sigma=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
\lambda_jP_\lambda$. The model reads the **joint occupation readout** through
the finite family $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$: the joint law in a
declared sector preparation $\rho$ is
$$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)\qquad (\lambda\in\Lambda_n),$$
and the marginal law of $N_j^\sigma$ is recovered by
$\mu^{N_j^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\sum_{\lambda:\lambda_j\in B}\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)$,
because the eigenvalue decomposition of $N_j^\sigma$ groups the $P_\lambda$
by the value $\lambda_j$.

**(e) Total occupation.** By clause (d) of the cited theorem,
$\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$; hence the
**total occupation** $\sum_jN_j^\sigma$ has the degenerate outcome law
$\delta_n$ in every declared sector preparation, and the joint law is
supported on $\Lambda_n$: the total number of particles read by the model is
$n$ with certainty.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of the model and
read the cited spectral mathematics through P2 under the choice hypotheses of
clause (a); they add no physical assumption beyond
the sector declaration and the finite-mode idealization of clause (b). The
occupation readouts are sector quantities in the sense of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]];
the exclusion and occupation-count consequences are proved on this page
([[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] and
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]]). No measured
count, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical claim is made.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral mathematics. Let a species sector with parameters
$(H,m,s,\sigma)$, integer $n\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and permutation
unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$ be declared, and let $\rho$ be a declared
sector preparation. In formulas involving labelled-space operators, $\rho$
denotes its canonical zero extension from clause (d) of the species-sector
definition; the same symbol denotes its restriction on the sector. Then:

(a) *invariance of the preparation*: $U_\pi\rho U_\pi^{*}=\rho$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$;

(b) *indistinguishability of relabelled readouts*: for every $\pi$ and every
assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ of the labelled model (a densely defined
self-adjoint operator on $H^{\otimes n}$ with a declared unit), the operator
$A_\pi:=U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}$ with domain $U_\pi D(A)$ is an assigned sharp
observable of the labelled model with the same unit, and for every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{A_\pi}_\rho(B)=\mu^{A}_\rho(B);$$
for bounded $A$ this reads
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,U_\pi AU_\pi^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$;

(c) *sector-preserving quantities*: if $A$ is an assigned sharp observable
that preserves the sector and satisfies $U_\pi AU_\pi^{*}=A$ on its domain for
every $\pi$, then $A$ induces the sector quantity of clause (e) of the sector
definition and its law on sector preparations is the same as that of
$A_\pi=A$.

The theorem is conditional on the adopted sector: it establishes that within
the model no assigned readout of the labelled space can distinguish the labels,
and it asserts nothing about which statistics a physical species realizes.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]], and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare a finite-mode
model as in
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] with $d$
declared modes $f_1,\dots,f_d$, $n\ge1$ particles and statistics choice
$\sigma$, with sector space $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$,
occupation readouts $N_1^\sigma,\dots,N_d^\sigma$, joint projections
$(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}$ and joint law
$\mu^{N}_\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_\lambda)$. Then for every
declared sector preparation $\rho$:

(a) *fermionic exclusion*: if $\sigma=-$, then
$$\mu^{N_j^-}_\rho\bigl([2,\infty)\bigr)=0\quad(j=1,\dots,d), \qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,N_j^-(N_j^--I)\bigr)=0,$$
and the joint law is supported on the occupation configurations with entries in
$\{0,1\}$:
$$\mu^{N}_\rho\bigl(\{\lambda\in\Lambda_n:\lambda_j\ge2\ \text{for some }j\}\bigr)=0;$$

(b) *no restriction in the symmetric sector*: if $\sigma=+$, then for every
$\lambda\in W(n,d)$ the projection $P_\lambda$ is nonzero, and for the pure
declared sector preparation of the ray of $m_\lambda$ the joint law gives
weight one to $\lambda$; in particular for $n\ge2$ and any $j$ the
configuration with $\lambda_j=n$ occurs;

(c) *total occupation*: in either sector $\sum_{j=1}^{d}N_j^\sigma
=n\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$, so the total occupation has the
degenerate law $\delta_n$ and every outcome of the joint readout satisfies
$\sum_j\lambda_j=n$.

The exclusion in (a) is a conditional consequence of the adopted antisymmetric
sector and of the declared finite-mode readout; the theorem asserts no measured
occupancy, no detector behaviour and no derivation of the statistics of any
species.

## Scope of the page

**Adopted assumptions.** The page adopts the sector and species assignments of
P6 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
which species is bosonic or fermionic, its mass, spin label and statistics,
and, for a charged species, its charge, are declared model parameters;
the symmetric or antisymmetric
sector of the $n$-particle space is part of that declaration. The finite-mode
occupation model of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] adds the
declared finite mode family as an idealization. These are assumptions of the
model, not consequences of the Hilbert-space formalism and not measurements.

**Conditional results.** The mathematical items of the page construct the two
permutation sectors and their occupation bases
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]]), count the
occupation configurations ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]])
and decompose a two-factor sector into opposite-symmetry summands
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-two-factor-symmetry-decomposition]]). The
physical results are conditional on the adopted sector:
[[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-permutation-invariance]] proves that sector
preparations and relabelled readouts are statistically indistinguishable, and
[[pthm-nrqm-identical-particles-orbital-occupation-exclusion]] proves the
exclusion of double occupations in the antisymmetric sector together with the
bosonic contrast. All of these are deductions from the stated postulates,
idealizations and mathematical hypotheses.

**What is not claimed.** The page does not derive the spin-statistics
connection: the relativistic theorem is outside this framework and the link
between the spin label and the sector is a declared model assignment
(clause (iv) of P6). It does not claim that the declared modes are an exact
description of any apparatus or species, does not treat infinite mode families
or the continuum of modes, and introduces no dynamics of the sector, no
interaction and no instrument; the interaction example of the companion page
is a conditional computation in a declared model. Nothing on the page
attributes particle-like trajectories, spatial avoidance or a force to the
exclusion statement.

**Empirical status.** The page records no measurement and no data. Whether some
laboratory ensemble realizes a declared sector preparation, a declared mode
family or a declared apparatus is a tested identification with uncertainty
under the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; comparisons of model
predictions with counts would test the combined model and apparatus
assumptions, and agreement would be evidence, not a deductive proof of the
model. The design's separate dedicated statistics treatment is a named
destination of the later many-body page and is not silently claimed here.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real
$\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda
r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and

$$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$

The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel
function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are
asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about
complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let $H_{0}$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=3$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem.
Let $D^{2}_{j}$ denote the second weak partial derivative in the $j$-th
coordinate, defined componentwise on the locally integrable classes of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]),
write $\Delta_{w}:=D^{2}_{1}+D^{2}_{2}+D^{2}_{3}$ for the weak Laplacian
(defined on the classes whose three second weak partial derivatives lie in
$L^{2}$), and let $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_{0}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\Delta_{w}f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_{0});$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_{2}(H_{0}f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^{2}$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, the
operator $H_{0}+M_{V}$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain
$D(H_{0})$, coincides with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf$
on the same domain; in particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ the eigenvalue equation
$(H_{0}+M_{V})\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared central-potential model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **central-potential model**. Its declared
state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of clause (a), with the
position and momentum families $Q_{j}$, $P_{k}$ of that clause
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). A **declared central
potential** of the model is a function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ of the
form $V(x):=v(|x|)$ for $x\ne0$, where $v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is real,
bounded and measurable and $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\|v\|_{\infty}=\sup_{r>0}|v(r)|$ is
finite; the assignment $V(0):=0$ is a declared convention that does not affect
the $L^{2}$ theory. The potential energy is read in joules. The model declares
the **Born position law** of the framework for a unit class $\psi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}),$$
the spin-zero reading of clause (b) of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]. The pair asserts no derivation
of a central force law from $H_{0}$ or from P5: the restriction to a declared
central potential is an assumption of the model, and an assignment of a
concrete material system to the model is an identification in the sense of
clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$. With $M_{V}$ the
bounded multiplication operator of clause (a) of the same theorem, the
**assigned energy operator** of the model with central potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. By clause (c) of the cited theorem
$H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{V})$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$\Delta_{w}=D_{1}^{2}+D_{2}^{2}+D_{3}^{2}$ the weak Laplacian of that lemma. If
$\psi\in D(H_{V})\setminus\{0\}$ and $E\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$H_{V}\psi=E\psi$, the time-independent equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ is an equality in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and hence in distributions; it is a partial
differential equation in the three spatial variables. If $V\in C^{2}(\Omega)$
on an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, then the class $\psi$ has a
representative in $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ for every
$0<\alpha<1/2$, and the equation holds pointwise there. To justify this,
write $f:=(2m/\hbar^{2})(E-V)\psi$, so $-\Delta\psi=f$ in distributions.
On every relatively compact open subset of $\Omega$, the weak product rule
(obtained by local smooth mollification of the $C^{2}$ factor and passage to
the $L^{2}$ limit) gives, for every multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$,
$$D^{\beta}f=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}\sum_{\eta\le\beta}\binom{\beta}{\eta}D^{\eta}(E-V)D^{\beta-\eta}\psi\in L^{2};$$
the factors $D^{\eta}(E-V)$ are bounded on compact subsets and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3})$, so $f\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.
Integration by parts against compactly supported smooth test functions makes
$\psi\in H^{1}(\Omega)$ a local weak solution in the sense of
[[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]] for
$L=-D_i(\delta_{ij}D_j)=-\Delta$, whose divergence coefficients are
$a^{ij}=\delta_{ij}$ and $b^{i}=c=0$. They satisfy the uniform ellipticity
condition of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$\theta=1$ and have the required local coefficient derivatives of every
order. The interior regularity theorem
[[thm-interior-h-k-plus-two-elliptic-regularity]] with $k=2$ therefore gives
$\psi\in H^{4}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. Every ball compactly contained in
$\Omega$ is a bounded smooth domain and hence a $W^{4,2}$ extension domain by
[[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]. The higher-order Sobolev
embedding [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] with $n=3$, $k=4$, $p=2$
then gives a representative with continuous derivatives through order two and
locally Hölder-continuous second derivatives of every exponent
$0<\alpha<1/2$; this is the meaning of
$C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ here. These representatives agree on
overlaps because they are continuous and represent the same almost-everywhere
class. Both sides of the equation are then continuous and agree almost
everywhere, so they agree pointwise. The model adopts
$(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its declared energy observable; its self-adjointness is
the cited theorem's, and no further spectral property is presupposed here.

**(d) The declared spherical reading.** Let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from
$H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,\bar m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$, written
$U\psi=(u_{l\bar m})_{l\ge0,-l\le\bar m\le l}$, and let $(Y_{l\bar m})$ be the complete
orthonormal family of that theorem; $l,\bar m$ are integers, while $m>0$
continues to denote the mass. For a fixed $(l,\bar m)$, let
$\iota_{l\bar m}:L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)\to K$ insert its argument
in that coordinate and zero in every other coordinate, and define the
isometric **spherical lift** $J_{l\bar m}:=U^{-1}\iota_{l\bar m}$, so that
$$J_{l\bar m}u(x)=\frac{u(r)}{r}Y_{l\bar m}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega,\ r>0).$$
The **spherical sector** $(l,\bar m)$ is the range of this lift. Its
**admissible reduced domain** is fixed by the assigned energy domain:
$$\mathcal D_{l\bar m}:=\{u\in L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C):J_{l\bar m}u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\}.$$
Thus every weak Cartesian derivative through order two of the lift must
belong to $L^{2}$ on all of $\mathbb R^{3}$, including neighbourhoods of the
origin. This condition and the global square integrability specify
admissibility at both endpoints; no independent half-line boundary parameter
is part of the model. In particular $C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)
\subseteq\mathcal D_{l\bar m}$ by clause (d) of the cited theorem. The
**effective potential** is
$$v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}(r):=v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\qquad(r>0),$$
whose second summand is called the **angular-momentum barrier**; both
summands, and $v^{\mathrm{eff}}_{l}$, are read in joules. For $E\in\mathbb R$,
the model's **declared radial equation** in the sector $(l,\bar m)$ is
$$u\in\mathcal D_{l\bar m},\qquad H_VJ_{l\bar m}u=EJ_{l\bar m}u\quad\text{in }L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
A **radial eigenpair** additionally requires $u\ne0$. The associated
one-dimensional differential expression is
$$u\longmapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}u''+\Bigl(v(r)+\frac{\hbar^{2}l(l+1)}{2mr^{2}}\Bigr)u,\qquad u:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C,$$
where $u''$ means the distributional second derivative on $(0,\infty)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). The expression
alone, without the specified lifted domain, does not define a radial
eigenvalue problem. On $C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, its equation
with right-hand side $Eu$ is equivalent almost everywhere to the declared
radial equation above by the spherical-reduction theorem of this page;
pointwise equivalence additionally requires continuity of $v$. No full-domain
differential reduction or endpoint classification is presupposed here.
The angular-momentum quantum numbers $l$ and $\bar m$
appearing in the reading are labels of the orthonormal family $(Y_{l\bar m})$; the
identification of $l$ with a total angular momentum of a material system is a
separate assignment of the framework's angular-momentum items and is not made
here.

**(e) Stationary and bound-state vocabulary.** A **stationary vector** of the
model with potential $V$ and **energy** $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
vector with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalised, $\|\psi\|=1$; its
eigenvalue is its **binding energy**, read in joules, relative to the
chosen **energy reference** $0$. Here $E<0$ is a vocabulary convention;
no assertion that $0$ is a spectral continuum threshold follows for an
arbitrary bounded central potential. A continuum threshold requires a
separate spectral determination for the particular operator. In particular,
adding a constant potential shifts the free operator and its spectrum by
that constant without changing its eigenvectors. The model reads the energy
outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$
as the point mass $\delta_{E}$, the reading of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
position density of that preparation as $|\psi|^{2}$ by
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b), with $s=0$
and the state, position and choice hypotheses of (a). These are
declarations of the model under P2; they construct no sample, detector or
measured value, and they assert no stability, decay or formation claim.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
state space, position and momentum assignments, an assigned energy operator
for a real bounded measurable central potential, a declared spherical reading
with its effective potential and radial equation, and a stationary-state and
bound-state vocabulary. They adopt P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematics, and the additional central-potential model assumption and
spherical reading of clauses (b) and (d); in particular the central form of the
potential, the model's use of the full three-dimensional space as its state
space and the identification of the spherical sectors with angular-momentum
labels are declarations of the pair. The model excludes from its scope, until
their own items introduce them: the Coulomb potential $\propto-1/r$ and other
unbounded or singular potentials; spin and magnetic couplings; relativistic
corrections; finite nuclear size; the radiation extension, spontaneous
emission and radiation reaction; external electromagnetic fields; and any
many-body or shielding modification of a central potential. No numerical value
of $m$, $\hbar$ or of any potential is fixed here, and no empirical result is
asserted.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared
central-potential model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=0$, a real bounded measurable central potential
$V(x)=v(|x|)$ and assigned energy operator $H_{V}$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],

$q_{-}=q_{+}=q$ has $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$), reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map
$\Phi$, its unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the total operator $H_{2}$ on
$H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$, the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}$
and the relative operator $C_{\mu}$, together with the one-centre results
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] applied with mass
parameter $\mu$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the identity $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$
holds on the tensor product, and $C_{\mu}$ is exactly the one-centre Coulomb
operator of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
parameter $\mu$; the model's relative problem is therefore the declared
one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$;

(b) the relative bound energies are
$$\mathcal E_{n}:=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu a_{\mu}^{2}n^{2}},\qquad a_{\mu}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{\mu\kappa}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
with model degeneracy $n^{2}$ within the relative problem and the same radial
and position readings as in
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] with $m$
replaced by $\mu$;

(c) the total operator $H_{2}$ has no eigenvalues at all:
$\sigma(H_{2})=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},+\infty)$, the whole negative
part $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},0)$ of the spectrum is continuous,
and each relative bound energy $\mathcal E_{n}$ is the lower endpoint of its
continuous centre-of-mass channel $[\mathcal E_{n},+\infty)$, hence a channel
threshold rather than an eigenvalue of $H_{2}$;

(d) let $P_{R,j}:=-i\hbar\partial_{R_j}$ on the factor domain
$$D(P_{R,j})=\{\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)\text{ as a weak derivative}\},$$
and define the lifted total-momentum component on the composite state space by
$$\widetilde P_{R,j}:=U_{\Phi}^{-1}(P_{R,j}\otimes I)U_{\Phi},\qquad D(\widetilde P_{R,j})=U_{\Phi}^{-1}\{F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R}\times\mathbb R^{3}_{r};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}F\in L^{2}\text{ as a weak derivative}\};$$
it is self-adjoint on this maximal weak-derivative domain, has momentum unit
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and has no nonzero eigenvectors in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$. A state of definite total momentum would
be a simultaneous eigenvector of the three lifted components, so the model
has no such normalisable state. Since $H_{2}$ has no
eigenvalues, for every $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$ and
nonzero relative bound vector $u$ with $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$, any
nonzero tensor product $\varphi\otimes u$ in the transformed $(R,r)$ tensor
space, equivalently $U_{\Phi}^{-1}(\varphi\otimes u)$ in the composite
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})$ state space, is not an eigenvector; the
stationary-state criterion therefore excludes its pure preparation as a
stationary state;

(e) *Reading.* The reduced mass obeys $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$ and
satisfies $\mu\le\min\{m_{1},m_{2}\}$ with $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$
at fixed $m_{1}$; the model reads the one-centre model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b) with mass
$m_{1}$ as the fixed-nucleus limiting description, and the relative energies
$\mathcal E_{n}$ are strictly weaker in magnitude than the fixed-nucleus
energies $-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
two-body model and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured mass, charge
or level, no transition, photon or radiation statement, no binding or
formation dynamics, and no identification of the model with a laboratory
atom beyond the tested identification of clause (e) of the model definition.

## Remarks

- **What the page establishes.** The pair declares a central-potential model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]) and a Coulomb and
  two-body hydrogen model
  ([[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]]), proves the
  spherical reduction of smooth compactly supported vectors, with the radial
  equation read almost everywhere and pure-preparation readings only for
  nonzero vectors after normalization
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-spherical-reduction-of-smooth-states]]), and derives
  the energy-observable and flow reading
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]), the bound
  energies $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ with $n^{2}$-fold
  model degeneracy and the completeness of the bound states in the negative
  spectral subspace with a nonzero continuum
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]]), the radial
  and ground-state position readings
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]]), and the
  two-body reduced-mass decomposition with the relative levels as thresholds
  and the absence of stationary total states
  ([[pthm-nrqm-central-two-body-reduced-threshold-and-total-momentum]]). Every
  item is conditional on the cited postulates, the declared model and the
  cited mathematics; none establishes that the model or its postulates
  describes nature.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no reported spectral
  line, no count, no calibration, no detector model, no sampling assumption
  and no statistical inference appears on the page, and no numerical value of
  $\hbar$, $m$, $\kappa$, $q$, $m_{1}$, $m_{2}$ or $\varepsilon_{0}$ is fixed
  by any item. The transition frequencies, line intensities and selection
  rules of a hydrogen-like system require the radiation extension and the
  light-matter coupling of later items, and the scattering, ionisation and
  continuum processes require the three-dimensional scattering pair; neither
  is built or assumed here. The dipole matrix elements and their angular
  selection rules are reserved to the light-matter pair, and the numerical
  comparison with measured spectra to a future experiment item with its own
  preparation, calibration, sampling and uncertainty record; no such item
  exists in this batch.

- **Excluded physics.** The gross-structure model excludes spin and magnetic
  couplings, relativistic fine structure and the splitting of the
  $n^{2}$-fold degeneracy, finite nuclear size and nuclear structure,
  recoil corrections beyond the two-body reduced-mass formulation, QED
  corrections including the Lamb shift, hyperfine structure, shielding and
  many-body modifications of the $1/r$ potential, external fields, and
  radiation reaction. The source treatments describe several of these
  corrections as small compared with the gross-structure energies; no such
  magnitude comparison is a premise of any item on this page, and none of the
  excluded effects is claimed to be negligible by this page.

- **Empirical status of the model's numbers.** Statements such as "the
  hydrogen ground-state binding energy is about $13.6$ electronvolts" are
  conditional evaluations of the model's formula with measured constants
  (such as the fine-structure constant, the electron-to-proton mass ratio or
  the Rydberg constant) as inputs; they carry the uncertainties, conditions
  and conventions of those inputs and are not measurements of hydrogen by
  this page. Agreement of a computed transition frequency with a measured
  line would test the combined model, apparatus and constant assumptions; it
  would not be a deductive proof of the model.

- **Physical-interface note.** The model declarations, the readings and the
  scope exclusions above are the public physical interface of the pair;
  changing them requires the ordinary direct and indirect consumer review
  under the workflow rules, and the empirical qualifications carried here
  must be preserved by every later item that consumes these results.

retained_claims_mapping.rule: Retain every old statement, model assumption, proof obligation and source qualifier. Actual authored carrier is current repaired supplier; historical design is retained scope, not current acceptance.

canonical_claims.statement:
Let $\ell>0$ and $E_\star>0$ be real reference scales, let $m>0$ and
$\hbar>0$ be real, and define
$$h:=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}}>0 .$$
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let
$W\in C^2(I;\mathbb R)$, let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and let $u:I\to\mathbb C$
be a function. Then:

(a) $u$ is of class $C^2$ on $I$ and satisfies
$$u''(\xi)=\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^2}\,u(\xi)\qquad(\xi\in I)$$
if and only if the function $\psi:\ell I\to\mathbb C$, $\psi(x):=u(x/\ell)$,
is of class $C^2$ on the open interval $\ell I=\{\ell\xi:\xi\in I\}$ and
satisfies
$$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\psi''(x)+E_\star W(x/\ell)\,\psi(x)=E_\star\lambda\,\psi(x) \qquad(x\in\ell I);$$

(b) if $a<b$ are points of $I$, then each of the following identities holds
under its indicated strict-sign hypothesis:

(i) if $W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ for every $\xi\in[a,b]$, then
$$\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m\bigl(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda\bigr)}\,dx ;$$

(ii) if $\lambda-W(\xi)>0$ for every $\xi\in[a,b]$, then
$$\frac1h\int_a^b\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m\bigl(E_\star\lambda-E_\star W(x/\ell)\bigr)}\,dx .$$

All square roots here are the nonnegative real square roots of strictly
positive numbers. Part (i) is the forbidden-region exponent identity; part
(ii) is the allowed-region phase identity.

The identities are statements about the displayed functions and integrals
only. The number $h$ is dimensionless because $\hbar$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$
and $\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}$ is in $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,s}$;
no physical interpretation, no approximation and no error estimate is
asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and $H_0=H_0^*$ a self-adjoint operator on its exact dense domain $D=D(H_0)$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Let $E\in\mathbb R$ be an isolated eigenvalue with $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$, and let its orthogonal spectral projection $P_0=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ have finite rank $r\ge1$. The PVM and gap calculus are those of [[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]]. Let $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $v=\|V\|\ge0$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]). Put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D$, and define
$$\Omega_v=\begin{cases}\{\lambda\in\mathbb C:|\lambda|<g/(2v)\},&v>0,\\\mathbb C,&v=0.\end{cases}$$
For $\lambda\in\Omega_v$ write $q_\lambda=2|\lambda|v/g<1$, $\Gamma=\{z:|z-E|=g/2\}$ oriented counterclockwise, and $\Delta=\{z:|z-E|<g/2\}$.

**(a) Resolvent and exact domain.** $H_\lambda$ is closed and densely defined on $D$. Every $z\in\Gamma$ is a resolvent point, with the convention $R_\lambda(z)=(z-H_\lambda)^{-1}:H\to D$ of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], and
$$R_\lambda(z)=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(\lambda VR_0(z))^k,\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{2/g}{1-q_\lambda},\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)-R_0(z)\|\le\frac2g\frac{q_\lambda}{1-q_\lambda}.$$
